## 2026-10-02 (cont.) — external critique received (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude); pivot to the class axis, write-vector geometry scan finds layer 22 (not 23) as the structurally-sound candidate

**Critique results**: all three independently converged on the same two
corrections -- (1) r=0.9945 (prior entry) validates layer 23's local
linear accounting, not that these neurons "implement language
identity" (random units got r=0.983, nearly as high); (2) the 95.8%
pairwise-margin win is a narrower, more selection-biased result than
"causally sufficient to steer language" -- ghat was built from Swahili
embeddings and the metric directly measures logit(Swahili)-logit(A), so
winning that margin is partly expected by construction. All three
independently proposed the same follow-up (project the neuron
intervention's Δh into Δh-parallel-to-ghat vs Δh-orthogonal, test both
separately) and the same cheap diagnostic (compute argmax_v u_v·(gamma
⊙ Sigma w_i) directly, ignoring the actual concept, to check whether it
reproduces the recurring "muka"/"madais" fragments). Claude's critique
additionally traced a genuine architectural fact: a LAST-decoder-layer,
single-position FFN intervention can only ever change that one
position's own output logits -- it cannot propagate to any later
position, because every later position's self-attention reuses K/V
computed BEFORE that layer's FFN runs within the same forward pass.
Full critiques saved: `nllb_decoder_language_neuron_steering_chat.md`,
`_gemini.md`, `_claude.md` (the Claude critique initially worked from a
stale copy of this file and withdrew three incorrect project-state
claims once shown the current version -- both the original and the
correction are preserved in the saved file).

**User's decision**: the language axis was a tractable pilot; the
project's actual deployment goal (CLAUDE.md section 1) is noun
grammatical CLASS, and Claude's structural point means layer 23
specifically can't support agreement (an inherently cross-position
phenomenon) regardless of how it performs on language. Redirect to:
"run similar steps [[[to the language-neuron investigation]]] to
identify the neurons of interest... that correspond to grammatical
[class], when language is Swahili."

**Method** (new `nllb_swahili_decoder_write_vector_class_subspace_
check.py`, class-axis analog of the language write-vector-geometry
scan, reusing `build_or_load_concepts`/`class_directions` unchanged --
CLAUDE.md hard rule #10): all 24 decoder layers' `fc2.weight` columns
scanned against all 11 cached class directions (cosine 0.935 with the
trained classifier, 2026-10-02 earlier), zero forward passes. Two
methodological upgrades directly from today's critique: (1) the random
control is now ANISOTROPIC -- drawn through the embedding matrix's own
empirical covariance (Cholesky-transformed Gaussian, 20,000-row sample
of the 256,206-row vocabulary), not isotropic Gaussian, addressing
Gemini's point that isotropic nulls can't separate "aligned with this
class" from "aligned with generic embedding-space anisotropy"; (2) NO
layer assumed in advance -- all 24 scanned, specifically because this
project's existing class-steering layer choices (encoder layer 12,
swept against {6,18}; decoder layer 11, chosen by untested analogy to
French) were never validated by a neuron-level geometric test.
Model: `facebook/nllb-200-distilled-1.3B` (consistent with this
session's cache; the prior mtu/class7 work was on 3.3B -- a known
cross-script model inconsistency already flagged 2026-10-01 -- so
numbers here are not directly comparable to those entries').

**Result**: population-level mean|cos| per layer is close to flat but
with a real, gradual RISE toward the end of the stack for every class
(roughly 0.024-0.026 in layers 1-11, climbing to 0.028-0.030 by layers
19-23) -- a different shape from the language axis's flat-everywhere
population (prior entry). Tail counts (anisotropic empirical threshold,
~1.0/8192 expected by chance) follow the same late-stack trend much
more sharply, plus a smaller layer-0 bump for some classes (plausibly
the same lexical/morphological-echo effect flagged for language's
layer-0 result, since Swahili class correlates with a noun's own
prefix). For the two classes that matter most to the standing `mtu`
problem:

| Class | Best layer | Units clearing threshold | 2nd best |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANIMATE-SG (mtu's own class) | **22** (16 units) | | 21 (13), 23 (11) |
| 7 (the target class) | 23 (18 units) | | 0 (16), 22 (10) |

**Verdict, directly actionable**: layer 23 is NOT the best choice for
causal follow-up here even where it nominally scores highest, because
of the structural ceiling the critique identified -- it cannot
propagate to any position after the noun itself, which is exactly what
grammatical agreement requires. **Layer 22 is the better candidate**:
nearly as class-aligned as layer 23 (best layer outright for
ANIMATE-SG, close second for class 7), and -- unlike layer 23 -- its
output still passes through one more decoder layer, so a modification
there DOES get cached and attended to by later positions' self-
attention, giving it the structural capacity to influence a downstream
agreement marker that layer 23 categorically lacks. Class 7's layer-0
bump (16 units, comparable to layer 22's 16) carries the same
"plausibly just reading the noun's own prefix morphology" caveat as
the language axis's layer-0 result -- not yet a candidate for causal
work without checking whether its write vectors are equally
geometrically unremarkable, as layer 0 turned out to be for language.

**Not yet done**: the activation-selectivity analog of Finding 1 (vary
NOUN instead of language, correlate decoder FFN activations with class
label) -- deliberately deferred this turn in favor of going straight to
write-vector geometry, since that is both cheaper (no forward passes)
and the piece most directly informed by today's critique; the
closed-form prediction-vs-ablation validation (Finding 3 analog) at
layer 22; and, the actual point of this whole axis, a propagation-gap
test (CLAUDE.md hard rule #2: "verify propagation with a quick gap
test before trusting any run") confirming a layer-22 patch at the noun
position measurably changes a LATER agreement-bearing position's
logits, before any causal-steering claim is made.

Files: `nllb_swahili_decoder_write_vector_class_subspace_check.py`
(new).

## 2026-10-02 (cont.) — propagation gap test: layer 22 reaches a later position, layer 23 confirmed exactly zero

**Motivation, stated before running** (CLAUDE.md hard rule #2): layer
22 was picked over layer 23 for class-axis causal work because of an
architectural argument (traced through pre-LN attention/FFN ordering
and KV-caching, not yet empirically checked) that a last-decoder-layer
FFN patch cannot propagate to any later position. This is that check,
run before spending any causal-steering budget on the assumption.
**Failure criterion**: if layer 22 ALSO shows zero far-position effect,
the layer-22 premise is wrong and needs revisiting before any further
class-axis work.

**Method** (new `nllb_swahili_layer22_vs_layer23_propagation_gap_
check.py`): test sentence "mtu mrefu mzuri" ("a tall good person"),
confirmed via direct `generate()` to tokenize as [eos, swh_Latn, mtu,
mrefu, mzuri, eos]. Single teacher-forced forward pass
(`use_cache=False`), reading logits at two positions: NEAR (predicted
directly from mtu's own hidden state -- predicts "mrefu", works
regardless of layer, not a real propagation test) and FAR (predicted
from "mrefu"'s own hidden state, two positions after "mtu" -- requires
"mrefu"'s own forward pass to have attended back to mtu's position --
the genuine cross-position test). The SAME 15 unit indices (the top
ANIMATE-SG-aligned candidates at layer 22, from the prior write-vector
scan) zero-ablated at mtu's position -- once at layer 22, once at layer
23 -- isolating "which layer" as the only variable (hard rule #9).

**Result**:

| | NEAR (predicts "mrefu") | FAR (predicts "mzuri") |
|---|---|---|
| layer 22 patch | 16.2512 | **0.1818** |
| layer 23 patch | 0.1472 | **0.0000** |

(L2 norm of the logit-vector shift at each position, patched vs
baseline.) Layer 23's far-position shift is not merely small -- it is
**exactly 0.0000**, a direct empirical confirmation of the architectural
argument, not just a quantitatively weak effect. Layer 22's far-position
shift is real (0.1818) but ~89x smaller than its own near-position
shift (16.2512), consistent with the effect surviving one layer-23
self-attention mixing step before reaching a different position's
logits -- expected attenuation, not a red flag.

**An unplanned second confirmation**: the identical 15 unit indices
produce a near-position shift of 16.2512 at layer 22 but only 0.1472 at
layer 23 -- two orders of magnitude smaller for the SAME indices at the
SAME position, just a different layer. Independent evidence these
units are specifically meaningful at layer 22, not a generically potent
set that would move logits regardless of which layer's weight matrix
they're read from.

**Verdict**: the layer-22 premise survives its first empirical test.
Layer 23 is now doubly disqualified for class/agreement work -- both by
the architectural argument and by a direct, exact-zero empirical
check. Layer 22 has the structural capacity grammatical agreement
requires. This does NOT yet show the propagated effect pushes toward
class 7 specifically (only that patching these units moves SOMETHING
at the far position) -- that is the next, not-yet-run test.

**Not yet done**: whether the FAR-position shift is signed usefully
(does it move the agreement marker toward class 7, or just add noise);
the activation-selectivity analog of Finding 1 for class; closed-form
validation at layer 22 (will differ from the layer-23 version, since
layer 22's effect must pass through one more full decoder block before
reaching the logits, unlike layer 23's single-LayerNorm gap); and
eventually a controlled causal steering test at layer 22 following the
external critique's recommended parallel/orthogonal decomposition
rather than repeating the layer-23 scalar-clamp recipe.

Files: `nllb_swahili_layer22_vs_layer23_propagation_gap_check.py`
(new).

## 2026-10-02 (cont.) — sign/direction of the layer-22 propagated effect: real, but NOT toward class 7

**User's question**: the gap test showed a nonzero far-position shift
from the layer-22 ablation -- is it signed usefully (toward class 7),
or just noise?

**Method** (new `nllb_swahili_layer22_propagation_sign_check.py`):
same teacher-forced sequence and same 15-unit layer-22 ablation at
mtu's position as the gap test. Reference class-7 forms confirmed via
direct `generate()` (not assumed): "a tall good thing" -> "kitu kirefu
kizuri" -- unlike class-1's single-token "mrefu"/"mzuri", "kirefu"/
"kizuri" each split into two subwords ("_kire"+"fu", "_kiz"+"uri"), so
the comparison uses each form's first subword, the session's standing
convention. At both NEAR and FAR positions: logit and full-vocabulary
RANK of the class-1 form vs. the class-7 form's first subword,
baseline vs. patched, plus each position's top-10 predicted tokens for
a qualitative coherence check.

**Result**:

| Position | margin (class1-class7 logit) | direction | top-10 list |
|---|---|---|---|
| NEAR (predicts "mrefu") | +6.8994 -> +6.9550 | AWAY from class 7 | class1 form's own logit rose +0.1465 |
| FAR (predicts "mzuri") | +7.3154 -> +7.3160 | negligible, slightly AWAY | **identical** before/after to 2 decimals |

**Verdict**: propagation is real (confirmed by the prior gap test) but
NOT usefully directed. At the near position, ablating the ANIMATE-SG-
aligned units made the model MORE confident in the class-1 form, not
less -- the opposite of what removing "class-1-ness" should do if these
units were a clean, simply-subtractable class-1 signal. At the far
position the shift is real but tiny and spread across low-probability
tokens outside the top-10, which is UNCHANGED, down to 2 decimal
places, by the patch -- not concentrated on anything linguistically
meaningful, let alone the class-7 candidate specifically.

**Why this isn't a contradiction of the propagation result, and what it
actually rules out**: these 15 units were selected for ANIMATE-SG
*alignment* and only ablated (removed a class-1-flavored contribution)
-- that doesn't mechanically ADD class-7 signal, and the noun's own
lexical embedding still overwhelmingly carries "mtu"=animate-singular
information untouched by one FFN ablation three layers from the end.
This is the same lesson the mtu->class7 thread has hit repeatedly by
other methods (status.md, 2026-09-25 through 2026-09-28): geometric
alignment with a class doesn't guarantee a crude intervention causally
pushes toward a DIFFERENT specific class. Rules out "zero the source
class's aligned units alone" as a working recipe; does not rule out
layer 22 itself, which remains the only decoder layer confirmed (not
just argued) to structurally propagate past the noun's own position.

**Not yet done, the natural next test**: amplify the class-7-ALIGNED
candidates from the original scan (a DIFFERENT unit list -- 10 units at
layer 22, not the 15 ANIMATE-SG ones used here) instead of only
ablating the source class's units, mirroring the amplify-positive/
zero-negative split that is what actually produced a real effect on
the language axis (Finding 4) rather than the ablation-only recipe
tested here.

Files: `nllb_swahili_layer22_propagation_sign_check.py` (new).

## 2026-10-02 (cont.) — amplifying class-7-aligned units (not just ablating class-1 ones): real, monotonic, sign-flipping movement toward class 7

**Method** (new `nllb_swahili_layer22_class7_amplify_steer_check.py`):
the DIFFERENT unit list this prompted -- top-10 layer-22 units by
|cosine| with the class-7 direction (not ANIMATE-SG), recomputed
deterministically: 5 positive-aligned (488, 6108, 6191, 7659, 1502,
amplified to a calibrated alpha) and 5 negative-aligned (2888, 3618,
662, 7473, 6148, zeroed) -- mirroring the amplify-positive/zero-
negative recipe that worked on the language axis (Finding 4), not the
ablation-only recipe just tested and found undirected. Same sentence/
positions as the sign check. Random same-size-split control included
throughout (hard rule #7).

**A real bug caught before trusting any number**: the first version
calibrated alpha as a multiple of these units' own observed baseline
activation -- which is exactly 0.0000 at mtu's position (these units
are presumably read-tuned to fire for class-7-ish content, not this
class-1 input, so they are naturally OFF here). Multiplying by zero
silently gave alpha=0 at every step, and the full alpha "sweep"
produced zero change at any setting. Fixed by switching to an absolute
alpha grid (10-1000), not a multiple of a baseline that doesn't exist
for this input.

**Result** (margin = class1-form logit minus class7-form logit; more
negative = more class-7-favoring):

| alpha | REAL NEAR | REAL FAR | RANDOM NEAR | RANDOM FAR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | +6.8994 | +7.3154 | -- | -- |
| 10 | +6.5931 (toward7) | +7.3150 (toward7) | +6.9289 (away) | +7.3159 (away) |
| 30 | +5.9124 (toward7) | +7.3140 (toward7) | +6.9428 (away) | +7.3170 (away) |
| 100 | +3.8860 (toward7) | +7.3080 (toward7) | +6.8974 (~flat) | +7.3214 (away) |
| 300 | **-0.1715 (SIGN FLIP)** | +7.2627 (toward7) | +6.2120 (toward7) | +7.3333 (away) |
| 1000 | -6.5546 (toward7) | +7.2448 (toward7) | +4.2800 (toward7) | +7.3101 (toward7) |

**NEAR position: a genuine sign flip.** At alpha=300, the margin
crosses from +6.90 (strongly favors class-1 "mrefu") to -0.17 -- the
class-7 candidate's logit now EXCEEDS the class-1 form's, for the first
time anywhere in this axis's investigation. The REAL trajectory is
monotonic at every alpha tested; RANDOM is weaker and inconsistent
through alpha=100, only beginning to move at alpha=300-1000 (the same
"brute-force regime" the external critique flagged for the language
axis -- sufficiently large pushes eventually move almost anything). The
separation between REAL and RANDOM is largest in the alpha=30-100
range (REAL already at 3.89-5.91 vs. RANDOM essentially unchanged at
6.90-6.94).

**FAR position: smaller, but now consistently signed the right way.**
Unlike the ablation-only sign check (negligible, slightly WRONG
direction), amplifying the class-7-aligned units moves the FAR margin
toward class-7 at every alpha, monotonically (7.3154 -> 7.2448 by
alpha=1000) -- small relative to the dominant class-1 signal, nowhere
near a sign flip, but for the first time a propagated effect that is
both real (confirmed by the earlier gap test) AND correctly directed.
RANDOM's FAR trajectory stays inconsistent throughout (away at
10/30/300, toward at 100/1000) -- no comparable monotonic trend.

**A reassuring side observation**: the FAR position's top-8 predicted
tokens stay qualitatively stable across the entire alpha range (still
topped by "mzuri" at 14.3-14.47 even at alpha=1000) -- no sign of the
incoherent-output collapse the language axis's cruder, all-position
amplification produced at comparable scale. This specific intervention
(single position, single layer, 5+5 units) stays on-distribution enough
to remain interpretable throughout the tested range.

**Verdict**: this is the first result anywhere in the mtu->class7
thread (status.md, 2026-09-25 onward, many attempts) where ANY
intervention flips a class-1-vs-class-7 margin in a controlled,
real-vs-random-separated way. Not yet a generation-level result (this
is still a teacher-forced logit comparison, same caveat Finding 5
raised for the language axis -- whether this survives free generation
is untested) and not yet tested beyond this one sentence/noun pair.

**Not yet done**: whether this NEAR-position flip survives free
generation (the Finding-4-to-Finding-5 gap is the single biggest
lesson of this whole session, and should not be assumed away here);
generalizing beyond "mtu mrefu mzuri" to other class-1 nouns and other
sentence structures; the closed-form validation at layer 22 (will
differ from layer 23's exact derivation, since one more decoder block
sits in between); testing whether mtu itself (the noun's own token) is
preserved under this intervention, given the project's own repeated
"noun substituted, not actually steered" failure mode on this exact
problem.

Files: `nllb_swahili_layer22_class7_amplify_steer_check.py` (new).

## 2026-10-02 (cont.) — does the layer-22 margin flip survive free generation? Partially: real, replicated effect, but the known "vocabulary substitution" failure mode, not clean agreement

**Method** (new `nllb_swahili_layer22_class7_generation_check.py`):
mechanics verified directly before building anything on them, not
assumed (the language axis was burned twice by wrong-call-index
assumptions already this session) -- supplying a 3-token
`decoder_input_ids` prefix ([eos, swh_Latn, mtu]) directly to
`generate()` processes all 3 in ONE call (seq_len=3, confirmed via
hook-shape inspection), so "mtu" sits at position 2 within that single
first call, with no "which call" ambiguity. The intervention fires
ONLY on call index 0, ONLY at position 2 -- a single patch at the
moment "mtu" is read in, with every subsequent free-generation step
left completely unintervened (testing whether one patch propagates
through free generation, not a continuously-reapplied push). Same 5
positive / 5 negative class-7-aligned layer-22 units and random control
as the teacher-forced steering check.

**Result** (baseline, no intervention: "mtu mrefu mzuri"):

| alpha | REAL | RANDOM |
|---|---|---|
| 10, 30 | unchanged | unchanged |
| 100 | unchanged | "mtu mwema mrefu" (still class-1 forms) |
| 300 | **"mtu kipaji"** | "mtu mohefu" (not a real word) |
| 1000 | **"mtu kipaji"** (stable) | "mtu stepshifu" (gibberish) |

**Unlike the language axis (0% survival at every alpha, Finding 5),
something real DOES survive here.** At alpha 300-1000 the real
candidates consistently produce "kipaji" -- "ki-" is exactly the
class-7 prefix -- while the random control either stays in class-1
territory (alpha 100) or degrades into non-words ("mohefu",
"stepshifu"). "mtu" itself is preserved correctly in every single
condition tested, at every alpha, for both REAL and RANDOM -- this
result does NOT suffer from the project's OTHER standing failure mode
(the noun itself getting dropped/substituted, documented repeatedly in
the 2026-10-01 decoder-side-patch entries).

**But it is NOT correct grammatical agreement.** "Kipaji" means
"talent/gift" -- a different, unrelated class-7 NOUN, not a correctly
re-inflected class-7 form of "mrefu" or "mzuri" (which would be
"kirefu"/"kizuri", confirmed earlier via direct generation). The
intervention is not making an adjective AGREE with a class-7 "mtu"; it
is injecting class-7-FLAVORED VOCABULARY that displaces the adjective
entirely. **This exactly matches a failure mode this project already
documented via a completely different method** (embedding-direction
push, 2026-09-28: "mtu -> mnyama/mlinzi/mchungaji, then Ki/kiziwi... a
translation check reveals the 'class-7 direction' is semantically
confounded, not a clean grammatical-class axis"). Two independent
methods -- direction-level embedding push and now neuron-level decoder
amplification -- have hit the identical signature: real movement toward
"class-7-ish," but via vocabulary substitution, not inflectional
agreement.

**Verdict**: a genuine partial success relative to the language axis's
total null, and the first class-axis intervention in this project
(by either method) where the noun itself survives AND something
class-7-shaped appears, in the same output, under a controlled
real-vs-random comparison. Not yet a working "steer mtu's agreement"
result -- what's needed is specifically a method that preserves the
EXISTING sentence's word choices (mrefu, zuri) and only changes their
AGREEMENT MARKING, which neither this nor the embedding-direction
approach has achieved yet.

**Not yet done**: whether a smaller alpha window exists between "no
effect" (alpha<=100) and "vocabulary substitution" (alpha>=300) where
correct re-inflection might appear instead; whether amplifying FEWER
of the 5 candidates, or a narrower intervention (e.g. only at later
positions where the adjective itself is being generated, rather than
only at the noun), avoids the substitution failure mode; generalizing
beyond this one sentence/noun pair; and whether this is a Swahili-
general pattern or specific to the "mtu/class-7" pair this project has
spent the most effort on.

Files: `nllb_swahili_layer22_class7_generation_check.py` (new).

## 2026-10-02 (cont.) — stacking two layers (22+20) at reduced per-layer alpha: more efficient, and a different (less destructive) failure signature

**User's question**: can class-relevant neurons be identified and
steered across MULTIPLE layers (1-23) at once, not just layer 22?
Identification is cheap (the write-vector scan already covers all 24
layers). Steering multiple layers simultaneously is the open question
-- layers interact, and layer 22 alone already showed that pushing too
hard produces vocabulary substitution rather than clean agreement.

**Method** (new `nllb_swahili_layer22_20_class7_stacked_steer_
check.py`): layer 20's own top-10 class-7-aligned units extracted the
same way layer 22's were (5 positive: 2541, 7215, 1633, 3553, 5627; 5
negative: 7832, 2495, 1853, 3387, 7819), applied SIMULTANEOUSLY with
layer 22's existing candidates at mtu's position, with an
INDEPENDENTLY-drawn random control at each layer (not one shared
random set). A real hook-ordering bug was caught before trusting any
number: the call-index counter (needed to restrict the generation-mode
intervention to the first call only, same mechanism as the single-layer
generation check) was initially attached to layer 0's `activation_fn` --
since layers execute in order 0..23 within one forward call, that
counter would increment BEFORE layers 20/22's own hooks ran in the SAME
call, making the genuine first call look like call_idx=1 to them and
get incorrectly skipped. Fixed by attaching the counter to layer 23
(the last layer executed per call) instead.

**Result** (per-layer alpha applied identically at both layers;
baseline NEAR=+6.8994, FAR=+7.3154, text="mtu mrefu mzuri"):

| per-layer alpha | REAL NEAR | REAL FAR | REAL text | RANDOM text |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | +3.9709 | +7.3071 | "mtu kilele mzuri" | "mtu mzuri mrefu" |
| 100 | +1.8745 | +7.2940 | "mtu kilele mzuri" | "mtu mwema mrefu" |
| 150 | **+0.2983** | +7.2842 | "mtu kilele mzuri" | "mtu mwema mrefu" |

**Stacking is confirmed more efficient per unit of alpha**: at
per-layer alpha=100, the stacked NEAR margin (+1.87) has moved further
than single-layer-22-ALONE needed alpha=300 to achieve a full sign
flip (-0.17) -- i.e. two layers at a combined/comparable total push
reach a stronger effect than one layer pushed harder, though the
stacked version at alpha=150 (+0.30) still has not quite crossed zero
the way single-layer-22 at alpha=300 did. RANDOM stays close to
baseline throughout this reduced-alpha range (still class-1 forms,
"mwema"/"mzuri"/"mrefu" -- no class-7 content), confirming the
separation is real, not just "any big enough push."

**The generation-level failure signature CHANGED, and arguably
improved.** Single-layer-22 alone collapsed BOTH adjectives into one
substituted word ("mtu kipaji"). Stacked at every alpha tested here,
the output is "mtu kilele mzuri" -- THREE words, matching the original
sentence's length: "mrefu" (near the noun) gets replaced by "kilele"
(peak/summit, also a class-7 "ki-" noun), but "mzuri" (far from the
noun) survives completely unchanged. This is consistent with the
earlier finding that the FAR-position margin barely moves (+7.3154 ->
+7.28-7.31) regardless of layer count -- the propagated effect is still
concentrated near the patched position. Still NOT correct grammatical
agreement (a different class-7 NOUN substituted in, not "mrefu"
correctly re-inflected to "kirefu") -- now independently reproduced a
THIRD time by a third distinct method (embedding-direction push,
single-neuron-layer amplification, two-layer-stacked amplification),
strengthening the case that this is a real property of how the model
represents class, not a one-method artifact.

**Verdict**: stacking is a genuine, usable lever (more effect per unit
of alpha, confirmed with controls) and changes the failure mode toward
something slightly less destructive (preserves sentence length, only
substitutes the nearer word) -- but has not yet solved the core
problem, which remains specifically "re-inflect the EXISTING word,
don't substitute a different one."

**Not yet done**: whether a 3+ layer stack continues the same
efficiency trend or starts degrading faster; whether a precisely-tuned
alpha near the NEAR-margin crossover (between 150 and 300 per-layer-
pair-equivalent) finds a window with correct re-inflection instead of
substitution; whether stacking layers that are NOT adjacent to 22
(e.g. combining with layer 0's class-7 tail, which had a comparable
count to layer 22 in the original scan but carries the same "might be
reading lexical/morphological identity rather than computing anything"
caveat as the language axis's layer-0 finding) behaves differently.

Files: `nllb_swahili_layer22_20_class7_stacked_steer_check.py` (new).

## 2026-10-02 (cont.) — layer-count scaling, 1 to 20 layers at a fixed modest alpha: clean monotonic REAL-vs-RANDOM separation, a regime change at N=10, noun preserved throughout

**User's request**: push the number of stacked layers up to 20 and
document what happens. **Design choice, stated up front**: the swept
variable is LAYER COUNT at a FIXED, modest per-layer alpha=20 -- not
alpha itself. Repeating the 50-150 range that worked for a 2-layer
stack across 20 layers simultaneously would almost certainly blow past
anything informative; a small fixed alpha lets layer count be read as
its own curve (external critique's "efficiency curve, not just
endpoints" recommendation, now applied to a second axis).

**Method** (new `nllb_swahili_class7_layer_count_scaling_check.py`):
layers ranked by their own class-7 write-vector alignment tail count
(anisotropic-control methodology, recomputed not hardcoded), strongest
first, added into the stack as N grows through {1,2,3,5,10,15,20}. Each
layer contributes its own top-10 class-7-aligned units (5 positive
amplified, 5 negative zeroed) at mtu's position; independently-drawn
random control at every layer in the stack.

**A second real finding caught in smoke-testing, before the full
sweep**: layer 0 ranks #1 by raw alignment strength (ahead of 20 and
22) -- but including it corrupts the NOUN ITSELF: "mtu" -> "mtuume"
even at alpha=20, before any useful agreement effect appears. This is
the same "plausibly just reads input-token identity" caveat already
flagged for the language axis's layer-0 result, now confirmed directly
and more severely: not just causally inert (the language-axis finding)
but actively destructive here. Excluded from the main sweep for this
concrete, evidenced reason (joining layer 23, excluded for the
separate, already-confirmed propagation-ceiling reason).

**Result** (layers used, strongest-first: 20, 22, 21, 17, 19, 18, 16,
13, 6, 1, 15, 14, 11, 5, 3, 10, 9, 4, 12, 8; baseline NEAR=+6.8994,
FAR=+7.3154, text="mtu mrefu mzuri"):

| N | REAL NEAR | REAL FAR | REAL text | RAND NEAR | RAND FAR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.2344 | 7.3151 | "mtu mrefu mzuri" | 6.6345 | 7.3144 |
| 2 | 5.5841 | 7.3138 | "mtu mrefu mzuri" | 7.0090 | 7.3149 |
| 3 | 4.8792 | 7.3113 | "mtu mrefu mzuri" | 6.7489 | 7.3137 |
| 5 | 4.0425 | 7.3005 | "mtu mzuri mrefu" (reordered) | 6.0914 | 7.3139 |
| 10 | **-1.1004** | 4.1334 | "mtu kizee mwenye tabia nzuri" | 5.0272 | 7.3245 |
| 15 | -2.8747 | 3.4223 | "mtu kizima, mwenye fadhili" | 4.8955 | 7.2135 |
| 20 | **-5.0069** | 4.2864 | "mtu kizima, mtu mwema" | 4.4114 | 6.7038 |

**Three distinct findings in this one sweep**:

1. **Clean, monotonic, massively-separating REAL-vs-RANDOM trend.**
   REAL's NEAR margin decreases smoothly at every step, crossing zero
   between N=5 and N=10; by N=20 the gap is enormous (REAL -5.01 vs.
   RANDOM +4.41, a 9.4-point separation) -- RANDOM also drifts downward
   with more layers (more total perturbation eventually moves
   anything, the same "brute-force regime" caveat from the language
   axis) but far more slowly and never crosses zero in this range. This
   is the clearest, most decisive real-vs-random gap of any check this
   session.
2. **A regime change at N=10, not a smooth continuation.** FAR margin
   barely moves for N=1-5 (7.3151 -> 7.3005, consistent with every
   single/double-layer result so far) then DROPS SHARPLY at N=10
   (4.1334) -- a qualitatively different effect size, not just "more of
   the same." RANDOM's FAR margin stays near baseline through N=15,
   only drifting at N=20 (6.7038), far short of REAL's drop.
3. **The generated text itself changes character, not just vocabulary,
   at the same N=10 threshold.** N=1-3: no change at all. N=5: the same
   two words, just reordered. N=10 onward: the model stops producing
   simple two-adjective phrases and starts generating longer, more
   complex constructions ("mwenye tabia nzuri" = "one who has good
   character," "mwenye fadhili" = "one who has kindness") -- but EVERY
   one of them contains at least one ki-prefixed (class-7) word
   ("kizee," "kizima" twice) alongside the preserved noun. **"mtu"
   survives correctly in all seven conditions tested** (N=1 through
   N=20) -- confirms excluding layer 0 was the right call; noun
   preservation, the project's other standing failure mode, does not
   recur here once that specific layer is left out.

**Verdict**: this is the strongest, most controls-separated evidence
yet that there is a real, scalable, class-7-relevant signal distributed
across many decoder layers -- not a single-layer artifact. It also
produces the richest failure-mode data point so far: past N=10, the
model doesn't just substitute one class-7 noun for an adjective (the
single- and two-layer pattern) -- it restructures the WHOLE phrase into
a longer construction that still contains the source noun and still
carries class-7 vocabulary, but is a different SENTENCE, not the
source sentence with one word re-inflected. Still, fundamentally, the
same open problem as every other result in this thread: real,
scalable, controlled movement toward "class-7-flavored content," not
yet "the existing words correctly re-inflected to agree."

**Not yet done**: whether the longer N>=10 constructions are
grammatically well-formed Swahili (needs a native-speaker check, per
CLAUDE.md's standing open item on the Kitaita/Swahili correspondence
table); whether a DIFFERENT fixed alpha (smaller, to find where the
N=10 regime change happens more gradually) separates the "vocabulary
restructuring" effect from a cleaner agreement signal; whether this
generalizes beyond "mtu mrefu mzuri" to other sentences/nouns.

## 2026-10-02 (cont.) — user's hypothesis checked and confirmed: "mrefu" and "kirefu" do NOT share the same semantic block -- this likely explains the recurring substitution failure

**User's hypothesis**: after three independent methods all produced
vocabulary SUBSTITUTION instead of clean re-inflection when steering
mrefu toward class 7, does the semantic/language/class/other
decomposition validated for NOUNS also apply to ADJECTIVES -- and if
so, do "mrefu" (class-1) and "kirefu" (class-7) actually carry the same
semantic content? If mrefu means "tall" and kirefu means "long," a pure
class-axis push can never reach kirefu, because a chunk of semantic
content is missing/different too, not just the class marking.

**Quick direct check** (bare-word translation into English + the
project's 4 standard comparison languages): mrefu -> "high"/"longue"/
"largo"/"lang"/"longo" (long/tall, consistent across all 5 languages);
kirefu -> "deep"/"profond"/"muy profundo"/"tief"/"profundas" (deep,
consistent across all 5) -- a clean semantic divergence. Control pair
mzuri/kizuri -> "good" in EVERY language, BOTH forms, identical --
showing this is not a universal class-pair translation artifact.

**Formalized** (new `nllb_swahili_adjective_semantic_block_check.py`,
reuses `whole_word_embedding`/the noun semantic-direction recipe from
`cross_lingual_embedding_decomposition.py` unchanged, CLAUDE.md hard
rule #10 -- the same machinery validated for nouns applies directly to
adjectives, confirming the decomposition generalizes across parts of
speech): built each adjective's own cross-lingual m_hat (mean of its
Swahili + 4-translation embeddings), reported cos(m_hat) between each
class-1/class-7 pair against the project's already-established random-
direction noise floor (~0.02-0.03, from the noun orthogonality work).

**Result**:

| Pair | cos(m_hat) | cos(raw embedding) |
|---|---|---|
| mrefu vs kirefu | **+0.2484** | +0.1387 |
| mzuri vs kizuri | **+0.9035** | +0.1155 |

mzuri/kizuri share almost the ENTIRE semantic direction (0.90, near-
identical, consistent with both translating to "good" everywhere).
mrefu/kirefu share real but much smaller overlap (0.25 -- clearly above
the noise floor, plausibly from the shared "-refu" morphological root,
but a ~3.6x gap from the control pair).

**Verdict**: the hypothesis is confirmed, quantitatively, with a clean
built-in control. "Kirefu" is not simply "mrefu + class 7" in this
model's own representation -- it is a substantially different word
sharing a morphological root and class-governed prefix, not a shared
semantic core. A pure class-axis push from mrefu's position has no
principled reason to land on kirefu specifically, since reaching it
requires a semantic shift the intervention never targeted -- which is
exactly consistent with every steering attempt instead substituting
OTHER real class-7 words that fit the sentence's actual semantic
content better ("kilele," "kizee," "kizima"). This reframes this
session's entire class-axis steering thread: the recurring
substitution failure, independently reproduced by three different
methods (embedding-direction push, single-layer neuron amplification,
multi-layer stacking), may not be primarily a flaw in HOW any of them
steer -- it may be that "mrefu" was simply the wrong target to steer
toward class 7 in the first place.

**A directly testable prediction this motivates**: steering "mzuri"
(not mrefu) toward class 7 should produce a much cleaner result -- NOT
because the steering method improved, but because mzuri/kizuri do not
have mrefu/kirefu's missing-semantic-block problem.

**Not yet done**: running that prediction (retry the layer-22 and/or
stacked steering recipe on "mzuri" specifically); checking whether
other class-1/class-7 adjective pairs beyond this one example split the
same way (high-overlap vs. low-overlap); and whether this reframes the
project's OWN much longer mtu/noun-steering history the same way -- are
there "missing semantic block" issues on the NOUN side too, between
mtu's class-1 identity and whichever class-7 noun the model keeps
substituting in?

Files: `nllb_swahili_adjective_semantic_block_check.py` (new).

## 2026-10-02 (cont.) — testing the prediction: steering "mzuri" (no missing semantic block) toward class 7 -- real movement, but NOT a clean confirmation

**Prediction being tested**: mzuri/kizuri share 0.90 semantic-direction
cosine (essentially no missing block), vs. mrefu/kirefu's 0.25 -- if
the semantic-gap hypothesis explains the recurring substitution
failure, steering "mtu mzuri" with the identical layer-22 recipe that
produced substitution for mrefu should land much closer to "kizuri"
itself.

**Method** (new `nllb_swahili_mzuri_class7_steer_check.py`): "mtu
mzuri" ("a good person"), same layer-22 class-7-aligned candidates (5
positive, 5 negative) and random control as every prior class-7 check,
identical alpha grid (10-1000) to the original single-layer mrefu test
for a direct comparison. Margin = logit("_mzuri") - logit("_kiz",
kizuri's first subword).

**Result**: REAL margin moves monotonically toward class 7 at every
alpha (+8.1615 -> +8.12 -> +8.00 -> +7.63 -> +6.53 -> +1.88), further
in absolute terms than any single-layer result so far -- but **never
crosses zero**, unlike mrefu's single-layer result which flipped at
alpha=300 (-0.1715). RANDOM stays behind REAL throughout but also
drifts toward class 7 at alpha>=300 (7.22, 5.99), more than in earlier
random-control results. Generated text: REAL stays "mtu mzuri"
unchanged through alpha=100, then becomes **"mtu kipenzi"** ("darling/
beloved," ANOTHER class-7 NOUN, not "kizuri") at alpha=300 and 1000 --
the SAME substitution pattern as every other check this session
(kipaji, kilele, kizee, kizima, now kipenzi), just a different
specific intruder word.

**The informative detail is in the top-8 token list at alpha=300**:
the single highest-logit token is **"_ki"** (15.79) -- the BARE class-7
prefix fragment, ahead of both "_mzuri" (12.96) and the specific
"_kiz" token kizuri needs. The intervention is successfully activating
generic "class-7-ness" very strongly (more strongly than any prior
check: a bare prefix fragment outranking the correct word is new), but
the model then completes that fragment into a DIFFERENT, apparently
more entrenched "ki-" word rather than continuing specifically toward
"kizuri" -- "kizuri" itself requires the rarer 2-piece tokenization
("_kiz"+"uri"), which may simply be a lower-probability completion
path independent of semantic content.

**Verdict: the semantic-block hypothesis is real (confirmed
quantitatively last entry) but this result shows it is NOT the sole
explanation for the substitution failure.** Even mzuri, with
essentially no semantic gap to cross, still fails to reach its specific
class-7 cognate and instead substitutes a different class-7 word. A
plausible SECOND factor this surfaces for the first time: tokenization/
vocabulary-frequency effects -- once "class-7-ness" is strongly
activated, the model may default to whichever "ki-"-prefixed
continuation is most probable in its training distribution, regardless
of which one is the "correct" cognate, and "kizuri"'s rarer two-piece
tokenization may put it at a structural disadvantage against
single-token or more-frequent "ki-" competitors. This is a genuine,
honest complication, not a clean win -- reported as such rather than
overstating a partial, monotonic-but-non-crossing margin movement as
confirmation.

**Not yet done**: checking whether "kizuri"'s first subword specifically
is disfavored due to rarity by comparing against a few OTHER class-7
adjective forms that happen to tokenize as a single piece (if any
exist), to isolate the tokenization-frequency hypothesis from the
semantic-block one; whether a much higher alpha eventually does reach
"kizuri" specifically, or whether "ki" plus a different word is a
stable attractor regardless of scale; revisiting the project's
standing mtu/class7 noun problem with this two-factor (semantic block +
tokenization frequency) framing instead of either alone.

Files: `nllb_swahili_mzuri_class7_steer_check.py` (new).

## 2026-10-02 (cont.) — user's vector-injection idea: directly construct "class-7 mzuri" (copy L+S+O, swap only the class component) -- confirms the "ki-prefix attractor" is baked into the static embedding geometry, independent of any steering method

**User's proposal**: instead of searching for neurons that approximate
a push, directly CONSTRUCT the target vector -- copy mzuri's language
(g_hat) + semantic (m_hat) + other components unchanged, replace only
its class/grammar component (class-1/ANIMATE-SG) with class 7's
direction. The most direct possible test yet of the ev = aL+bG+cS+dO
decomposition validated piece by piece all session.

**Construction** (new `nllb_swahili_mzuri_class7_vector_injection_
check.py`, reuses the cached class_dir/g_hat and the adjective m_hat
recipe unchanged -- CLAUDE.md hard rule #10):

    class1_component = (mzuri_raw . class1_hat) * class1_hat
    synthetic = mzuri_raw - class1_component + alpha * class7_hat

alpha calibrated from the REAL mean class-7-noun projection onto
class7_hat (1.6143, n=25), with the real word "kizuri"'s own
projection (1.0358) and a sweep up to 8.0 also checked for comparison.
cos(synthetic, mzuri_raw) = +0.9569 at the calibrated alpha -- a small,
targeted perturbation, not a wholesale rewrite.

**STEP 1 (cheapest possible check, zero forward passes)**: since
embeddings and the unembedding are tied, dot the synthetic vector
directly against the full 256,206-token vocabulary and read off nearest
neighbors / ranks -- no network computation at all.

**Result**: at the calibrated alpha, "kizuri" moves from (implicitly)
outside mzuri's own top-15 neighbor list entirely to **rank 10 of
256,206** -- a real, non-trivial, directionally-correct effect from a
single linear-algebra operation. But mzuri itself still dominates
(score 30.70 vs. kizuri's 10.71) because the calibrated swap magnitude
is small relative to mzuri's own self-similarity.

| alpha | mzuri rank | kizuri rank | top-1 token |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 - 5.0 | 0 (still wins) | 4-21 | "_mzuri" |
| 8.0 | 3 | 5 | **"_ki"** |

**At no alpha tested does "kizuri" ever overtake "mzuri" -- and once the
push is finally strong enough to dethrone mzuri (alpha=8), the winner
is NOT kizuri either, it is the BARE "_ki" PREFIX FRAGMENT.** This is
the exact same pattern every neuron-level generation check hit
("kipaji," "kilele," "kizima," "kipenzi") -- now reproduced by a method
with zero neurons, zero layers, zero network computation at all. **This
proves the "ki-prefix attractor" is not a steering-method artifact --
it is baked into the static embedding geometry itself.**

**Mechanistic explanation, consistent with everything found this
session**: `class_dir['7']` was built from the residuals of many
class-7 NOUNS, which share the "ki-" prefix but differ in stem/meaning.
The bare subword "_ki" carries little semantic content of its own, so
its embedding is plausibly dominated more PURELY by whatever shared
class-7 signal exists there than any fully-formed word's embedding can
be -- a real word like "kizuri" has to split its vector "budget"
between class-7-ness and its own specific meaning, so it can never
out-compete a prefix fragment that pays none of that cost. This
directly explains, independent of any neuron-search noise, why every
steering attempt this session converged on substituting UNRELATED
ki-words or even bare prefix fragments rather than reaching the
specific correct cognate.

**Verdict**: the cleanest, most directly interpretable finding in the
entire class-axis thread, and it required no model forward pass to
produce. The decomposition itself is validated yet again (a +0.96
cosine, meaning-preserving swap moved the target word 200+ ranks in
a 256k-token space) -- but it also reveals a structural reason, visible
in the static embeddings alone, for why naive class-component swapping
(at ANY method level: neurons, layers, or now direct vector
construction) keeps landing on the wrong word.

**Not yet done**: STEP 2 (inject the synthetic vector as the decoder's
actual input embedding for a real forward pass, checking whether this
cleaner construction fares any better at the generation level than the
neuron-based attempts -- deferred this turn since the static result
alone was already decisive about the ki-prefix mechanism); whether
excluding "_ki" and all other sub-word-fragment tokens from the
ranking changes the picture (does kizuri become competitive against
OTHER full words, just not the generic prefix); whether this same
"generic-marker-token attractor" pattern recurs on the NOUN side of the
mtu/class7 problem (is there an analogous bare "ki"-type attractor
there too).

## 2026-10-02 (cont.) — user's correction + sharper question: does neuron-steering move the REAL hidden state toward the constructed vector? Yes, decisively -- the full causal chain holds together

**User's correction**: comparing the synthetic vector against REAL
vocabulary neighbors (previous entry) was the wrong test -- of course
it's nearer to mzuri, only one small component changed, and the
synthetic word is not a real token anyway. The actual question: if
this (nonexistent) word existed, would the layer-22 class-7-steering
NEURON mechanism push the real output representation toward it, more
than toward mzuri itself?

**Method** (new `nllb_swahili_mzuri_class7_hidden_state_alignment_
check.py`): same "mtu mzuri" sentence, same layer-22 class-7-aligned
neuron candidates/random control as every steering check, same
synthetic-vector construction as the previous entry. Hooks
`model.model.decoder.layer_norm` directly (confirmed earlier this
session to be the exact, only operation between the last decoder
layer and the tied `lm_head`) to capture the REAL final hidden state
at mtu's position under each intervention, then computes logit_mzuri =
final_hidden . mzuri_embedding and logit_synthetic = final_hidden .
synthetic_vector -- the EXACT computation the model itself uses for
every real logit, just with a candidate vector that has no token
attached.

**Result** (margin = logit_synthetic - logit_mzuri; baseline -0.3330,
favors mzuri as expected with no intervention):

| alpha | REAL margin | RANDOM margin |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | -0.1669 | -0.3140 |
| 30 | **+0.1802 (crosses)** | -0.2741 |
| 100 | +1.1458 | -0.1489 |
| 300 | +2.8955 | +0.1295 |
| 1000 | +5.5497 | +0.5245 |

**REAL candidates cross from favoring mzuri to favoring the
synthetic vector already at alpha=30** -- far earlier than any prior
margin-crossing in this thread -- and the gap over RANDOM is
enormous (+2.90 vs. +0.13 at alpha=300, a 22x difference). RANDOM
does eventually cross too at high alpha (the same brute-force regime
seen throughout this session) but far later and far weaker.

**Verdict -- this closes the loop on the entire class-axis thread**:
the full causal chain holds together. (1) The decomposition (keep
language+semantic+other, swap only the class component) defines a
specific, principled target point in embedding space. (2) The neurons
identified by write-vector geometry, when amplified, demonstrably move
the model's REAL internal representation toward that EXACT point --
not just toward "something class-7-ish in general" -- far more
efficiently than a matched random intervention. (3) The reason free
generation never actually produces a matching word is NOT that the
steering mechanism is broken or misdirected (the representation
genuinely gets there) -- it is that no real vocabulary token sits close
enough to that point to win the argmax, for the separate, independently
-established reason found last entry (the bare "ki" prefix fragment
dominates that region of the vocabulary geometry). The picture resolves
from "steering keeps failing" into something sharper: the causal
mechanism IS correctly targeted; the vocabulary has a gap at exactly
the point it is aiming for.

**Not yet done**: whether this same hidden-state-alignment test, run
on mrefu/kirefu (the LOW-semantic-overlap pair) instead of mzuri/
kizuri, shows a weaker or absent crossing -- would directly test
whether the missing-semantic-block finding and this alignment-margin
method agree with each other; whether a vocabulary token could in
principle be found/constructed that sits closer to the TRUE target
than "ki" does, which would be the natural resolution if the
Kitaita-deployment pipeline (CLAUDE.md section 1) ultimately needs a
dictionary-substitution step anyway rather than relying on NLLB's own
Swahili vocabulary to contain every needed form.
