## 2026-10-09 (cont. 12): THE "-ki-" GAP IS A DATA PROBLEM, CONFIRMED BY
DIRECT CORPUS INSPECTION -- a fifth of the mined silver-label candidates
compare two IRRELEVANT nouns against a controller that sits outside the
mined window entirely; three new zero-NLLB-cost syntactic control rules
fix this, and ONE OF THEM (perception-verb object control) is the first
mechanism of ANY kind to resolve the previously-declared-unfixable
mbwa/kijana structural ceiling

Per the user's "let's keep trying different approaches" directive.
Noticed, before writing any code, that every one of this project's own
EXISTING trusted validation examples for "-ki-" subject resolution
(mvulana/kalamu; all 12 items in `validate_roundtrip_and_attention.py`)
follows ONE template: "[Subject] ali{ona|kuta} [Object] {sm}ki{root}
{fv}." -- a perception-verb complement ("saw/found X doing Y"), where
the OBJECT, not the subject, controls the participle (standard cross-
linguistic object control for perception-verb small clauses; English
"I saw John running" is the same construction). Checked the already-
mined `mine_ki_candidates.py` output DIRECTLY to see whether the
training/silver-label data for attempts 3-4 actually reflects this
construction.

**It does not, mostly.** Root-distribution check on the 185 raw mined
candidates: 40/185 (21.6%) have ki-verb root 'sem' (sema = "say"). Read
6 of these in full context: every one is an "akisema"/"wakisema"
reported-speech INTRODUCTION ("Mungu akavibarikia, akisema, Zaeni...").
The two "candidate nouns" mine_ki_candidates.py finds nearby in these
cases are from the QUOTED SPEECH CONTENT that follows ("maji"/"ndege"/
"nchi" in the example above) -- completely unrelated to who is
speaking. The TRUE controller (here, "Mungu") is the SAME SUBJECT as
the preceding clause and typically isn't even one of the two mined
candidates at all. This means roughly a fifth of attempts 3-4's silver-
labeled training/eval data was comparing two WRONG candidates for a
question whose real answer lay outside the mined window entirely --
likely a real, concrete contributor to those attempts' weak selectivity
(+0.054, +0.107), separate from and additional to the representational
hypothesis cont. 11 tested.

A second check, scanning for the nearest OTHER (non-'-ki-') verb
preceding each non-'sem' candidate: found 31/145 cases where that
governing verb's root ends in 'kuw' (forms of 'kuwa'/"be", e.g.
"ali(po)kuwa ... akifanya" = "was/when-was ... doing"). This is a
periphrastic continuous/progressive construction -- the '-ki-' verb
IS the real predicate and MUST share 'kuwa's own subject BY
CONSTRUCTION, not by any kind of inference -- another case where the
"compare 2 candidate nouns" framing doesn't even apply.

**Three new rules, checked in order, BEFORE the live self-loss
fallback -- all zero NLLB cost (pure syntax over positions/roots
already extracted by `decompose_verb`)**, added to `kitaita_e2e_
pipeline.py`'s per-clause `-ki-` handling (`SPEECH_ACT_ROOTS`,
`PERCEPTION_ROOTS` module constants + the rule block replacing the old
unconditional self-loss call):

  1. **Reported-speech same-subject**: if the '-ki-' verb's own root is
     a closed-set speech-act root (sem/amb/ulize/uliz/arifu/jibu) ->
     predicted subject = the nearest PRECEDING clause's own resolved
     subject.
  2. **Periphrastic 'kuwa' same-subject**: if the nearest preceding
     verb's root ends in 'kuw' -> predicted subject = that verb's own
     resolved subject.
  3. **Perception-verb object control**: if the nearest preceding verb
     is a closed-set perception/cognition root (on/kut/siki/kumbuk,
     covering OM-prefixed forms too, e.g. 'mwon'/'mkut') AND that
     clause has a resolved OBJECT -> predicted subject = that OBJECT.

Self-loss only runs when none of the three rules apply (e.g. a genuine
adjunct clause with no recognized governing-verb pattern).

**Rule 3 is the headline result.** Checked directly against every piece
of existing trusted evidence for this construction:
- Mvulana/kalamu (the original motivating case): rule 3 fires,
  correctly predicts 'kalamu' -- matches the live self-loss answer
  exactly.
- All 12 items in `validate_roundtrip_and_attention.py`'s already
  round-trip-corrected battery (11/12 confirmed + 1 ambiguous, 2026-
  10-09 cont. 9): every ITEM's `correct_sm` is, by construction, the
  OBJECT's own class marker -- rule 3's prediction matches every one of
  them, confirmed by inspecting the ITEMS table directly, not re-run
  (same evidence, newly recognized as a clean confirmation of this
  rule specifically).
- **Mbwa/kijana**: rule 3 fires and correctly predicts 'kijana' --
  checked directly (full decomposition printed): 'aliona' correctly
  identifies mbwa=subject/kijana=object via the ordinary probe (as
  always), then 'akitembea' OVERRIDES from the probe's own guess
  ('mbwa') to 'kijana' via rule 3. **This is the FIRST mechanism of any
  kind -- trained probe, distilled probe, or live self-loss -- to
  resolve this case**, which cont. 9 explicitly declared "a HARD
  STRUCTURAL CEILING... not a bug... no morphological signal left to
  exploit by ANY marker-swapping method." Rule 3 is not a marker-
  swapping method (it never compares mbwa's and kijana's markers at
  all, only their grammatical ROLE in the governing clause), so the
  ceiling simply does not apply to it. (The separately-documented
  'kijana' statistical-table misclassification bug, 7/8 instead of the
  correct animate 1/2, is untouched by this fix and still affects the
  DOWNSTREAM Kitaita surface form -- flagged, not silently fixed here.)

**Rules 1/2, empirical check** (`validate_ki_control_rules_roundtrip.
py`, new): reused this project's own TRUSTED round-trip-correction
methodology (14/14 track record) rather than hand-waving from textbook
grammar -- per standing methodology preference, used REAL, FULL verse
text from the actual mined candidates (not hand-authored sentences),
with only the '-ki-' verb's marker swapped to a wrong value (one of the
mining process's own actual distractor candidates). Time-limited to 9
of 15 planned rule-1 items before stopping (hard rule #5 still clears:
n=9 >= 8):

  Strict substring match: 6/9 corrected [95% CI 0.354, 0.879], 0/9
  unchanged-toward-distractor, 3/9 unclear (NLLB paraphrased too freely
  for exact-string matching -- the SAME known limitation this project
  already documented in cont. 9, not a new problem).
  By-eye re-read of the 3 unclear cases (same manual-check discipline
  cont. 9 used, which found a HIGHER true rate than the naive automated
  check): 1 more clearly supports the rule (GEN.1.22 -- NLLB's
  paraphrase substituted a different verb but kept the SAME "a-"
  subject marker), 1 stays genuinely ambiguous (JOS.4.21 -- the
  construction was elided in the paraphrase). Revised: 7/9 [95% CI
  0.453, 0.937].

**One of the 9 cases (2CH.32.4) concretely confirms a real, specific
limitation, reported honestly rather than hidden**: "...kijito
kilichopita kati ya nchi... wakisema..." -- here "kilichopita" ("that
passed") is a RELATIVE CLAUSE verb modifying "kijito"/"chemchemi"
(stream, an UNRELATED noun phrase), not the true matrix clause, but it
sits closer to the '-ki-' verb than the real antecedent ("watu
wengi...wakazizuia", they gathered/blocked). The "nearest preceding
verb" heuristic (both in this test script and in rule 1/2's production
implementation) picks up "kilichopita" here, which would predict the
WRONG marker ("ki-", matching the stream, not "wa-", matching the
people). Tellingly, when round-trip-tested, NLLB's own regeneration
picked neither my rule's wrong prediction NOR the artificial distractor
-- it produced "wakisema" (wa-), the TRUE non-confounded answer. This
is informative two ways at once: it independently reinforces that the
underlying GRAMMATICAL claim (same-subject chaining to the real matrix
clause) is sound even on a case designed to break the naive heuristic,
while also CONFIRMING (not just theorizing) that this project's current
"nearest preceding verb" implementation can be fooled by an intervening
relative clause on an unrelated noun phrase. Not fixed here -- would
need real clause-boundary/deprel detection beyond what `decompose_verb`
provides; flagged as a known, open limitation of rules 1/2's current
implementation.

**Rule 2 (periphrastic 'kuwa'), evidence tier stated honestly**: no
real "kuwa...-ki-" instance with 2 class-contrasting nearby candidate
nouns existed in the 185 mined candidates to test the SAME way as rule
1 (the pattern was found via governing-verb-root inspection, not via
the noun-contrast mining criterion) -- the planned 3 hand-built round-
trip items for rule 2 were NOT run (time-limited this session). Rule 2
is currently validated only at the "doesn't crash, fires as designed,
sensible output" level (one hand-built pipeline test, see below) --
weaker evidence tier than rule 1 or rule 3; stated plainly, not rounded
up.

**Zero regressions, verified**: `probe_pipeline_regression.py` extended
to 11 cases (updated the former `ki_structural_ceiling_mbwa_kijana`
case to assert the NEW correct behavior -- kijana must now win, not
just "doesn't crash" -- and added 2 new cases for rules 1/2). **11/11
passing** after wiring all three rules into production.

**What this does NOT change**: the core gold-treebank-trained nsubj/
obj/amod/case/poss/acl probes and the live self-loss mechanism are
UNTOUCHED -- these three rules are a NEW, EARLIER-checked layer in
front of them, not a replacement. Self-loss still fires (and is still
needed) for genuine adjunct '-ki-' clauses with no recognized governing-
verb pattern -- e.g. the original mvulana/kalamu-STYLE case would still
need it if there were no perception-verb governing it. The multi-layer
distillation attempt from cont. 11 remains unwired, unchanged, and now
additionally explained: a meaningful share of its own training data was
asking the wrong question entirely (sema-type mis-specified contrasts),
independent of whatever representational limits also apply.

**Open for next session**: (a) finish the remaining 9 of the originally
planned 15+3 round-trip validation items (time-limited, not abandoned);
(b) consider whether a cheap clause-boundary heuristic (e.g. excluding
a "nearest preceding verb" that is itself the dependent of a relative-
marker-bearing form) would fix the 2CH.32.4-style confound without a
full parser; (c) the separately-flagged 'kijana' class-misclassification
bug (7/8 instead of animate 1/2) remains open and now visibly affects
output via this session's own fix (correctly identifies kijana as
subject, but still produces its OLD, wrong class's Kitaita marker).

Files: `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (extended: `SPEECH_ACT_ROOTS`,

## 2026-10-09 (cont. 13): "how well does it generalize?" -- quantified
real-corpus coverage per rule (37.3% combined, but very unevenly spread:
2.2% for rule 3, the one with the strongest validation), then closed
rule 2's evidence gap directly: 32/33 real sentences ALREADY agree
with the rule in UNMODIFIED corpus text (no model needed), and the one
disagreement exposed a second, distinct, real bug

User asked directly how well cont. 12's three rules generalize.
Answered with a coverage measurement across all 185 mined candidates
(not estimated): rule1(reported-speech)=32/185 (17.3%), rule2
(periphrastic kuwa)=33/185 (17.8%), rule3(perception object-control)=
4/185 (2.2%), no-rule-applies=108/185 (58.4%, still falls to self-
loss). Net: 37.3% of real cases get a free-rule answer; the rest are
unchanged from cont. 11. Flagged plainly that rule 3 -- the one that
resolved the mbwa/kijana "unfixable" case -- is validated ONLY within
one template (ona/kuta + adjacent object) and is rare in this corpus's
register; rule 2 covers the MOST real text but had almost no real
generalization evidence (one hand-built sentence). User asked to close
that gap.

**Step 0, done BEFORE spending any NLLB compute (cheaper than a model
check and, being a direct corpus fact, arguably STRONGER evidence)**:
checked whether 'kuwa's own subject marker and the '-ki-' verb's own
marker ALREADY AGREE in the real, UNMODIFIED text, across all 33 real
rule2 instances.

  Agreement: 32/33 = 0.970 [95% CI 0.847, 0.995]

This is the single strongest piece of evidence for any of the three
rules so far -- not an NLLB preference, a plain corpus-attested fact
about how periphrastic "kuwa ... -ki-" is actually written.

**The ONE disagreement (JOB.4.16) is not a Rule 2 failure -- it
surfaced a second, distinct, real bug, found by inspecting the full
verse rather than assumed**: "Kulikuwa kimya, nami nilisikia sauti,
ikinena," ("There was silence, and I heard a voice, speaking"). The
TRUE governing verb for "ikinena" is "nilisikia" (I heard, a
PERCEPTION_ROOTS verb -- this should have been a Rule 3 case, not Rule
2 at all). Checked directly: `decompose_verb('nilisikia')` -> `None`.
`decompose_verb()` only recognizes NOUN-CLASS subject-marker prefixes
(SM_TABLE: a/wa/u/i/li/ya/ki/vi/zi/ku), never PERSON markers (ni-/tu-/
m-/2sg u-), so 1st/2nd-person-marked verbs are invisible to the shared
"nearest preceding verb" search used by all three rules -- the search
silently skipped past "nilisikia" and landed on "Kulikuwa" (an
unrelated, IMPERSONAL/EXISTENTIAL "there was" predicate several tokens
further back), a genuine MIS-ROUTING bug, not evidence against the
rule's own claim. This is a DIFFERENT failure mode than cont. 12's
confirmed relative-clause confound (2CH.32.4) -- two independent, now-
confirmed ways the shared governing-verb search can be fooled, both
still open.

**Step 1: NLLB round-trip correction on REAL corpus sentences** (not
hand-authored, same discipline as rule 1), `validate_ki_rule2_
roundtrip.py` (new). Time-limited to 9 of 20 planned items (hard rule
#5 still clears: n=9 >= 8):

  Strict substring match: 4/9 corrected [95% CI 0.189, 0.733], 0/9
  unchanged-toward-distractor, 5/9 unclear.
  By-eye re-read of the 5 unclear cases (same manual-check discipline
  as rule 1/cont. 9): 3 more clearly support the rule (NLLB's free
  paraphrase substituted a different TAM/construction but KEPT the
  rule-predicted marker, e.g. PSA.104.6's "maji yakasimama" keeps
  "ya-", not the distractor "i-"), 1 stays genuinely ambiguous (JDG.
  17.1 -- the whole construction was elided), 1 is interesting but
  inconclusive (JOB.29.6 -- NLLB substituted "miguu"/i- for "hatua"/zi-,
  a near-synonym with a DIFFERENT class, neither confirming nor
  refuting the specific prediction). Revised: 7/9 [95% CI 0.453, 0.937]
  -- same "0 clear misses, several hidden behind free paraphrasing"
  pattern as rule 1's check.

**Net read**: Rule 2 goes from "almost no generalization evidence"
(cont. 12) to arguably the BEST-evidenced of the three rules -- a
near-universal (32/33) real-corpus-internal fact, PLUS independent
NLLB round-trip confirmation with zero clear misses. The person-marker
blind spot in `decompose_verb()`'s governing-verb search is now a
second, confirmed, shared, open limitation across all three rules
(alongside cont. 12's relative-clause confound) -- not fixed this
session; both would need the same kind of upgrade (either a person-
marker table added to the governing-verb search, or real clause-
boundary detection) to close.

**Not done**: the remaining 11 of 20 planned rule2 round-trip items;
re-checking whether the relative-clause confound (cont. 12) and this
new person-marker blind spot co-occur anywhere, or how often either
one actually fires across the FULL 185-candidate set (only spot-
checked here, not exhaustively counted).

## 2026-10-09 (cont. 14): direct user bug report, found and fixed in the
SAME session -- cross-clause subject leakage within ONE sentence (no
period, so split_sentences() never applies); plus wiring Swahili
conditional '-ki-' into the Kitaita REWRITE step for the first time
(previously only IDENTIFICATION was fixed, leaving a literal "?" in
the output)

**Bug 1 (reported): "Mtoto alipika mayai, mbwa alipokuwa akilala."**
('mtoto' cooked eggs; 'mbwa' was sleeping) wrongly re-selected 'mtoto'
(clause 1's subject) as subject of 'alipokuwa'/'akilala' too, even
though 'mbwa' sits immediately before and is the obviously correct
local subject. Root cause: identify_relations()'s cross-candidate win-
condition has NO concept of clause locality -- the SAME failure family
as the original Kudai/Wanaharakati false positive, just triggered by
comma-juxtaposed clauses with no sentence-ending punctuation.

Fix: for the 2nd+ verb in a sentence, restrict subject candidacy to
nouns NOT already claimed by an earlier clause, positioned strictly
between the previous verb and this one; fall back to the single
carried-forward previous-clause subject only when that local window is
empty (preserves legitimate pro-drop, e.g. "Mwalimu alisoma kitabu
kisha akalala"). The FIRST verb's resolution is unchanged (this is
exactly the scope cont. 11's position-independence validation covers --
one real clause, no competing clause in the pool yet). Object
resolution unchanged (full pool) -- scoped to the reported bug only.
Verified: 'mbwa' now correctly wins for both 'alipokuwa' and 'akilala'.
Added as a 12th persisted regression case; **12/12 passing**.

**Bug 2 (found while testing bug 1's fix): Swahili conditional/
participial '-ki-' had NO branch in `kitaita_sentence_generator.
translate()`'s TAM dispatch at all** -- `TAM_SWAHILI_TO_LABEL` already
labels Swahili 'ki' as "conditional" but nothing downstream ever
checked that label, so it fell through to the generic "no mapping
rule" flag and emitted a literal "?" placeholder (e.g. "u?sela") even
once the probe pipeline correctly identified WHO the subject was (cont.
12-14's work) -- REWRITE and IDENTIFICATION are separate steps, and
only IDENTIFICATION had been fixed.

Found that `kitaita_tam_allomorphy.py` already has a native-speaker-
verified Kitaita "conditional" TAM category with two attested variants
(`ki`/`ka`) that was simply never wired into production. New
`CONDITIONAL_TAM_HYPOTHESIS = "ki"` (kitaita_verified_corrections.py):
chosen to parallel the standing, unresolved hypothesis (2026-10-07 cont.
5) that Kitaita's ki/ka split mirrors Swahili's own ka(narrative)/
ki(conditional) split, rather than reusing 'ka' (already mapped from
Swahili's SEPARATE narrative -ka- elsewhere in this generator).
EXPLICITLY flagged as a hypothesis, not native-speaker-confirmed for
this mapping -- every other TAM branch in translate() is either corpus-
confirmed or speaker-verified; this one is not, stated plainly in the
trace every time it fires.

**Webapp**: restarted with both fixes live (`kitaita_local_webapp.py`,
http://localhost:8765/).

Files: `nllb_probe_identification.py` (extended: identify_relations()
per-verb candidate restriction), `kitaita_verified_corrections.py`
(new: CONDITIONAL_TAM_HYPOTHESIS), `kitaita_sentence_generator.py`
(extended: conditional TAM branch), `probe_pipeline_regression.py`
(12/12 passing).

## 2026-10-09 (cont. 15): user pushback -- "too many edge cases... let's
go back to the drawing board... what is the exact limit of the Hewitt
probe?" -- then two targeted checks before committing to any rewrite:
does self-loss generalize to ORDINARY (non-'-ki-') subject
identification, and does the Swahili-trained probe transfer to English?

**The Hewitt-probe limit, explained and then tested, not just argued**:
relation_probe.py reads a LINEAR function off ONE static, pooled
encoding of the sentence as written -- an OBSERVATIONAL question. Self-
loss asks a COUNTERFACTUAL one (build hypothetical variants, compare
regeneration likelihoods across full encoder+decoder runs) -- the probe
structurally cannot ask that question, no matter how trained, since it
never sees the alternative variants at all. Attempt 4's multi-layer
probe (cont. 11, selectivity +0.107) shows SOME of that information is
linearly present at some depth, but there's no principled reason to
expect a static readout to ever match a method that gets to inspect the
model's behavior under intervention.

**Check 1: does self-loss generalize to ordinary SVO subject ID?** New
`validate_self_loss_ordinary_svo.py` -- same exact (verb, nsubj, obj)
gold triples and adversarial/easy stratification as the trained probe's
own published Part B result (n=63, combined 0.937). Caught and fixed a
real bug in the script itself before trusting any output: gold `feats`
use `"Bantu5"`/`"Bantu10"` format, not bare digits as first assumed --
silently resolved ZERO of 78 triples until checked directly against
the raw feats.

  Self-loss COMBINED: n=33, acc=0.879 [95% CI 0.727, 0.952]
  (trained probe, same triples' superset: n=63, acc=0.937 [0.848,0.975])

CIs overlap -- not a disaster -- but two findings argue against "one
mechanism settles everything": (a) self-loss got the SINGLE case this
whole relation-probe track was built around wrong -- "Madaktari ...
waliitisha mkutano" (loss_obj=1.007 barely beats loss_subj=1.042); the
trained probe was specifically validated to get this right. (b) 14 of
47 valid triples (30%) had subject and object sharing ONE class --
completely undecidable for self-loss by construction, the SAME
structural ceiling documented for '-ki-' verbs, now confirmed to bite
ORDINARY sentences at real scale, not a rare edge case. Self-loss also
needs `decompose_verb()` to succeed (15/78 failures) and real class
features, the same applicability bound as the rule-based approach.
**Net: self-loss is a reasonable fallback, not a universal replacement
-- it has different blind spots of comparable size, not fewer.**

**Check 2: cross-lingual data availability + a live transfer test.**
Checked which of this project's already-downloaded-but-unused treebanks
(English EWT, German GSD, Spanish AnCora, French GSD, Finnish TDT) have
gold ENHANCED dependencies marking control-structure subjects
(`nsubj:xsubj`) -- exactly the relation Swahili's own treebank has 5/226
of. Only English: **3,020 real xsubj edges** (train+dev combined); zero
in the other four. `conllu_utils.py`'s `Token` class does not parse the
enhanced DEPS column at all currently -- would need a small, additive
extension to use this.

Before building that (a real, unstarted piece of work), ran a MUCH
cheaper, already-answerable question first, per direct user request:
**does the EXISTING, SAVED Swahili-trained nsubj/obj probe (never
retrained) transfer zero-shot to ENGLISH**, via NLLB's shared encoder
space? New `validate_swahili_probe_on_english.py`, reusing extract_svo_
triples on English UD EWT gold trees, lang_code="eng_Latn" embeddings,
same adversarial/easy stratification. First pass (n=12, too thin to
trust -- adversarial stratum had n=1, below hard rule #5's floor) was
scaled up to the full available EWT dev+train (3000 sentences sampled,
252 valid triples):

  SUBJ: non-adv n=180 acc=0.900 [0.847,0.936]; ADVERSARIAL n=72
        acc=0.917 [0.830,0.961]; COMBINED n=252 acc=0.905 [0.862,0.935]
  OBJ:  non-adv n=126 acc=0.841 [0.768,0.895]; ADVERSARIAL n=126
        acc=0.913 [0.850,0.951]; COMBINED n=252 acc=0.877 [0.831,0.912]
  (Swahili-ON-Swahili, same methodology: SUBJ 0.937 [0.848,0.975],
   OBJ 0.889 [0.788,0.945]; chance baseline for 21-way argmax ~0.048)

**This is a real, striking result, not just "roughly as accurate":
the adversarial stratum scores HIGHER than the easy stratum for BOTH
subj and obj**, reproducing the EXACT structural signature (cont. 11)
that validated the original probe as capturing real syntactic
structure rather than a recency/position artifact -- now independently
confirmed on a language the probe never saw one token of in training.
Bonus: Swahili's own OBJ-adversarial stratum was always too thin to
validate (n=2, cont. 11) -- English's greater density answers that
SAME open question (n=126, clearly survives) via the cross-lingual
route, a direct, concrete demonstration of the user's "use a denser
language to resolve data scarcity" idea, already working for the
EXISTING probe, before any new English-specific training exists at all.

Caveat, stated plainly: EWT (news/blogs) and SWH_UDT (GlobalVoices
news) are a similar register -- some of this may be genre-assisted, not
purely language-general; and this is raw zero-shot accuracy, not a full
Hewitt & Liang selectivity number (would need a freshly-trained English
control probe, not done here, though the chance baseline (~0.048) vs.
observed (~0.88-0.91) margin is large enough that this gap is minor.

**Net read**: this substantially de-risks the proposed next step
(train a probe on English's 3,020 real xsubj control edges, test
zero-shot transfer to Swahili's '-ki-' construction) -- bidirectional
transfer of this exact relation-probe architecture via NLLB's shared
space is now empirically checked, not just cited from Chi/Hewitt/
Manning 2020 by analogy.

Files: `validate_self_loss_ordinary_svo.py` (new),
`validate_swahili_probe_on_english.py` (new). No production code
changed -- diagnostic/validation only.

## 2026-10-09 (cont. 16): external critique round -- 3 LLMs (Claude,
Gemini, ChatGPT) given a self-contained writeup of everything above
(`ki_subject_identification_critique_prompt.md`); all three
independently converged on the same reframe

Core convergent diagnosis: we were treating control resolution as a
2-place relation (embedded verb, candidate) when it is actually 3-place
(matrix predicate, candidate's grammatical role w.r.t. the matrix verb,
candidate) -- rule 3 worked precisely because it is the only mechanism
that conditions on the matrix verb at all; every learned method
(trained probe, distilled probe, cross-lingual probe) only ever saw
(embedded verb, candidate), structurally blind to the one thing that
decides the answer.

**The single most actionable point (Claude's response)**: 221 of 226
`-ki-` verbs DO have a real gold head attachment (comp/mod/conj/
parataxis/advcl) -- we had been reading "no nsubj edge" as "no
supervision exists" when attachment supervision exists at 97.8%. This
opens a compositional, mostly-already-trusted pipeline: (1) train the
EXISTING structural/relation probe to find the `-ki-` verb's governing
head (an ordinary attachment problem, replacing the "nearest preceding
verb" string-position heuristic -- fixes BOTH confirmed blind spots at
once, since attachment needs neither linear proximity nor subject-
marker recognition); (2) route object- vs. subject-control via the
edge label + a small closed list of matrix-verb lexical classes
(tabulate against the 221 real edges before assuming the split); (3)
inherit the argument from the already-validated baseline probe (0.937/
0.889). This is the "one mechanism" originally wanted, compositional
rather than monolithic.

Other convergent points: (a) Claude's bucket A/B/C framing -- quantify
how much the shared-marker "structural ceiling" actually matters for
Kitaita OUTPUT, not just Swahili-internal undecidability (tested
immediately after, see below); (b) a cheap, direct falsification test
of the finite/non-finite transfer-failure hypothesis: run the English
xsubj probe on Swahili's genuinely non-finite `ku-` infinitive
complements -- not yet run; (c) ChatGPT's pushback that n=14 (the
zero-shot Swahili transfer test) cannot distinguish "somewhat works"
from "chance," and that EWT's `xsubj` distribution is dominated by
subject control while our entire test battery is object-control,
meaning a probe that learned "default to matrix subject" would score
AT OR BELOW chance on our battery by construction, independent of any
finite/non-finite story -- an alternative explanation not yet ruled
out.

Files: `ki_subject_identification_critique_prompt.md`,
`ki_subject_identification_critique_claude.md`,
`ki_subject_identification_critique_gemini.md`,
`ki_subject_identification_critique_chat.md` (all new, project root).

## 2026-10-09 (cont. 17): bucket A/B/C quantified -- the "structural
ceiling" (same Swahili marker, undecidable by any marker-based method)
is real and confirmed on the headline case, but is a MINORITY of
already-rare same-marker pairs once checked against actual Kitaita
output, not a pervasive problem

Direct test of Claude's critique proposal: for same-Swahili-marker
noun pairs (undecidable by self-loss/the trained probe by
construction), does the ambiguity actually change the KITAITA output?
Looked up both nouns' Kitaita translations + Kitaita noun class via
this project's existing dictionary (`kitaita_sentence_generator.
build_lookup_tables`, 2936-entry Swahili->Kitaita noun dictionary with
each entry's own `propagated_class` field -- no NLLB needed, pure
lookup). Bucket B = same Kitaita class (doesn't matter which noun
wins); Bucket C = different Kitaita class (genuinely, provably stuck).

**Headline case, confirmed directly, not assumed**: mbwa->'koshi',
kijana->'mdawana' -- DIFFERENT Kitaita classes. The famous "unfixable"
case really was a genuine bucket-C case, not a false alarm -- solving
it (rule 3) was solving something that actually mattered for output.

**Mined real `-ki-` corpus (185 candidates, within-instance same-
marker noun PAIRS, n=47 with usable Kitaita dictionary data on both
sides -- the best-powered, most directly relevant number)**:

  B (same Kitaita class, doesn't matter): 41/47 (87.2%)
  C (different Kitaita class, genuinely stuck): 6/47 (12.8%)

**The structural ceiling is real and confirmed, but a minority of an
already-small subset of cases** -- most same-Swahili-marker ambiguity
turns out to be moot once you check whether it actually changes the
Kitaita output. This substantially de-risks continuing to rely on
marker-based methods (self-loss, the trained probe) as the PRIMARY
mechanism, with syntactic rules like rule 3 reserved for the smaller,
genuinely-stuck bucket-C remainder, rather than needing a universally
marker-independent mechanism everywhere.

**Caveat, stated plainly**: the SAME check on ordinary-SVO gold
triples (not the `-ki-` construction) was far less powered -- only 2
of 15 same-marker pairs had BOTH nouns in the Kitaita dictionary at
all (13/15 missing a dictionary entry entirely), a real lexicon-
coverage gap, not a null result; not treated as a finding at n=2 per
hard rule #5.

Files: `bucket_abc_analysis.py` (new). No production code changed --
diagnostic/validation only. **Next step** (per the critique's
suggested ordering): tabulate the 221 real gold `-ki-` verb head-
attachment edge labels against their matrix-verb lemma, to check
whether the object-control/subject-control split is as clean as
hypothesized before building the governor-attachment probe.

## 2026-10-10: external-paper mapping (Tenney/DepProbe, Liu et al.,
Papadimitriou et al., Clark et al., etc. -- see
`ki_subject_identification_critique_*.md`-adjacent request) against
this project's own history, then a direct test of the one genuinely
untested idea it surfaced: Liu et al.'s "probe arc-existence and arc-
label separately" applied to the ORIGINAL Kudai/Wanaharakati false
positive (2026-10-06), not the mbwa/kijana case attempts 1-2 (cont. 9)
already tested it against.

Mapping, for the record: Tenney-style labeled-relation probing is
already the production architecture (nsubj/obj/amod/case/poss/acl
probes); Clark et al.'s training-free attention-head method was tried
on NLLB and confirmed to be a generic previous-token-head artifact for
subject tracking (CLAUDE.md section 8), independently corroborating
Htut et al.'s skepticism of Clark et al.; Papadimitriou et al.'s A/S/O
framing is informally supported by the already-done zero-shot Swahili
probe -> English EWT transfer result (cont. 15) but never run in their
exact frame; Limisiewicz & Mareček / White et al.'s orthogonal/
nonlinear probe architectures are untried candidates for the stalled
multi-layer distillation attempt; Ravfogel/Finlayson/Mueller's causal
methods are loosely echoed by this project's own batched self-loss
check and earlier steering gap-tests, not run in their formal version.
Liu et al.'s arc-existence probe is the one with a live, already-
trained, already-saved artifact (`edge_presence_probe.pt`, attempt 2,
cont. 9) that had only ever been re-tested against the WRONG motivating
case -- user picked this one to actually run.

**Direct test (`test_edge_presence_on_kudai_case.py`, new, no
retraining -- loads the saved probe)**: for "Wanaharakati pia
wanaziomba nchi nyingine kushinikiza viongozi wa serikali ya Honduras,
ambao hivi karibuni walizindua Tume ya Honduras ya Kudai Amani.":

- **Absolute threshold does not fix it**: edge-presence(Kudai,
  Wanaharakati) = 0.843, still positive -- the probe still predicts an
  edge exists in absolute terms, same failure mode as attempts 1/2 on
  the other case.
- **A win-condition gate (same style as `_wins_as_label`: must beat
  EVERY other noun candidate's edge-presence score for the same verb)
  DOES correctly veto Wanaharakati for Kudai** -- `Tume` wins instead
  (4.289 vs Wanaharakati's 0.843). Tume is not Kudai's real gold
  dependent either (that's `Amani`, its object, scoring 0.972, itself
  beaten by `viongozi` at 1.138) -- the probe's ranking is not
  correctly finding Kudai's TRUE edge, but it doesn't need to for this
  specific purpose: the veto only needs Wanaharakati to not win, and it
  doesn't.
- **The same win-condition gate BREAKS a currently-correct production
  case**: for `walizindua` (Wanaharakati's real, already-correctly-
  identified long-distance nsubj, three clauses away, cont. 26), the
  gate's winner is `Tume` (4.647) or `ambao` (4.455), not Wanaharakati
  (1.454) -- applying this gate would have suppressed a case the
  pipeline currently gets right.
- Pattern across both verbs: edge-presence scores track CLAUSE-LOCAL
  proximity (Tume/ambao/viongozi, all structurally close to the
  relative clause containing both test verbs) far more than genuine
  gold attachment, for both the false positive AND the real long-
  distance case -- a positional/locality confound, not the clean
  arc/no-arc signal the architecture was meant to provide.

**Verdict: Liu et al.'s arc-existence idea, as already implemented in
this project's `edge_presence_probe.pt`, does not fix the Kudai case
either as an absolute gate (no change) or as a relative win-condition
gate (fixes Kudai, breaks walizindua -- net regression, not adopted).**
This is a third confirmed failure of the general "separate existence
from label" family against this project's two standing motivating
cases (mbwa/kijana via attempts 1-2; Kudai/Wanaharakati here), and adds
a new, specific diagnosis -- a locality confound -- not previously
documented for this probe. Consistent with the cont. 16 external-
critique framing: a probe trained on isolated (head, candidate) pairs,
with no conditioning on matrix-clause structure, cannot distinguish
"close in the string" from "really attached," in either direction.
n=1 sentence, qualitative motivating-case diagnostic only (same
evidentiary status this project has always given the Kudai/mbwa-kijana
cases individually) -- not a claim at any n, per hard rule #5.

No production code changed (`identify_relations()`/
`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` untouched); nothing wired in, nothing
reverted. The governor-attachment-probe direction from cont. 16/17
remains the one live, not-yet-tried proposal this project's own
critique round converged on; this result doesn't bear on it directly
(a head-attachment probe over the FULL dependency label set is a
different object than a binary "is there a noun 20 slots over there
related" classifier). File: `test_edge_presence_on_kudai_case.py`
(new, `Code_Experiments/`).

## 2026-10-10 (cont. 1b): built and trained the governor-attachment
probe, per direct request, resuming the track the user paused on
2026-10-09 (cont. 17) -- real improvement over the production
heuristic, but modest, and it does not by itself close the routing gap.

**Step 1 (critique's own prescribed order, never run before): tabulated
real gold '-ki-' verb head attachment against matrix-verb lemma**
(`tabulate_ki_governor_attachment.py`, no NLLB, pure CoNLL-U, SWH_UDT+
AfriSUD all splits, 1757 sentences). 319 '-ki-' verbs found (same
decompose_verb/tam_marker=='ki' filter as production). Results:
- 313/319 (98.1%) have a real gold head -- consistent with the earlier-
  cited 221/226 (97.8%) figure, now independently re-derived on this
  project's current code rather than re-citing the old number.
- Head UPOS: VERB 40.6%, **AUX 25.9%**, NOUN 11.8%, SCONJ 9.3%, ADP
  7.7%, rest small -- confirms rules 1-3's implicit assumption ("the
  governor is verb-shaped") covers only a slice of real cases; AUX-
  headed (mostly 'kuwa' periphrastics) and NOUN/SCONJ/ADP-headed cases
  were never separately characterized before.
- The '-ki-' verb's own deprel: comp 56.5%, mod 25.6%, conj 7.3%,
  parataxis 3.5%, advcl 2.6%, rest small -- matches the critique's
  cited label set almost exactly, confirming that citation was accurate.
- **Existing closed-list lexical routing (SPEECH_ACT_ROOTS/'...kuw'/
  PERCEPTION_ROOTS) covers only 25.2% of real governing heads; 74.8%
  fall to "other, no rule applies."** Even a perfect head-finder would
  still leave most cases needing either an expanded lexical list or a
  sensible default -- a separate, NOT-attempted-here problem.
- **The CURRENT production heuristic ("nearest preceding verb-shaped
  token") agrees with the real gold head only 66/127=52.0% of the time**,
  even restricted to the easiest subset (gold head tagged VERB).
  Disagreement examples are mostly genuine long-distance governors
  (e.g. real head 19 tokens earlier than the nearest verb-shaped token),
  not edge cases -- real, concrete justification for a structural probe,
  not an assumption.

**Step 2: built and trained the probe** (`governor_attachment_probe.py`
+ `train_and_save_governor_attachment_probe.py`, reusing RelationProbe/
train_concord_probe/evaluate_concord_probe/build_control_labels_binary
from nllb_concord_source_probe.py UNCHANGED, hard rule #10 -- same
pattern as edge_presence_probe.py, extended to a non-noun-restricted
candidate pool since real governors span almost every UPOS). Trained on
SWH_UDT+AfriSUD, 80/20 sentence split (1713/1757 kept after NLLB
alignment).

- Held-out classification: REAL acc=0.931 F1=0.655 vs CONTROL acc=0.527,
  **SELECTIVITY +0.404** (n=554, 62 positive) -- real, above-control
  signal, same range as this project's other validated probes.
- External win-rate (does the real head beat every other candidate),
  held-out only: probe 34/62=0.548 [95% CI 0.425,0.666] vs. heuristic
  27/62=0.435 [95% CI 0.319,0.559] on the SAME 62 held-out verbs --
  directionally better, CIs overlap.
- **Paired head-to-head on the same 62 cases** (the more informative
  comparison): both correct 21, probe-only-correct 13, heuristic-only-
  correct 6, both wrong 22. Net +7 cases in the probe's favor; a quick
  binomial check on the 19 discordant cases (13 vs 6) gives p~0.08 --
  real and consistent in direction, but NOT decisive at conventional
  significance, reported honestly rather than rounded up.

**Net state**: a real, moderate, probably-genuine improvement at finding
the real '-ki-' governor over the current string-position heuristic,
with routing (control-type dispatch) still unsolved for ~75% of real
cases regardless of head-finding quality. Not yet wired into
`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` -- doing so requires a decision this project
hasn't made about the "other, no rule" majority bucket (fall back to
self-loss? default to same-subject-as-matrix, the cross-linguistically
common control default? expand the lexical lists?), which is a separate
scope decision, not assumed here. Files: `tabulate_ki_governor_
attachment.py`, `governor_attachment_probe.py`, `train_and_save_
governor_attachment_probe.py` (all new), `saved_identification_probes/
governor_attachment_probe.pt` (new, trained weights).

## 2026-10-10 (cont. 1c): wired the governor-attachment probe into
production, per direct request ("wire in as head-finder only"). Zero
regressions.

Added `nllb_probe_identification.find_ki_governor()` -- loads the saved
`governor_attachment_probe.pt` (lazily, same pattern as pos_probe,
optional/graceful if missing), scores EVERY other token in the sentence
as a candidate governor for a given '-ki-' verb (same unrestricted pool
the probe was trained on), returns the best-scoring index. In
`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.decompose_sentence_with_probes()`, replaced the
"nearest preceding verb-shaped token" computation (`preceding_verbs[-1]`)
that fed rules 2/3 with a call to this function. Deliberately NOT falling
back to the old heuristic when the probe's pick isn't a usable,
already-resolved preceding verb clause -- that would reintroduce the
exact position-based failure the swap exists to fix; in that case rules
2/3 simply don't fire and self-loss remains the fallback, unchanged.
Rule 1 (reported-speech) was already heuristic-independent and is
untouched.

**Regression battery (`probe_pipeline_regression.py`): 12/12, zero
regressions** -- all standing motivating cases (mvulana/kalamu rule 3,
mbwa/kijana rule 3, rule 1, rule 2, cross-clause leakage, the two
standing zero-competing-candidate cases) still fire exactly as before,
now via the probe-identified governor instead of the string heuristic.

**Honest scope note, unchanged from cont. 1b**: this only improves
finding the governor; the control-type ROUTING gap (74.8% of real cases
have no matching rule in SPEECH_ACT_ROOTS/'...kuw'/PERCEPTION_ROOTS)
is untouched and remains the next real bottleneck if this track
continues. Files: `nllb_probe_identification.py` (extended:
`find_ki_governor`), `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (extended, hard rule
#10).

## 2026-10-10 (cont. 1d): ranked the uncovered 74.8% "other" bucket by
governor frequency before guessing what to add -- the single biggest
entry turned out to be a CONJUNCTION, not a verb, which reframed the
whole "expand the lexical list" plan; then checked the gold data again
BEFORE writing rule 4, since a naive version would have been wrong on
the majority of real cases.

Ranked `other (no rule)` governors by root frequency
(`examples_ki_other_bucket.py`, new): top entries were `wakati` (10.3%
of the bucket) and `huku` (3.0%) -- both subordinating conjunctions
("when/while"), not verbs. The next-biggest (`ni`, `ya`, `wa`, `kwa`,
`za`, `na`) are copulas/associative/prepositional particles, structurally
different again -- left alone, not swept into one list. Also caught a
real, separate bug while checking: `decompose_verb("ukimwi")` ("AIDS," a
plain noun) spuriously parses as a '-ki-' verb (u-SM + ki-TAM + "mw"
root + i-FV) -- a surface-pattern collision inflating the "other"
bucket's count with noise, flagged not fixed. The genuine remaining
long tail (`eleza`/"explain", `kamatwa`/"was arrested", `uawa`/"was
killed", `andika`/"write") is only 2-3 occurrences each -- too sparse
and varied to "expand the list" the way rules 1-3 did.

Files: `examples_ki_other_bucket.py` (new, diagnostic only, no
production code changed by this entry).

## 2026-10-10 (cont. 1e): built rule 4 (wakati/huku -> same-subject
default) -- but checked the gold data FIRST, since the naive version
would have been wrong on the majority of real cases, not a safe
default.

Before writing anything: checked how often real `wakati`/`huku`-governed
'-ki-' clauses actually carry their OWN overt local subject vs. need
inheritance from the matrix clause. Of 31 real gold cases across
SWH_UDT+AfriSUD, **20/31 (64.5%) have their OWN local subject** right
there in the clause -- e.g. "wakati kampeni zikiendelea" = "while the
CAMPAIGN was continuing," kampeni (not the matrix subject) is the real
one. Only 11/31 (35.5%) genuinely have no local subject and need
inheritance (e.g. "huku akiwahakikishia wananchi" -- the minister
reassuring, nothing local to find). An unconditional same-subject rule
would therefore have been wrong on the MAJORITY of real cases -- worse
than doing nothing. The signal that correlates cleanly with which
bucket a case is in: whether a fresh noun token sits strictly between
the conjunction and the '-ki-' verb (same "local window" check the
cross-clause-leakage fix, cont. 14, already uses).

**Built rule 4 with that guard**: `TEMPORAL_CONCESSIVE_CONJUNCTIONS =
("wakati", "huku")`, matched against the governor's raw surface form,
not a stripped root (`decompose_verb("wakati")`/`decompose_verb("huku")`
both confirmed to return `None` -- conjunctions have no SM/TAM/root/FV
structure to strip in the first place). Only applies the same-subject-
as-matrix default when there is NO fresh noun candidate between the
conjunction and the '-ki-' verb; otherwise leaves the regular probe's
(already-correct, local) answer untouched.

**Verified on two hand-built, lexicon-covered test sentences** (two
earlier attempts hit unrelated lexicon-coverage gaps -- "waziri"/"eneo"/
"wananchi" and "kampeni" aren't in this project's 319-word lexicon at
all, confirmed via empty `noun_hits`; a separate, pre-existing coverage
limit, not a rule-4 bug, that affects the guard the same way it affects
everything else in this pipeline):
- "Mwalimu alisoma kitabu huku akifanya kazi." (no local candidate) --
  rule 4 correctly fires, 'mwalimu' inherited as subject of 'akifanya'.
- "Mwalimu alisoma wakati mbwa akilia." ('mbwa' sits directly between
  'wakati' and 'akilia') -- rule 4 correctly does NOT fire; 'mbwa' is
  independently confirmed as its own subject via the pre-existing self-
  loss fallback, untouched by this change.

**Regression battery: 12/12, zero regressions.** Files:
`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (extended: `TEMPORAL_CONCESSIVE_CONJUNCTIONS`,
rule 4, hard rule #10).

## 2026-10-10 (cont. 1f): direct user proposal -- "switching to probe
fully for detection will help resolve ukimwi" -- confirmed, found a
bigger-than-expected contamination problem (15.7%, not a one-off), and
fixed it at BOTH the live-inference site and the offline-research site
(which had silently forked the same detection filter into 2 copies).

Checked before changing anything: (1) is `ukimwi` ("AIDS," a plain
noun) protected in production by the existing "nouns get claimed before
the verb decomposer runs" ordering? NO -- confirmed `_noun_lookup
("ukimwi", ...)` returns `None` (not in the 319-word lexicon), so it
was NOT protected; this was a live, real production bug, not just
training-data noise. (2) Does the already-trained POS probe correctly
tag `ukimwi` as NOUN in real context? YES, confirmed directly on the
real corpus sentence containing it.

**Quantified the contamination properly** (not just the one word):
50/319 (15.7%) of all `-ki-` verb detections across SWH_UDT+AfriSUD are
gold-tagged NOUN/PROPN, not VERB -- `decompose_verb`'s surface-pattern
match alone (SM+TAM+root+FV) spuriously fires on real nouns that
happen to collide with the shape, dominated by `wakimbizi` ("refugees")
and `ukimwi` ("AIDS"), both common words. This is bigger than a single
curiosity -- it had been quietly inflating every percentage reported in
cont. 1b/1d (the 319-verb counts, the 74.8%/25.2% routing split, the
52.0% heuristic-agreement rate) with real but mislabeled data.

**Found a real process gap while fixing it**: the '-ki-' detection
filter (decompose_verb + tam_marker=='ki' + root_guess>=2) existed as
TWO separate copies -- `tabulate_ki_governor_attachment.find_ki_verbs`
and `governor_attachment_probe.find_ki_verb_tokens` -- plus a THIRD
inline copy in `train_and_save_governor_attachment_probe.py`'s own
test-set construction. Fixing the filter in one would have silently
left the others wrong. Consolidated to ONE definition (`find_ki_verbs`,
now gold-UPOS-gated) and updated all three call sites to import it
(hard rule #10) -- this should have been one function from cont. 1b
onward, not three.

**Two separate fixes, same underlying bug, different available ground
truth**:
1. Offline/research path (gold CoNLL-U data available): `find_ki_verbs`
   now requires `t.upos == "VERB"` directly from the treebank -- gold
   truth, strictly better than any proxy.
2. Live inference path (`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.decompose_sentence_with_
   probes`, free text, no gold UPOS available): added a veto using the
   already-trained POS probe -- `if pos_tags[i] == "NOUN": continue`
   before accepting a `decompose_verb` result as a verb candidate, same
   pattern as the existing ADJ veto just above it. Deliberately a VETO
   on confident NOUN, not a requirement for confident VERB -- the POS
   probe's own VERB recall is 91.4%, not perfect, so requiring positive
   agreement would risk new false negatives on real verbs it's merely
   unsure about. Verified directly: "Mwalimu anaogopa ukimwi." ("The
   teacher fears AIDS") now correctly leaves `ukimwi` untouched instead
   of treating it as a live '-ki-' verb needing subject resolution.

**Re-ran everything downstream of the fix, not just the detector**:
- Tabulation re-run on clean data (269 '-ki-' verbs, down from 319):
  head-attachment rate 98.5% (was 98.1%, materially unchanged), routing
  coverage 27.9% (was 25.2%, modest real improvement from removing
  noise), heuristic agreement 53.4% (was 52.0%, unchanged within
  noise) -- the governor-attachment probe's underlying justification
  holds, numbers are now more trustworthy, not substantively different.
- Rule 4's wakati/huku validation (cont. 1e) re-checked on clean data:
  still exactly 31 cases, 20/31 own-subject vs. 11/31 needs-inheritance
  -- unaffected, since the contamination was governed by different
  words (ya/kwa/ni), not wakati/huku.
- **Retrained the governor-attachment probe on clean data**: selectivity
  improved to **+0.459** (was +0.404), recall 0.655 (was 0.581), F1
  0.704 (was 0.655) -- training on cleaner labels genuinely helped, not
  just cosmetic. Head-to-head vs. the heuristic: still net +7 (13 fixed,
  6 regressed), same magnitude as before, now on cleaner ground truth.
  Saved weights overwritten.
- **Regression battery re-run after each of the two production changes
  (NOUN veto, then the retrained probe weights): 12/12 both times, zero
  regressions.**

**Known, disclosed, NOT fixed**: `mine_ki_candidates.py` (the free-text
Bible-corpus miner feeding the self-loss silver-distillation attempts,
cont. 9 of 2026-10-09) has the exact same unguarded `decompose_verb`
pattern-match and no gold UPOS available to gate it with (free text, no
treebank). Same bug shape, different subsystem, not touched this
round -- that subsystem is already flagged as a dead end as attempted
(selectivity +0.054/+0.107, both far below gold-probe range) and not
currently wired into production, so lower priority than the two live
fixes above.

Files: `tabulate_ki_governor_attachment.py` (extended: `find_ki_verbs`
now gold-UPOS-gated, canonical definition), `governor_attachment_probe.
py` (removed duplicate detector, now imports the canonical one),
`train_and_save_governor_attachment_probe.py` (removed third duplicate,
imports the canonical one), `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (extended: POS-
probe NOUN veto on verb candidacy, hard rule #10), `saved_
identification_probes/governor_attachment_probe.pt` (retrained,
overwritten).

## 2026-10-10 (cont. 2): direct user proposal -- "fix Kudai by treating it
as a noun, since its role there is nominal" -- tested against the trained
POS probe (pos_probe.py), not assumed. Result: disconfirmed as stated, but
narrows down the real fix.

Ran `tag_pos()` (the already-trained, saved POS probe from 2026-10-08) on
5 hand-built "X anapenda ku-ROOT" infinitive-complement sentences plus the
real Kudai sentence. **Bare intransitive infinitives (kucheza, kucheka,
kusoma, kuandika, kuchecka) all tagged NOUN.** But adding an object flips
the SAME infinitive to VERB: `kusoma` alone -> NOUN; `kusoma kitabu` ->
VERB (kitabu itself tagged NOUN, correctly). Re-ran the real sentence:
`Kudai` (in "...ya Kudai Amani") tags **VERB**, same as `kushinikiza`
elsewhere in the same sentence -- both are bare infinitives immediately
followed by their own object (Amani; viongozi), same shape as the
synthetic "kusoma kitabu" case.

**Diagnosis**: the POS probe is not tracking finiteness/nominal-use at
all -- it's tracking "does this infinitive govern a following object,"
which correlates with VERB only because object-governing infinitives
look more like ordinary transitive verbs to a shallow linear probe, not
because the probe has learned anything about non-finite/control
structure. This means **filtering nsubj-candidacy by POS-probe NOUN tag
would not have caught the real Kudai case** -- it fires on bare
intransitive infinitives only, and Kudai (object-bearing) gets VERB from
the same mechanism as any transitive verb. Confirms (again, this time via
direct test rather than code-reading) that the fix needs to check
FINITENESS specifically (a real TAM marker after the subject-marker
slot, independent of POS category or object presence) -- not yet built.
n=7 sentences, qualitative diagnostic only, not a rate claim (hard rule
#5). No production code changed. File: `test_pos_probe_kuchecka.py`
(new, `Code_Experiments/`).

## 2026-10-11: "object identification" -- clarified which of 3 distinct
things this meant before starting (syntactic obj-relation ID, already
solved; object-MARKER presence/stripping in decompose_verb, a live bug;
object-marker REWRITE for Swahili-internal concord transplant, the
original Stage 4/5 gap). User picked the second. Built it on real gold
evidence, not assumed reference grammar; demonstrated end-to-end;
12/12 regression.

**Checked the gold data first**: SWH_UDT's `NounClass[obj]` feature (52
real instances; AfriSUD has no feats at all, confirmed earlier session)
gives direct ground truth. Confirmed directly, not assumed: this
feature does NOT mean an object-marker STRING is present on the verb --
e.g. gold `walithibitisha` ("they confirmed," Bantu1) and `hawangetoa`
(Bantu3) carry no object-marker substring at all. Object marking really
is optional, exactly as the 2026-10-05 note said -- this is presence-
DETECTION, not blind stripping.

**Built OM_TABLE from the confirmed cases**: class 2 "wa" (9 real
instances), class 5 "li" (5), class 9 "i" (4), class 1 "m"/vowel-
conditioned "mw" (5), class 6 "ya" (1), 1sg person "ni" (1). Every
CONFIRMED class (2,5,6,9) turns out to use the EXACT SAME string as
SM_TABLE's existing subject marker for that class -- classes 3/4/7/8/
10/11 extrapolate on this now-confirmed SM==OM pattern (standard
Bantu/Swahili fact, Ashton 1944/Mohammed 2001), not directly attested
in this corpus sample. Class 1 is the one CONFIRMED exception (SM "a"
vs OM "m"/"mw"). Person markers 2sg/1pl/2pl from reference grammar;
flagged, not resolved: 2pl and class-2 "them" are genuinely the SAME
string ("wa") in Swahili itself, not a gap in this table.

**Architecture: enumerate, don't strip** (`extract_swahili_grammar.
find_object_marker_candidates`, new `VerbFormEntry.object_marker_
candidates` field, `decompose_verb()`'s existing `root_guess`/
`final_vowel` UNCHANGED for every existing caller). Rejected blind
stripping on purpose -- same surface-collision risk as the '-ki-' verb-
detection bug fixed 2026-10-10 (a root that happens to START with an
OM-looking string, e.g. 'kuimba' with candidate OM 'i-', would be
wrongly truncated). The decision of which candidate (if any) is real is
made where the EVIDENCE actually lives: `translate_sentence_with_
probes()`'s existing Dice-score lookup against the Kitaita root
dictionary, reusing the already-existing (and, it turns out,
correctly-named) `OBJECT_MARKER_RISK_ROOT_DICE_THRESHOLD` as the bar --
only switches when the CURRENT root is already weak AND a candidate's
root scores clearly better; never disturbs an already-good match.

**Found and fixed a second, previously undocumented gap in the same
sweep**: `decompose_verb()` required a TAM match to return anything at
all -- bare infinitives (ku- + [object marker] + root + FV, grammatical
with NO tense marker) were silently unrecognized entirely, not just
root-corrupted. Confirmed directly: `kumtia`, `kuwafanya`, `kuyatatua`,
`kuwaunganisha`, `kuwasaidia` and 4 more real gold NounClass[obj]
examples all returned `None` before this fix. Added a bare-infinitive
branch (`sm=="ku"`, no TAM) using the same candidate-enumeration
mechanism.

**Validated three ways**:
1. Searched the Kitaita root dictionary directly for cases where
   stripping an OM candidate would improve the Dice score by >0.15:
   **47 real cases**, several converging cleanly from multiple person/
   class variants onto the same correct root (`wamez`/`yamez`/`mmez` ->
   `mez`, 0.2-0.3 -> 0.67; `msujudi`/`kusujudi`/`nisujudi` -> `sujudi`,
   ~0.25 -> 0.50) -- real linguistic signal, not noise.
2. **End-to-end demonstration**: "Nyoka alimmeza chura." ("The snake
   swallowed the frog") -> subject/object correctly identified (nyoka/
   chura), object marker `-m-` correctly detected, root corrected
   `mmez` (Dice 0.21) -> `mez` (Dice 0.67), flagged transparently as a
   heuristic correction, NOT silently applied. Kitaita output uses the
   corrected root.
3. **Regression battery: 12/12, zero regressions** -- critically, NONE
   of the existing "weak Dice match" warnings (akitembea/tembe, anakunywa/
   kunyw, akisema/sem, alipika/pik, akilala/lal) got spuriously
   "corrected" -- the heuristic correctly found no better-scoring
   candidate for any of these genuinely-unmarked intransitive verbs and
   left them untouched, exactly as designed.

**Scope, stated plainly**: this fixes Swahili ROOT EXTRACTION accuracy
in the e2e Swahili->Kitaita pipeline (`decompose_sentence_with_probes`/
`translate_sentence_with_probes` only -- the older non-probe `decompose_
sentence`/`translate_sentence` path was not touched). It does NOT
address the original Stage 4/5 gap from `nllb_concord_rewrite_
pipeline.py` ("obj -> object marker" REWRITE for Swahili-internal
concord transplant, excluded there since 2026-10-09) -- that's a
different task (rewriting an existing marker to match a NEW target
class), still open. Also not touched: the passive suffix "-w-" (a
different morphological layer, seen in several gold examples like
`alichapwa`/`amenyimwa` sometimes ALSO needing stripping) -- flagged,
not fixed.

## 2026-10-11 (cont. 2): obj REWRITE -- the original Stage 4/5 gap,
excluded from `nllb_concord_rewrite_pipeline.py` since 2026-10-09 for
lack of a presence-detection mechanism. Built on this morning's work,
caught and fixed a real reconstruction bug before trusting it, wired
into the actual 6-relation combined pipeline, demonstrated end-to-end
on a real sentence.

**`rewrite_object_marker(word, old_cls, new_cls)`** (nllb_concord_
rewrite_pipeline.py, alongside rewrite_sm/rewrite_adj_like/rewrite_poss/
rewrite_assoc): unlike those, the object marker is INFIXED (SM-TAM-OM-
ROOT-FV), not a prefix, so it can't reuse their strip-and-prepend
pattern. Locates the KNOWN old OM among `decompose_verb()`'s own
enumerated candidates (this morning's `OM_TABLE`); returns None (flag,
don't guess) if that exact candidate isn't present -- "currently
carries the noun's concord" (CLAUDE.md's own filter) is load-bearing
here, confirmed real: object marking is genuinely optional.

**Round-trip identity validation BEFORE any class-shifting attempt**
(all 49 real gold `NounClass[obj]`=BantuN examples, rewriting old_cls
-> SAME old_cls): first pass found a genuine bug -- `kulifuatilia`
("to follow it(cls5) up," no tense marker) was returning `None`
instead of round-tripping. Root cause: `decompose_verb()`'s TAM-
matching loop greedily consumes "li" as the PAST tense marker before
ever reaching the bare-infinitive-with-OM branch added this morning --
"li" genuinely collides between both readings (confirmed: TAM "li" and
class-5 OM "li" are the same string), and the TAM-first reading
returns early with `object_marker_candidates=[]`. **Found a second,
compounding bug while fixing the first**: naively adding `(tam, root,
fv)` as an extra OM candidate caused `rewrite_object_marker` to
reconstruct `v.subject_marker + v.tam_marker + new_om + ...`, DOUBLE-
COUNTING "li" (producing "kulilifuatilia", not "kulifuatilia") --
caught by the round-trip test itself before trusting the fix. Fixed
properly: `object_marker_candidates` entries now carry a 4th field,
`suppress_tam`, set True only for this ambiguous reading; `rewrite_
object_marker` and the presence-detection code in `kitaita_e2e_
pipeline.py` (this morning's work, same tuple shape, updated together)
both now check it before reconstructing.

**Final validation, after the fix**: round-trip identity 25/49 OK,
24/49 correctly flagged None (no OM present), **0/49 mismatches**.
Heterogeneous-class demo (5 hand-picked real verbs, genuine class
changes not just identity), all morphologically correct: `kuwafanya`
(cls2->9) -> `kuifanya`; `kuwasaidia` (cls2->1) -> `kumsaidia`;
`kuipatia` (cls9->2) -> `kuwapatia`; `kulifuatilia` (cls5->6) ->
`kuyafuatilia`; `alimwamuru` (cls1->2) -> `aliwaamuru`.

**Wired into the real 6-relation combined pipeline** (`run_pipeline()`
in `nllb_concord_rewrite_pipeline.py`, obj branch added right after
nsubj, reusing the SAME already-trained `nsubj_probe`'s "obj" label --
no new probe needed, the identification half was already validated at
0.889 win-rate). **End-to-end demonstration on a real gold sentence**
(loaded the already-saved identification probes directly rather than
paying the ~20-30min full retrain cost): "Nina furaha kwamba hatimaye,
suluhisho ya kiteknolojia limepatikana na kuwaunganisha wabunge na
wananchi" ("...and uniting the MPs and citizens"), target noun
`wabunge` (class 2), rewritten hypothetically to class 9 ->
`kuwaunganisha` correctly becomes `kuiunganisha` ("to unite IT"),
morphologically exact. Honest observation surfaced by this test, not a
new bug: the SAME run also flagged `wabunge` as a candidate object of
`Nina` ("I have") -- a pre-existing false identification from the
already-disclosed-as-imperfect (0.889, not 1.0) obj relation probe,
not something this change introduced; `rewrite_object_marker` correctly
found no object marker on `Nina` and safely returned None, so nothing
wrong was ever applied -- the safety net worked exactly as designed
even when fed a wrong upstream identification.

Files: `nllb_concord_rewrite_pipeline.py` (extended: `rewrite_object_
marker`, obj branch in `run_pipeline()`, hard rule #10), `extract_
swahili_grammar.py` (extended: `object_marker_candidates` tuples now
carry `suppress_tam`, fixing the "li" double-count bug), `kitaita_e2e_
pipeline.py` (updated to match the new 4-tuple shape).

## 2026-10-11 (cont. 3): acl:relcl REWRITE -- the LAST unsolved
mechanism gap in the original CLAUDE.md Stage 4/5 relation list (the
relative marker's position inside the verb was flagged unsolved since
2026-10-05 cont. 12-16). Built the same way as obj this session: real
gold data first, enumerate-don't-strip, round-trip validation before
any class-shift demo, then wired into the real 6-relation pipeline.

**Checked SWH_UDT's `NounClass[rel]` gold feature first** (67 real
instances -- same feature family as `[obj]`/`[subj]`, found while
checking those this morning). Confirmed directly, multiple independent
examples each: class 1 "ye" (aliyesoma, aliyelizuia), class 2 "o"
(waliokuwa, wanaoongoza, waliofariki x2), class 5 "lo" (linalosumbua,
linalopaswa), class 6 "yo" (wanayohitaji, yaliyopita), class 7 "cho"
(kilichotokea, kilichojitokeza, kinachotawala, kinachoitwa), class 8
"vyo" (alivyohukumiwa, wanavyowakilisha), class 9 "yo" (inayodumu,
inayotumika, iliyotolewa), class 10 "zo" (8 instances), class 11 "o"
(unaohusiana, usiojulikana). Classes 3/4/14 extrapolated (not directly
attested): for 4-10 the REL string is exactly ASSOC_TABLE's consonant +
"o" instead of "a" -- checked directly, every attested case matches
this transformation (ya->yo, la->lo, cha->cho, vya->vyo, za->zo); 1/2/3
are the confirmed exceptions, not derivable from ASSOC_TABLE. **Slot
order confirmed directly**: REL comes BEFORE any object marker, not
after -- "inayoikabili" = i-na-yo-i-kabili (REL "yo" then OM "i").

**Architecture: same enumerate-don't-strip discipline as OM_TABLE**
(`REL_TABLE`, `find_relative_marker_candidates`, new `VerbFormEntry.
relative_marker_candidates` field, populated only for FINITE verb forms
-- relative clauses need a conjugated verb, so the bare-infinitive
branch doesn't get this field). `rewrite_relative_marker()` in `nllb_
concord_rewrite_pipeline.py`: locates the known old REL string among
the enumerated candidates, swaps it for the new class's string, leaves
everything after it (including any object marker further inside the
word) untouched -- simpler than the obj case since REL rewrite doesn't
need to also decompose the remainder.

**Round-trip identity validation on all 67 real gold examples BEFORE
any class-shift demo** (the lesson from this morning's "li" bug, applied
proactively this time): **38/67 clean round-trips, 0/67 mismatches**,
17/67 correctly flagged None, 12/67 skipped (classes outside REL_TABLE,
e.g. locative class 16 which appears often in this feature but was
never built since no reference/corpus confirmation exists for it yet).
The 17 flagged-None cases were inspected individually, not just counted
-- a genuinely diverse, mostly-explainable set, not one bug repeated:
- Negation forms ("-si-") aren't decomposed by `decompose_verb()` AT
  ALL (a pre-existing gap, not introduced here -- "si" was never in
  TAM_MARKERS) -- affects `usiojulikana`, `usiojali`, `wasioamini`.
- A "manner-vyo" idiom: class-8 "vyo" used for HOW/manner relatives
  regardless of the literal head-noun class (`lilivyoongeza` tagged
  class 9 but surfaces "vyo", not "yo") -- a real, known Bantu pattern,
  not an error in either the gold tag or this table.
- **New finding, not previously documented**: REL undergoes VOWEL
  ELISION before a vowel-initial root, the same KIND of phenomenon
  already known for SM's u/w glide -- `kilichanganyika` is `ki-li-ch-
  anganyika` (REL "cho" elides its final vowel before "a-initial"
  anganyika), not matched by this round's plain substring search.
  Flagged, not fixed this round -- a real, disclosed limitation.
- The already-known "-ja-...-zo" suffix-REL pattern (`zijazo`).
- Conjoined verbs that share a referent without repeating the marker
  (`kinaongelea`, `utapoteza`, both deprel=conj).
- One likely corpus typo (`inyayoikabili` -- confirmed directly that
  the correctly-spelled `inayoikabili` parses and matches cleanly).

**Heterogeneous-class demo** (6 hand-picked real verbs, genuine class
changes): all morphologically correct -- `aliyesoma` (1->7) ->
`alichosoma`; `waliokuwa` (2->1) -> `waliyekuwa`; `kinachotawala`
(7->9) -> `kinayotawala`; `zinazounga` (10->8) -> `zinavyounga`;
`linalosumbua` (5->6) -> `linayosumbua`; `inayodumu` (9->10) ->
`inazodumu`.

**Wired into `run_pipeline()`'s real 6-relation combined pipeline**,
replacing the old "<IDENTIFIED but rewrite not attempted>" placeholder
-- no new probe needed, reuses the already-validated acl probe
(win-rate 0.836, n=55). **End-to-end on a real gold sentence** (loaded
the already-saved probes directly, skipped the retrain): "...msomi
aliyesoma katika nchi za Magharibi..." ("...a scholar who studied in
Western countries..."), target `msomi` class 1 -> hypothetically class
7, correctly produces `alichosoma`. **Regression battery: 12/12, zero
regressions.**

**With this, the original CLAUDE.md Stage 4/5 relation list is now
fully implemented**: nsubj, obj (identification + rewrite, this
morning), amod/det, associative/case, nmod:poss, and now acl:relcl
(identification + rewrite) -- the one mechanism gap that remained open
since this pipeline's very first combined run (cont. 26, 2026-10-05) is
closed. Remaining known limitations, all disclosed above rather than
hidden: vowel elision, negation forms, the manner-vyo idiom, and the
suffix-REL pattern are all real phenomena this round's plain-
substring-match approach doesn't cover -- a natural next increment if
this track continues, not attempted today.

relative_marker_candidates`, `decompose_verb()`'s finite-form branch,
hard rule #10), `bantu_grammar.py` (extended: `VerbFormEntry.relative_
marker_candidates`), `nllb_concord_rewrite_pipeline.py` (extended:
`rewrite_relative_marker`, acl:relcl branch in `run_pipeline()`, hard
rule #10).

## 2026-10-11 (cont. 4): Kitaita-side adjective concord, per direct
request ("a per class table that gives the adjective's prefix for
every adjective and an adjective root table, similar to what we have
for verbs"). Checked first whether the raw material already existed --
it did: `concord_families["adjective"]` in page1_vocabulary.json had 9
Bible-corpus-mined adjective families (built 2026-10-07), never
processed past an explicitly flagged "open lead, not pursued further"
note, never wired into `translate()`. Processed that existing data
(`extract_adjective_concord_tables.py`, new), did not re-mine the
corpus, and found a real, previously-undocumented structural question.

**Real finding**: kubwa's own prefix series (m-/i-/ki-/vi- for
default/ji/chi/va-class nouns -- "vi-" newly found this round from the
SAME mined data, "vikubwa"->"vibaa", Dice 0.44, "high" confidence, not
acted on until caught by a direct end-to-end test below) is a REDUCED
series, consistently SHORTER than the noun's own full subject-marker
prefix (kit_sm): ji->i, chi->ki, va->vi. This looks like a separate
Kitaita ADJECTIVE-concord series, parallel to how Swahili's own
ADJ_BASE differs from SM_TABLE. BUT: the one OTHER adjective with 2+
independently-confirmed classes, 'zuri' (good), does NOT follow this
reduced series -- both its confirmed classes (i-, wi-) use the noun's
FULL kit_sm + shared root 'ghokie', the SAME strategy as 'baya'
(already speaker-confirmed). **n=2 adjectives point two different
ways** -- genuinely unresolved which pattern is "the" Kitaita adjective
default, not asserted either way. Recorded as `KITAITA_ADJ_BASE_
HYPOTHESIS` (explicitly labeled hypothesis, not fact).

**Built, with honest confidence tiers, not uniform claims**:
- `KUBWA_FORM_BY_SM` extended to 3 confirmed classes (ji/chi/va), all
  from real corpus data, consistent with the m-/i-/ki-/vi- reduced-
  series pattern.
- `ZURI_ROOT = "ghokie"`, generalized the SAME way as baya (kit_sm +
  root), but explicitly flagged as a corpus STATISTICAL candidate
  (Dice 0.40-0.58), NOT native-speaker-verified like baya -- a
  materially weaker evidence tier, stated as such in the trace output.
- `ADJ_SINGLE_CLASS_CANDIDATE`: the other 6 mined stems (dogo, geni,
  refu, zito, chafu, fupi), each a SINGLE data point for ONE Swahili
  class only, explicitly NOT generalized to any other class (unlike
  zuri/baya, there's no second confirming class to show a pattern at
  all). 'dogo' flagged EXTRA untrustworthy: its best corpus match
  ("mtini") is very likely the SAME noun-collision artifact already
  found 2026-10-08 (mdogo/mtini), not a real adjective form.

**Found and fixed a real, would-have-shipped bug via direct testing**:
`compute_adjective_concord()` in `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` is a THIRD,
separate copy of the SAME kubwa/baya rule logic (for when an adjective
modifies a noun OTHER than the sentence's subject, e.g. the `amod_on_
object_mdogo` regression case) -- missed on the first pass, caught only
because renaming `KUBWA_IBAA_SM` broke its import and crashed the
regression battery. Also missed, same cause: `export_e2e_js_tables.py`
and `export_grammar_pages.py`. All fixed, all consistent now. **This is
the THIRD time this exact failure shape has appeared this session**
(object-marker tuple shape, '-ki-' verb detection, now this) -- grep
for every call site before renaming/extending a shared table is now a
standing lesson, not a one-off.

**Verified end-to-end on live sentences** (not just unit-level):
"Nyumba nzuri ilikuwa." (i-class, CONFIRMED) -> "Nyumba ighokie
ideka."; "Mwalimu mzuri alisoma." (u-class, EXTRAPOLATED, correctly
flagged as such in the trace) -> "Mwalimu ughokie udeshoma."; "Watu
wachafu walikuja." (class 2, the ONE class chafu has data for) ->
correctly applied "makakala"; "Vitabu vikubwa vilikuwa." (va-class) ->
correctly applied the newly-added "vibaa" (this exact sentence is what
caught the compute_adjective_concord bug above, before the va fix was
wired into that function too). **Regression battery: 12/12 after every
change.**

**Honest net state**: this is genuinely closer to root_kitaita's own
character (a statistical, Dice-scored candidate table with explicit
confidence tiers, mirroring how verb roots are already handled) than
to a finished, speaker-verified paradigm -- which is exactly what was
asked for ("similar to what we have for verbs"). Only kubwa (4 classes)
and baya (5 classes, speaker-confirmed) are reasonably solid; zuri (2
classes) and the single-class candidates for the other 6 stems need
either more corpus mining (cross-version aggregation, not yet done for
adjectives) or direct native-speaker testing via the Kitaita Workbench
to move past "statistical lead." The open structural question (reduced
adjective-series vs full-kit_sm) is the single most useful thing to
ask the speaker next, since it would resolve the default for every
future untested adjective at once, not just one word at a time.

Kijana mdogo akitembea." still shows untranslated 'mdogo' instead of
the 'dogo' single-class candidate 'mtini'. Traced directly rather than
assumed: `compute_adjective_concord()` (the non-subject-adjective path,
used here because 'kijana' is the SUBJECT of the SECOND clause
'akitembea', not a secondary/object noun) had the exact gap flagged in

label `ADJ_SINGLE_CLASS_CANDIDATE` is keyed by.

`_noun_lookup()` (the SAME class-resolution function every other noun
in this pipeline already uses, hard rule #10) to resolve the target
noun's Swahili class inside `compute_adjective_concord()` itself.

**Result, confirmed via the TRACE field (the flags field doesn't carry
adjective messages -- checked directly after an initial false read)**:
the fix works correctly, and correctly does NOT apply 'mtini' here --

`ADJ_SINGLE_CLASS_CANDIDATE["dogo"]` was attested for. This is NOT a

uncertainties (dogo/mtini is already flagged LOW-TRUST/likely a noun-
collision artifact; separately, kijana's OWN class is already
documented, since 2026-10-09, as a known animacy-override case that
should really take class 1/2 agreement despite its ki-/vi- shape --
never coded into a fix, only ever a narrative finding until now
confirmed still unfixed). Explained to the user rather than forced.

Regression battery: 12/12. Restarted the local webapp (same stale-
code lesson as cont. "It's good" -- Python doesn't hot-reload, and the
running instance predated this fix).

**Open, not done**: a general Swahili animacy-class-override table

the kitaita class groupings and we already have kijana -> mdawana
which uses adjective marker 'm'." Right, and more general than just
this one case: cont. 5's fix was gated on matching the TARGET noun's

seen` -- exactly the kind of label-matching this project has
repeatedly found unreliable. The actual signal that matters is the

whatever Kitaita-class pattern the candidate's OWN surface form
demonstrates -- which is already available via the SAME reduced-
prefix series (`KITAITA_ADJ_BASE_HYPOTHESIS`) kubwa already uses.

**Checked directly, not assumed, before generalizing**: does each of
the 6 single-class candidates' own Kitaita surface form decompose
against that reduced series (m-/i-/ki-/vi-)? **4 of 6 do, cleanly**:

neither starts with m-/i-/ki-/vi-) -- correctly stay as genuinely

root here, not kubwa's 3+ independently-confirmed classes). Added a

`translate()` and `compute_adjective_concord()` -- after the exact

three separate times (object-marker tuple shape, '-ki-' verb
detection, the kubwa/baya/zuri rules), a shared helper for the lookup
itself, not just parallel branches re-deriving it, is the actual fix
to the pattern, not just another instance of it.

## 2026-10-11 (cont. 7): direct user report -- "Mwanafunzi mrefu
alimwona mzee akitembea na viatu vyako," subject of 'akitembea' should
be 'mzee' (it already was, per the flags -- rule 3 fired correctly)
but "we aren't translating everything." Traced each gap separately
rather than assuming one cause.

**Real bug, fixed**: `mzee` ("elder") has a known Swahili class
(ANIMATE-SG, 319-word lexicon) but ZERO Kitaita translation candidates
at all. `translate()` treated this as a HARD STOP -- returned an
immediate error, which aborted the ENTIRE second clause including the
VERB, even though the verb's subject-marker only needs the noun's
CLASS, not a specific translated word. This is why the output showed
'akitembea' completely untranslated -- not a wrong subject, a verb
that never got built at all, which made the correct subject
identification invisible in the output.

**Fixed with a class-level fallback, scoped narrow on purpose**:
`SWAHILI_CLASS_DEFAULT_SM_GUESS = {"ANIMATE-SG": "u", "ANIMATE-PL":
"wi"}`, explicitly EXCLUDING the animal lemmas already confirmed to
diverge (mbwa/nyoka/simba/ndege/chui all take 'i', samaki takes 'ri' --
checked the lexicon directly: ANIMATE-SG covers 57 words, a mix of
unambiguous humans (confirmed 'u') and animals (confirmed OTHER
classes, inconsistent even with each other) -- a blanket rule would
have been a confident wrong guess for the animals, exactly the
"label lies" pattern this project keeps finding). Applied only when
no specific translation exists at all; the noun itself still stays in
the original Swahili (the existing assembly fallback already handles
this correctly once `kit_subject` is None -- no changes needed there).
Verified: 'akitembea' -> 'ukisela' now, correctly using the fallback
'u-' marker; 'mzee' correctly stays untranslated and flagged.
**Regression: 12/12.**

**Remaining gaps in this same sentence, reported honestly, not all
fixed**: 'mrefu' (tall) -- the already-known 'refu' single-data-point
lead that doesn't decompose against the reduced Kitaita prefix series
(cont. 6) -- correctly flagged, needs more data or direct speaker
input, not fixable by guessing. 'na' (with/and) and 'vyako' (your,
class 8 possessive) -- BOTH fall through as "no mechanism" because
the live free-text pipeline (`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`) has NEVER had

Direct user instruction, four sub-tasks in one message: "wire in

**(a) Why possessives weren't wired with adjectives.** Checked
directly: `tag_pos(['viatu','vyako'])` -> `[('viatu','NOUN'),
('vyako','OTHER')]`. Gold UD/SUD tags possessive pronouns DET/PRON, a
different category from true adjectives, even though the surface
morphology (concord prefix + stem) looks identical -- the adjective
sweep gates on `pos_tags[i]=="ADJ"` and so structurally cannot catch
these regardless of detection logic. Needed its own morphological
check, not a POS-probe fallback.

`find_possessive_pronoun()` (`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`): longest-

short possessive token is never mistaken for a verb. `identify_

loaded (win-rate 1.000, n=15, nmod:poss) since this module's first
version but NEVER CALLED anywhere -- extended its signature with

mirroring the `amod_probe` loop exactly (same win-condition pattern,
