## 2026-10-13 (cont. 2)

Direct user instruction, rearchitecting cont. 0's "i" class split:
"it would be just easier to come up with a new -i- class that has the
same subject markers as the existing i- class but that has different
adjective markers the way in Swahili they are treated as different
classes." Cont. 0's fix worked but was an invisible lookup-time hack
(a hardcoded noun set, `I_CLASS_NASAL_NOUNS`, checked only at the
moment of an adjective lookup) -- a noun's "real" class was never
recorded anywhere a human or the Word Bank could see or set it. This
replaces that with "i_nasal" as a GENUINE, independently selectable
class, same status as every other class ("u"/"ghu"/"ji"/etc).

**Design**: a noun's class can now literally BE "i_nasal" (in
VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS, noun_class_of, or the Word Bank's noun
dropdown) -- no per-noun side table needed, matching how every OTHER
class already works. The only new machinery is `TAM_SM_ALIAS =
{"i_nasal": "i"}` (kitaita_verified_corrections.py): applied EXACTLY
ONCE, immediately after a noun's class is first resolved in
`translate()` (kitaita_sentence_generator.py) and BEFORE any TAM-
conditioned vowel-shift logic runs, so every existing shift rule keeps
working unmodified on an "i_nasal" noun (it shares "i"'s whole TAM
paradigm by construction, per the Swahili class-4-vs-9/10 precedent).
Split one variable into two: `kit_class` (the raw, possibly-"i_nasal"
class, carried through to the ADJECTIVE block unmodified) and `kit_sm`
(TAM-normalized, used for literally everything else -- verb assembly,
vowel shifts). `compute_adjective_concord()` (kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py)
needed no such split -- it never builds a TAM-dependent string, so its
`kit_sm` (from `resolve_class_marker()`) can just BE the raw class
directly. Added `adjective_formula_prefix()` for the two FORMULA-based
adjective rules (baya/zuri, which splice a class string directly into
a word) -- identity for every class except "i_nasal", which resolves
to the real phonological prefix "nd-", not the literal text
"i_nasal-". The DICT-based rules (kubwa/refu/dogo/geni/fupi/zito/
chafu's FORM_BY_SM tables) needed no such conversion -- they're

## 2026-10-15: per-root verb fallback was person-blind -- fixed to derive a real root and run it through normal SM/TAM rules

User started the local webapp (`kitaita_local_webapp.py`, port 8765)
to test ahead of a meeting, explicitly deferring vocabulary-addition
work. Testing "Mwalimu anapenda kusoma." ("the teacher likes reading")
surfaced a genuine bug, caught by the user asking directly why a
correctly-identified 3rd-person noun subject (`mwalimu`, class `u`)
produced the verb form `kwadakunda` -- which bakes in `kwa-`, the
native-speaker-VERIFIED 2sg-present PERSON marker
(`PERSON_SUBJECT_MARKERS_BY_TAM[("2sg","present")]`), not anything
derived from `mwalimu`'s own agreement.

**Root cause, confirmed directly against `page1_vocabulary.json`**:
the root `pend` (love/like) has no root-level Dice candidate at all
(`root_level_kitaita_candidates: []`). The per-root FALLBACK
(`root_kitaita_candidate`, consulted when that happens) is built at
corpus-mining time by taking the single globally-highest-Dice
(Swahili surface form, Kitaita word) pair across **every** attested
inflected form of the root, with no constraint that the form's
person/tense matches anything -- for `pend`, 3 forms had any aligned
candidate at all (`ukipenda`->`kukakunda` Dice 0.40, `anapenda`
[**3sg, the one that actually matches `mwalimu`**]->`kiwachenyi` Dice
0.44, `unapenda` [2sg]->`kwadakunda` Dice 0.57), and the 2sg form won
purely on raw score. The generator then used that whole word AS-IS
(`root_is_full_form=True`), explicitly skipping subject-marker/TAM
substitution (the existing trace already said why: no known morpheme
boundary inside an opaque fallback word) -- so `mwalimu`'s own
correctly-computed `u`->`wa` present-tense marker was computed but
discarded, never reaching the output.

**Fix** (`kitaita_sentence_generator.py`): added
`_derive_fallback_root()`, a new, lower-priority resolution tier
between root-level Dice and the raw-fallback last resort. Instead of
trusting one person-specific whole word, it looks for a REAL root
hiding inside >=2 INDEPENDENTLY-aligned fallback forms (longest common
suffix across every pair of candidate words) -- the same
"agreement-across-independent-evidence" bar this project uses
everywhere else. For `pend`: `kukakunda` and `kwadakunda` share the
suffix `-akunda`; `kiwachenyi` (the non-agreeing 3sg outlier) shares
nothing with either and is correctly excluded. First pass used the
raw longest common suffix verbatim and got `-akunda` -> derived root
`akund`, which round-tripped to `waweakunda` -- phonologically odd
(vowel hiatus `ea`, not attested anywhere else in this project's
Kitaita output). Per the user's own direct correction ("penda ->
kunda"), added one more rule: Bantu verb roots are consonant-initial,
so a matched suffix that STARTS with a vowel has very likely overshot
into the PRECEDING TAM syllable's own final vowel (`ka`/`da` both
happen to end in `-a`), not the root -- trim leading vowels off the
match (while enough material remains) before treating it as the root.
That turns `-akunda` into `-kunda` -> derived root `kund`, exactly
matching the user's own stated answer. When a derived root is used,
`root_is_full_form` is left `False`, so the ALREADY-correct
subject-marker/TAM substitution logic runs normally on it instead of
being skipped.

**Result, confirmed directly** (`curl` against the restarted local
webapp): "Mwalimu anapenda kusoma." now produces "Mwalimu wawekunda
kushoma." -- `mwalimu`'s own verified `u`->`wa` present-tense marker is
now actually applied, instead of a 2nd-person marker from an unrelated
corpus sentence. Trace: `"Verb root 'pend': ... DERIVED root 'kund'
from 2 independently-aligned fallback forms agreeing on the shared
material '-kunda' ('ukipenda'->'kukakunda' Dice 0.40, 'unapenda'->
'kwadakunda' Dice 0.57) -- NOT native-speaker-verified, lower
confidence than a root-level Dice match, but runs through normal
subject-marker/TAM substitution below rather than reusing either whole
form as-is"`.

**Explicitly NOT claimed**: `kund` is NOT native-speaker-verified --
flagged as DERIVED in the trace, lowest of the three root-resolution
tiers (VERIFIED_ROOTS > root-level Dice > this), used only when
neither of those exists. Only tested on this one root so far; the
leading-vowel-trim rule is motivated by general Bantu root shape plus
this one confirmed case, not yet cross-checked against a second
multi-form-agreement root.

**Regression**: `probe_pipeline_regression.py`, 12/12, both before and
after the leading-vowel-trim refinement -- this fallback tier is new
and wasn't exercised by any of those 12 cases, so "no regressions" here
means "nothing broke," not "this path was re-validated by the battery."

**Separately noticed, NOT fixed (out of scope of this fix, flagging
for later)**: the present-tense TAM branch's trace string still says
"Kitaita zero-marked present (corpus-dominant form ... vs ~0 for the
'-we-' variant)" but the actual value used is `PRESENT_TAM_DEFAULT =
"we"` (cont. 15's deliberate override of the zero-marked corpus
default, per direct speaker style instruction) -- the trace wording
describes the superseded cont. 14 rationale, not the cont. 15 decision
the code actually implements. Self-consistent in behavior, misleading
in its own trace text; a hard-rule-#2-flavored loose end someone
should clean up.

**Changed call signature**: `build_lookup_tables()` now returns a
6-tuple (added `root_kitaita_derived` at the end) instead of 5;
`translate()`'s unpack updated to match. Every other caller that
destructures the full tuple by name (`kitaita_relations.py`,
`bucket_abc_analysis.py`, `export_e2e_js_tables.py`) updated to match;
callers that only index specific positions (`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`,
`kitaita_local_webapp.py`, `compare_js_python_translate.py`,
`probe_pipeline_regression.py`, `kitaita_sentence_batch.py`,
`build_pages.py`) are unaffected since the new element was appended at
the end, not inserted.

Files: `kitaita_sentence_generator.py` (new
`_derive_fallback_root()`; `build_lookup_tables()` and `translate()`
signatures), `kitaita_relations.py`, `bucket_abc_analysis.py`,
`export_e2e_js_tables.py` (tuple-unpack updates only, no logic
changes).

## 2026-10-15 (cont. 1): wired up 1st/2nd-person pro-drop + negation detection in the free-text pipeline; Swahili grammar reviewed first

User asked to review "the current Swahili grammar book" (the reference
tables in `extract_swahili_grammar.py`, not the stale `bantu_grammar_
swahili.json` mining snapshot) before extending it, to check it
generalizes rather than accumulating special cases. Reviewed: the
whole affirmative system is one template (`SM + TAM + [OM]? + ROOT +
FV`) driven by two flat tables (`SM_TABLE`, `TAM_MARKERS`) tried in one
greedy longest-match loop, with OM/REL handled as enumerated
candidates (never asserted) rather than extra branches. Confirmed this
generalizes cleanly before adding to it.

**Gap 1 -- 1st/2nd-person pro-drop** ("Ninapenda" = I like, no noun
subject at all). `kitaita_sentence_generator.translate()` already had
a full `person=` substitution path (`PERSON_SUBJECT_MARKERS_BY_TAM`,
built 2026-10-08) -- it was simply never reachable from free text:
`decompose_verb()`'s SM-candidate list only ever held NOUN-CLASS
strings (`SM_TABLE`'s values), so "ninapenda"/"tunapenda"/"mnapenda"
failed to parse as a verb AT ALL (none of SM_TABLE's strings prefix
them), and `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` explicitly refused ("pro-drop
subjects are not attempted here") whenever no noun was found.

**Gap 2 -- negation** ("sipendi" = I do not like). Swahili negative-
present has a different shape entirely (NEG-subject-prefix + root +
'-i', no TAM slot) and was not recognized by the decomposer at all --
`NEGATION_MARKERS` existed only as inert reference data exported to
`page3_verb_rules.json`, never consulted by any parser. Separately,
confirmed directly: there is NO Kitaita negation marker anywhere in
this project's data (CLAUDE.md open decisions) -- so the right
behavior is detect-and-refuse, never guess one.

**Fix, `extract_swahili_grammar.py`**:
- `PERSON_SM_TABLE = {"ni":"1sg","tu":"1pl","m":"2pl","u":"2sg"}`
  (reference grammar, Ashton 1944) merged directly into `decompose_
  verb()`'s existing SM-candidate loop -- zero new branches, same
  mechanism noun-class SMs already use. "u" collides with class 3/11's
  own string; left ambiguous here, disambiguated only at the sentence
  level (prefer a real noun subject when one exists).
- `NEGATIVE_SM_IRREGULAR` (si/hu/ha/hatu/ham/hawa for 1sg/2sg/3sg-cl1/
  1pl/2pl/3pl-cl2 -- genuinely suppletive, reference grammar) +
  `NEGATIVE_SM_TRANSPARENT` (classes 3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,11,15, generated
  PROGRAMMATICALLY as `"ha"+SM_TABLE[cls]` so it can't drift out of
  sync with the affirmative table). New `decompose_negative_verb()`,
  tried only as a fallback after every affirmative reading fails (zero
  risk to anything already working), requires final vowel literally
  '-i' as the one unambiguous signal this is negative-present and not
  an unrelated word. Scope: present only -- past/future/perfect
  negative have different shapes, flagged as a follow-on, not
  attempted.
- `bantu_grammar.VerbFormEntry` gets two new optional fields
  (`person`, `negated`) carrying this through.

**Fix, `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`**: both `decompose_sentence()` and
`decompose_sentence_with_probes()` now check the verb's own `.negated`/
`.person` whenever no reliable noun subject exists for it (sentence-
level AND per-verb, inside the probe-based nsubj loop) -- negated sets
a clear refusal flag (CLAUDE.md gap, never a silently-affirmative
output); a recognized person sets `d.person`/`clause["person"]` and
lets `translate(..., person=...)` run instead of refusing.
`translate_sentence()`/`translate_sentence_with_probes()`'s early bail-
out guards relaxed to let a person-only (no noun) case through.
**Found and fixed one real bug while testing this, pre-existing and
unrelated to the new tables**: "Mnapenda" (2pl) was being silently
claimed as a NOUN by `decompose_sentence_with_probes()`'s noun_hits
loop -- even though the POS probe correctly tagged it VERB -- because
`_noun_lookup`'s confidence filter was deliberately removed project-
wide (2026-10-09) and it matched a near-noise statistical candidate
(Dice 0.29, 1 attestation, no class). The noun_hits loop already
veto'd a confident ADJ tag from noun candidacy but had no symmetric
veto for a confident VERB tag (the verb_hits loop DOES veto a
confident NOUN tag, just not the reverse) -- added the missing,
symmetric veto.

**Verified directly** (`curl` against the restarted local webapp, all
after the VERB-veto fix):
- `"Ninapenda kusoma."` -> `"Nawekunda kushoma."` (1sg present, corpus-
  induced hypothesis, flagged as such)
- `"Unapenda kusoma."` -> `"Kwawekunda kushoma."` (2sg present, VERIFIED)
- `"Tunapenda kusoma."` / `"Mnapenda kusoma."` -> `"?wekunda kushoma."`
  (1pl/2pl present: correctly flagged "NO corpus evidence", not guessed
  -- PERSON_SUBJECT_MARKERS_BY_TAM genuinely has no entry for these two)
- `"Mwalimu anapenda kusoma."` -> unchanged (`"Mwalimu wawekunda
  kushoma."`) -- noun-subject path unaffected
- `"Sipendi kusoma."` / `"Hatupendi kusoma."` / `"Hampendi kusoma."` ->
  verb kept as the original Swahili word, with a clear NEGATION-
  DETECTED-BUT-UNSUPPORTED flag, no fabricated Kitaita negation.
- `probe_pipeline_regression.py`: 12/12, both before and after every
  change in this round (four separate checks: PERSON_SM_TABLE+decompose_
  negative_verb, the e2e wiring, and the VERB-veto fix).

**Noticed but NOT investigated further (out of scope today, flagging)**:
`"Walimu wanapenda kusoma."` (plural "teachers") resolved to the exact
same subject marker/output as singular `"Mwalimu..."` -- plural "walimu"
may be falling through to the same lemma/class as "mwalimu" rather than

User: "updated negation. add to pipeline." Pulled the live submissions

exceptions bar two flagged below:

    NEGATIVE = "nde" + [BARE, unshifted subject marker] + root + "-e"
    EXCEPT 1sg: "si" + root + "-e" (no "nde" at all)

before trusting it: (1) final vowel is "-e" not "-a" in every single
row, mirroring Swahili's own negative-present FV shift (-a->-i) with
Kitaita's own vowel; (2) 1sg's "Sikunde" is a clean suppletive
exception, directly paralleling Swahili's own irregular 1sg "si-" --
submitted independently, not assumed; (3) noun-governed rows (3sg
"Mwalimu...", 3pl "Watu...", and all 10 class rows) use the class's own

finding (negation patterns with the future person-marker set, not
present's); (5) 2pl's "ndemukunde" is just future's bare "m" + this
generator's PRE-EXISTING default-linking-vowel mechanism (already used
elsewhere for bare-consonant markers before a consonant-initial root) --
confirms that mechanism generalizes here, not a new rule. One real
anomaly, NOT silently resolved: 'va' class submitted "ndevikunde"
(marker "vi"), not the expected bare "va" every other class matched
exactly -- kept exactly as submitted (trust the speaker over the

## 2026-10-15 (cont. 7): first longer-sentence test finds a real gap -- Kitaita associative concord, now wired

User, testing longer sentences as planned: "we should use agreement
for mayai ya kuku -> maghi gha nguku instead of maghi ya nguku."
Reproduced directly first: `curl`'d "Mayai ya kuku ni mazuri." against
the live webapp -> "Maghi ya nguku ni ghiboie." -- 'mayai'/'maghi'
(verified 'ghi' class) and 'kuku'/'nguku' both translate correctly,
but the associative particle 'ya' passed straight through as literal
Swahili. Checked whether a Kitaita associative-concord mechanism
existed anywhere in this project before building anything new: no.
`nllb_concord_rewrite_pipeline.ASSOC_TABLE` is SWAHILI-side only
(class->Swahili particle, used for the Swahili-internal steering
pipeline); `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.decompose_sentence()` had a detection-
only stub that explicitly said "no Kitaita associative-concord table
exists, kept as-is" -- and `decompose_sentence_with_probes()` (the
DEFAULT path, what the webapp actually uses) had no associative-
particle handling AT ALL, not even that stub.

**Rule, confirmed for one class, applied as a flagged hypothesis
elsewhere**: the Kitaita associative particle for a governing noun's
class equals that SAME class's already-verified PRESENT-TENSE-shifted
subject marker (`PRESENT_SM_VOWEL_CONFIRMED` -- "consonant stays
fixed, vowel becomes 'a'", the exact table already used for verb
agreement throughout this session's person/negation work). This isn't
assumed -- it's a genuine, exact match directly confirmed by the
user's correction: 'ghi' class's present-tense verb marker is 'gha'
(tested this session: "Maghi ghawekunda"/eggs-like), and the
associative answer is ALSO 'gha'. First time that table has been used
for anything but verb agreement, so every OTHER class's answer via
this rule is an unconfirmed extrapolation of the same pattern, tiered
"hypothesis" not "verified" (only 'ghi' is "verified"). Reuses
EXISTING data rather than inventing a new table -- `TAM_SM_ALIAS`-
normalizes first (so 'i_nasal' routes through 'i', same as present-
tense verb agreement already does), then looks up `PRESENT_SM_
VOWEL_CONFIRMED`; returns (None, None) -- flagged, not guessed -- for
the 2 classes with no present-tense data at all ('lu', 'va' -- the
SAME two residual gaps the Subject-markers Word Bank tab from cont. 6
is asking about, a nice coherence check).

**Implementation** (`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`): new `associative_
particle_for_class()` (the rule above) and `apply_associative_concord()`
(scans the WHOLE token sequence for "NOUN1 PARTICLE NOUN2", resolves
the governing noun's Kitaita class via the two ALREADY-EXISTING helpers
`lookup_noun_kitaita()`+`resolve_class_marker()` -- no new noun-class-
resolution logic needed, just composed what already existed -- and
substitutes the particle via the SAME `d.secondary_nouns` placement
mechanism every other independently-substituted word already uses, so
no new assembly/rendering code was needed either). `ASSOC_PARTICLES`
promoted from a local inside `decompose_sentence()` to module level so
both decompose functions can share it. Wired into BOTH `decompose_
sentence()` (now takes a new optional `noun_class_of` parameter, its
one caller `translate_sentence()` updated to supply it from `tables[3]`)
and `decompose_sentence_with_probes()` (already had `noun_class_of`),
called once near the end of each, before the passthrough sweep, and
marks `assigned[i]=True` on a real substitution so a correctly-
translated particle doesn't ALSO land in `d.passthrough` and print a
stale, contradictory "no mechanism" flag alongside the correct answer
(caught this exact contradiction in the first live test, fixed before
calling it done). Also updated the OLD detection-only stub's flag
message in `decompose_sentence()` (which no longer accurately described
what happens to the particle) rather than leaving two different parts
of the code disagreeing about whether a mechanism exists.

**Verified directly** against the restarted local webapp:

## 2026-10-15 (cont. 8): second associative data point + "ni" copula + a real adjective/noun bug found along the way

User: "still not wired in for all classes Upendo wa Mungu -> Lukundo
lwa Mlungu. also 'ni' is the verb to be didn't the probes pick this
up?" Two direct reports, plus a third bug found while investigating
the second.

**1. Second associative data point, 'lu' class**: "upendo wa Mungu"
(God's love) -> "lukundo lwa Mlungu" -- associative particle "lwa".
Important: this does NOT match what cont. 7's present-tense-shift
HYPOTHESIS would have predicted for 'lu' (no data existed there either,
but a naive "consonant stays, vowel becomes a" extrapolation from bare
'lu' would give "la", not "lwa" -- the 'w' glide here parallels 'ku'-
>'kwa' in the SAME present-tense table, not 'ghu'->'gha' which has no
glide). Added `KITAITA_ASSOCIATIVE_VERIFIED = {"ghi":"gha", "lu":"lwa"}`
(kitaita_verified_corrections.py) as a new TIER 1, checked by
`associative_particle_for_class()` BEFORE the present-tense-shift
hypothesis (now tier 2) -- direct data overrides extrapolation whenever
both exist, same priority order as every other VERIFIED_* vs HYPOTHESIS
pair in this project.

**2. "ni" (invariant present-tense copula, "X ni Y" = "X is Y") was
never recognized as a verb at all** -- simply fell to passthrough.
This project already has a verified Kitaita copula mechanism
(`VERIFIED_KUWA_ROOT_COPULA` = "dek", fires whenever `swahili_verb
['root']=='kuw'` and an adjective follows, ZERO TAM always) built for
"kuwa"-based copulas ("alikuwa mzuri" etc.) -- "ni" is a different
lexeme (Swahili's own affirmative-present copula is irregular, with NO
subject agreement of its own, unlike every "kuwa" tense), but fills
the identical semantic slot, so new `decompose_verb_or_copula()`
remaps "ni" onto the SAME root='kuw' mechanism (synthesizes a
`VerbFormEntry(root_guess='kuw', subject_marker=None, ...)`) rather
than building a parallel one -- `decompose_verb()`'s own normal
recognition is tried first for every other token, "ni" is the one
special case. Swapped in at both existing `v = decompose_verb(tok)`
call sites (one per decompose function).

**3. Found while testing #2, a real pre-existing bug, not reported by
the user**: "mazuri" (predicate adjective, root "zuri") was being
silently claimed by the noun_hits loop via a near-noise STATISTICAL
noun-table match (Dice 0.26, n=1 attestation, "ghiboie") before the
adjective_hits loop -- which would have correctly resolved it via the
verified `ZURI_ROOT` concord table ("ghighokie" for 'ghi' class) --
ever got a chance to see it (that loop only looks at tokens not
already `assigned`). Exactly the same bug class this project already
fixed for 'kubwa' (2026-10-09) and 'mnapenda' (cont. 1, this session)
but apparently not generalized to every adjective. Fixed the same way
both prior fixes did: added a "known ADJ_ROOT (with prefix) wins
regardless of statistical noun-table matches" veto to the noun_hits
loop in BOTH decompose functions, checked FIRST, mirroring the
adjective_hits loop's own "known-root check first" principle (now
applied where it actually has an effect).

**Verified directly** against the restarted local webapp:
- "Upendo wa Mungu." -> "Lukundo lwa mlungu." -- exact match.
- "Mayai ya kuku ni mazuri." -> "Maghi gha nguku ghideka ghighokie."
  -- fully resolved end to end: noun+associative (cont. 7) + copula
  (new) + adjective concord correctly linked to its real governing
  noun (new fix), not a spurious noun-table guess. Trace confirms each
  piece: 'maghi' Dice 1.00 verified class 'ghi', copula 'dek' ZERO-TAM
  branch fired correctly, 'zuri' root resolved via ZURI_ROOT keyed to

## 2026-10-15 (cont. 9): correction -- "ni" recognition is NOT probe-based, checked directly

User: "but do the probes identify ni as a verb?" Checked directly
rather than assuming the earlier summary's phrasing was precise enough:
`tag_pos(['Mayai','ya','kuku','ni','mazuri'])` tags "ni" as **OTHER**,
not VERB (Mayai/kuku/mazuri all tag NOUN). `decompose_verb('ni')` (the
real SM+TAM+ROOT+FV morphological parser every other verb goes
through) returns `None` -- correctly, since "ni" is invariant, nothing
to analyze. So cont. 8's `decompose_verb_or_copula()` is a pure
HARD-CODED lexical special case for the literal string "ni", not
probe-driven recognition -- it works only because the verb_hits loop's
POS-tag veto exclusively blocks confident NOUN tags (not "anything
other than VERB"), so "OTHER" passes through unblocked, and the
special case fires regardless of what either probe thinks. This does
NOT generalize to any other copula-like particle automatically -- each
would need its own lexical special case the same way.

What IS genuinely probe-driven: once forced into `verb_hits`, the
SEPARATE relation probe (`identify_relations`, NLLB embeddings)
correctly picked "mayai" as "ni"'s subject on its own merits -- that
part was never in question, just the earlier claim about POS
recognition, now corrected for precision (CLAUDE.md: never claim more
than what was actually checked).

Files: none (no code change -- this was a verification/correction of
the prior entry's claim, not a bug).

## 2026-10-15 (cont. 10): relative marker glued onto the root -- "ninayofanya" -> "mafozi" bug found and fixed

User: "why did we translate ninayofanya to mafozi instead of
naweribonya?" Checked directly: `decompose_verb('ninayofanya')` already
correctly returns `root_guess='yofany'` (the relative marker 'yo' +
the real root 'fany' GLUED TOGETHER) alongside its own `relative_
marker_candidates=[('yo','fanya')]` -- it had already done the hard
part (finding the real split) but nothing downstream ever looked at
that field. `grep`'d the whole pipeline: `relative_marker_candidates`
was computed, carried on `VerbFormEntry`, and then simply never
consulted anywhere -- not threaded into the verb dict passed to
`translate()`, no presence-detection step the way object markers
already have one. So root resolution always used the corrupted
'yofany', which happened to have its OWN plausible-looking fallback
match ("mafozi", Dice 0.33, "high" cross-version confidence) -- not a
guess that went wrong, a real answer (decompose_verb's own candidate)
that was never asked for.

**Fix, mirrors the EXISTING object-marker presence-detection
mechanism, extended where it needed to be**: new `rel_candidates` key
threaded into `clause["verb"]` (decompose_sentence_with_probes);
relative-marker detection block added to `translate_sentence_with_
probes()`, right before the existing object-marker block, comparing
the unstripped root against each (relative-marker, candidate-root)
pair and switching when the candidate has better Dice evidence. One
real wrinkle the object-marker code didn't need to handle: its
existing comparison only checks `root_kitaita` (root-level Dice), but
here BOTH 'yofany' and 'fany' have NO root-level entry at all (only
fallback-table entries) -- a root_kitaita-only comparison would see a
tie (-1.0 vs -1.0) and never switch. New `_root_evidence_score()`
helper checks root_kitaita first, falls back to the whole-surface-form
fallback table's Dice otherwise -- confirmed directly before writing
the fix: 'fany' fallback Dice 0.45 (<-'atafanya') genuinely beats
'yofany' fallback Dice 0.33 (<-'yanayofanya'), so 'fany' wins on real
evidence, not just structural plausibility. Clears `om_candidates`
when a relative-marker switch fires (they were enumerated against the
UNSTRIPPED stem and are stale/potentially wrong once the root changes
-- re-checking for an object marker inside the corrected root is
explicitly out of scope, same deferred question `find_relative_
marker_candidates`'s own docstring already flagged).

**Verified directly** against the restarted local webapp: "Kazi
ninayofanya ni nzuri." -> "Kazi nawechabonya ideka ighokie." -- flag
confirms the switch fired ("unstripped root 'yofany' evidence=0.33 ->
corrected root 'fany' evidence=0.45"), and the corrected root resolves
through this session's OWN cont. 1 derived-fallback-root mechanism to
"chabony", the SAME root family the regression battery's existing
"akifanya"->"...chabonya" case already validates independently -- two
of today's fixes composing correctly together, not coincidence.
`probe_pipeline_regression.py`: 12/12, unchanged.

**Found incidentally, NOT a bug in this fix**: a STANDALONE single-
word sentence "Ninayofanya." (no surrounding context) gets mis-tagged
NOUN by the POS probe, which vetoes it from verb_hits before reaching
any of this -- checked directly: the SAME word in ANY real sentence
context ("Ninayofanya kazi.", "Kazi ninayofanya ni nzuri.", etc.) is
correctly tagged VERB. Sparse/unusual single-token input confusing the
POS probe is an already-accepted, documented tradeoff (CLAUDE.md:
"POS probe's own VERB recall is 91.4%, not perfect"), not something
this session touched.

**Open, same as object markers**: the relative marker 'yo' itself is
still just DROPPED (root fixed, marker not rendered in Kitaita) --
Kitaita relative-marker REWRITE remains unsolved (README/status.md),
unaffected by this fix.

Files: `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (new `_root_evidence_score()`; new
relative-marker presence-detection block in `translate_sentence_
with_probes()`; `rel_candidates` added to the verb dict in `decompose_
sentence_with_probes()`; that function's `tables` unpack now includes
`root_kitaita_fallback`).

User: "I don't agree with relative marker. yo- is the object marker do
we check for object markers or was this missed." Checked directly
rather than re-asserting: `OM_TABLE[9]='i'`, `REL_TABLE[9]='yo'` --

quoted directly from `extract_swahili_grammar.py`'s `REL_TABLE`
comment: "inyayoikabili" = i-na-**yo**-**i**-kabili (REL 'yo' THEN OM
'i', both present, in sequence, for the same class 9) -- proving
they're two distinct morphemes, not the same one. User accepted this
("got it makes sense").

**New report**: "how about hii kazi why didn't we translate it to iri
kazi?" Checked first: zero Kitaita demonstrative-concord mechanism
anywhere in the project (same gap class as associative concord/object
markers/negation before it) -- `nllb_concord_rewrite_pipeline.
DEM_PROXIMAL_TABLE`/`DEM_DISTAL_TABLE` are SWAHILI-side only (old
Swahili-internal steering pipeline), never wired into the free-text
e2e pipeline, not even flagged as missing.

`KITAITA_DEM_DISTAL_VERIFIED = {}` (kitaita_verified_corrections.py,
n=1 trusted like every other VERIFIED_* table -- distal "that" has

`apply_demonstrative_concord()` (kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py), mirroring
`apply_associative_concord()`'s architecture closely but handling the
OPPOSITE adjacency: Swahili demonstratives can precede OR follow their
noun ("hii kazi" / "kazi hii", both grammatical) -- checks the
following token first, then the preceding one. Wired into both
decompose functions at the same insertion point as associative
concord.

**Found and fixed along the way, not reported by the user**: "Hii
kazi" worked immediately, but "Kazi hii" (noun-then-demonstrative)
didn't -- checked directly: the POS probe tags "hii" as ADJ (a
reasonable mix-up, demonstratives modify nouns the way adjectives do).

then won the token's position during assembly (clauses are assembled
BEFORE secondary_nouns, where the demonstrative fix's own output
lives) with no real adjective-concord data for "hii" at all -- silently
blocking the correct "iri" substitution for the exact same token. Fixed
by vetoing any token in the demonstrative closed-set from adjective
candidacy in the first place, same "known closed-set wins over the POS
tag" principle already used earlier this session (ADJ_ROOT vs
noun_hits), just applied in the reverse direction.

**Verified directly** against the restarted local webapp: "Hii kazi ni
nzuri." -> "Iri kazi ideka ighokie."; "Kazi hii ni nzuri." -> "Kazi iri
ideka ighokie." -- both orders now correct. `probe_pipeline_
regression.py`: 12/12, unchanged throughout both fixes.

this session. "nzuri" (seen in testing, a different surface allomorph
of "zuri") was separately noticed NOT resolving via the adjective

## 2026-10-15 (cont. 14): RETRACTION/FIX -- cont. 13's Demonstratives tab broke the whole Word Bank page, no data was lost

User reported "the page has no option to edit/input words" and then,
more alarmingly, "Nouns and adjective roots are both at 0... where is
all the work we had done!" First checked the actual database directly
(`ArtifactData` query on `contributions`) before assuming anything --
**all prior contribution documents are intact** (adj:chafu:*, adj:dogo:*,
etc., all still there with their real submitted values). Nothing was
ever deleted; this was a pure rendering bug from cont. 13's own edit.

**Root cause, found by actually simulating the live script against a
stub DOM in Node (not just `node --check`, which only catches syntax
errors)**: `searchTerms` is a hardcoded object keyed by tab
(`{noun:"", verb:"", ..., subject:""}`) that cont. 13 never added a
`dem:""` entry to when adding the Demonstratives tab to `SECTIONS`.
`renderList()` calls `searchTerms[sec.key].trim()` for every section --
for "dem" this is `undefined.trim()`, a `TypeError`, thrown partway
through the SAME synchronous `render()` call that runs before
`initDb()`. Because the exception propagates out of `render()`,
**`initDb()` on the next line never executes at all** -- the database
connection and its `onSnapshot` subscription are never established, so
every tab's progress count stays frozen at whatever the one
pre-crash, pre-data `render()` pass computed (0 for everything), and
the Demonstratives panel itself never got its rows appended at all
(crashed before reaching them) -- matching BOTH user reports from one
single cause.

**Verified the fix properly, not just re-checked syntax**: ran the
actual script against a minimal stub DOM (`document.createElement`/
`getElementById`/etc.) in Node, confirmed it throws at exactly this
line before the fix; added `dem:""` to `searchTerms`; confirmed the
same harness now runs clean (7/7 tabs and panels built, no throw).
Then went further and simulated a real `window.claude.use("db")` /
`onSnapshot` call with 3 fake-but-realistically-shaped contribution
docs (2 adj, 1 noun) fed through the ACTUAL `applySnapshot` code path
-- confirmed the tab counts correctly update ("Nouns 1/136", "Adjectives
2/89"), proving the full render-&gt;initDb-&gt;snapshot-&gt;applySnapshot-&gt;
re-render cycle works end-to-end, not just that it no longer throws.
This level of check (simulate the actual runtime, not just assume from
reading code) is now the bar for any future edit to this artifact's
script -- `node --check` alone passed on the BROKEN version too.

Republished (same URL, version 10). The live database was never
touched by any of this session's `Artifact.publish` calls -- publishing
a new page version does not affect the artifact's separate `db`
capability data, confirmed directly by querying it before and
concluding it was always intact.

Files: artifact-only (version 10) -- no local Python/pipeline files
changed.

## 2026-10-17: fix -- 5 of the Word Bank's 119 "verb roots" were mis-segmented (OM/reflexive left attached, or a "ku-" infinitive misread as carrying a tense marker)

Direct user correction, 3 examples: "isaidi" (kuisaidia) should be
"saidi" -- the "i" is a class-9 object marker, not part of the root;
"jitawal" (kujitawala) should be "tawal" -- "ji" is the reflexive
object marker; "kukabiliwa" was wrongly split as two entries, "kabiliw"
(correct, from "inakabiliwa") and a separate, wrong "biliw". Confirmed
all three directly against `extract_swahili_grammar.py`'s
`decompose_verb()`, which this Word Bank list is built from.

**Mechanism, 2 distinct bugs, not 1:**
1. `decompose_verb()` enumerates object-marker candidates but, by
   design (OM_TABLE's own docstring: "never for blind unconditional
   stripping"), never strips them from `root_guess` -- so "isaidi"/
   "jitawal"-style roots keep the OM glued on unless a CALLER decides
   to use the candidate. `build_pages.py`'s verb-list builder
   (`build_pooled_noun_verb_lists`) never even reads
   `object_marker_candidates` -- a gap, not an intentional choice.
2. "kukabiliwa"/"kukabiliana"/"kukamatwa"/"kuhusiana" etc.: `ku-`
   (infinitive) is tenseless, but `decompose_verb()`'s TAM-matching
   loop runs unconditionally and will match a TAM string that is
   really just the root's own initial syllable (e.g. "ka" in "kabili-"
   collides with the narrative/consecutive TAM marker "ka") --
   confirmed directly: 254 distinct surface forms in the existing
   corpus dump hit this. The file's own code already special-cases the
   one sub-case where the colliding string is ALSO a legitimate object
   marker ("li"/"ki" -- root recovery is identical either way there);
   it does not special-case the rest.

**Why not a blanket regex fix** -- tested one directly on all 119
entries before touching anything: a naive "strip the one OM candidate
you find" rule mutilates genuine roots that happen to start with an
OM-shaped letter (e.g. "kumaliza" -> wrongly "aliz" instead of
"maliz"; "kuidhinisha" -> wrongly "dhinish"). A naive "ku- is always
tenseless, reject any TAM match" rule is also NOT universally safe:
"kutapunguzwa" could genuinely be a class-15-subject finite verb
(ku-SM + ta-TAM), a different, real construction that's indistinguishable
from the spurious case without sentence context this list doesn't carry.
Swahili doesn't mark this unambiguously in a single isolated surface
form -- this is a real ambiguity, not a parsing gap.

**What actually discriminates (evidence-gated, not assumed):**
cross-checked each candidate root against `page1_vocabulary.json`'s
14,378 other decomposed verb-root entries, restricted to forms whose
final vowel is 'a' (excludes contamination from nouns like "uhusiano"
that `decompose_verb()` mis-parses as verbs with a spurious final-vowel
'o'), requiring the stripped/corrected candidate to be independently
attested across MULTIPLE distinct subject+tense combinations (not a
single occurrence, and not from the same ambiguous-stripping mechanism
applied to itself -- caught "nganishw" this way: its only "evidence"
was the identical operation on the identical word, i.e. no real
corroboration). 5 of 119 cleared this bar:
- `isaidi` -> `saidi` (9x: yamesaidia, walisaidia, unasaidia, ...)
- `jitawal` -> `tawal` (242x: alitawala, anatawala, atatawala, ...)
- `jitayarish` -> `tayarish` (7x, none carrying "ji")
- `matw`+`kamatw` (duplicate entries, same root) -> merged into
  `kamatw`, count 5+5=10
- `biliw`+`kabiliw` (duplicate entries, same root) -> merged into
  `kabiliw`, count 3+18=21

35 more candidates were flagged ambiguous (evidence inconclusive or a
tie, e.g. "zuk" 19 vs 19, "fuatili" 8 vs 8) and deliberately left
UNCHANGED -- native-speaker call, not guessed.

**Scope, deliberately narrow**: fixed only the Word Bank Artifact's
119(->117)-entry verb-root list, via a one-off script, not
`extract_swahili_grammar.py`'s `decompose_verb()` itself.
`decompose_verb()` is relied on by ~15 other scripts (kitaita_
relations.py, mine_ki_candidates.py, validate_ki_*_roundtrip.py,
nllb_concord_rewrite_pipeline.py, ...) for already-exercised,
narrower checks (specific roots like "sem"/"on"/"kuw", `-ki-` governor
detection) that the counter-example above shows could be wrong in new
ways if "ku-always-tenseless" were applied blindly there too -- not
touched this round. `page1_vocabulary.json`/`page3_verb_rules.json`
were NOT regenerated (stale, pre-dates this fix; used here only as a
read-only evidence source via its 14,378 root entries).

Published: **Kitaita Word Bank** Artifact
(https://claude.ai/artifact/6eozxX4HtKZhce3FTfWnY2), now version 12.
Local source `Code_Experiments/kitaita_word_bank_updated.html` kept in
sync (confirmed byte-identical to the live artifact outside the fixed
JSON before publishing).

Files: `Code_Experiments/kitaita_word_bank_updated.html`, Word Bank
Artifact (v12). No changes to `extract_swahili_grammar.py` or any
other pipeline file this round.

## 2026-10-19: feature -- "Taita-fy" verbs/adjectives with no Kitaita root/concord, instead of leaving them as bare untouched Swahili

Direct user request: translations currently read awkwardly because a
verb/adjective with no Kitaita translation was previously kept as its
**original, fully Swahili, uninflected surface form** (e.g. a bare
"anapeleka" sitting inside an otherwise-Kitaita sentence) -- confirmed
directly in `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`'s own docstring (2026-10-09
correction: "in case you miss a word in kitaita use the swahili
word"). User's ask: when the ROOT itself has no Kitaita translation,
keep the Swahili root but still apply correct Kitaita subject-marker +
TAM agreement around it -- e.g. `anapeleka` (Swahili SM+TAM+root) ->
`wawepeleka` (Kitaita SM 'wa-' + Kitaita present '-we-' + Swahili root
'peleka'), not bare Swahili.

**Mechanism**: `kitaita_sentence_generator.translate()`'s verb-root
resolution chain (VERIFIED_ROOTS -> root-level Dice -> derived ->
per-form-fallback) previously ended with `return {"error": ...}` when
NONE of those four tiers had anything. Replaced that error with a new,
explicitly-flagged 5th tier: keep `swahili_verb["root"]` unchanged as
`kit_root`, leave `root_is_full_form=False` (critical -- that flag
means "already real Kitaita, don't re-inflect"; this is the opposite:
"Swahili stem, DO run the normal SM+TAM dispatch below"), and set a
new `root_untranslated=True` flag. Every subject-marker/TAM branch
below (present zero-marking, past re/de allomorphy, narrative -ka-,
future -cha-, glide alternation, linking-vowel insertion) already runs
unconditionally for any non-full-form root, so this one addition is
enough -- no changes needed to the substitution logic itself, only to
what happens when root resolution finds nothing. Same shape applied to
the ADJECTIVE dispatch chain's final `else` (previously just flagged
"no table, not guessed" and dropped the adjective to bare Swahili via
`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.assemble_in_order`'s own fallback) -- new
`adjective_untranslated=True` tier uses `kitaita_adj_prefix(kit_sm)`
(the one existing CROSS-STEM-generalized concord-prefix function) +
the untranslated Swahili stem. Flagged explicitly as a WEAKER, DOUBLE
guess than the verb case in both the trace and the code comment: this
project has already found the concord STRATEGY itself (not just the
stem) is unresolved and inconsistent across the 9 adjectives it has
any data for at all (baya/zuri use the noun's full subject marker +
shared root; kubwa/refu/dogo/geni/fupi/zito/chafu use a different,
reduced prefix series) -- applying the reduced-prefix series to a
totally new stem is not confirmed to be the right strategy, only the
one with an existing cross-stem generalization mechanism to reuse.

Both new flags are returned in `components` (`root_untranslated`,
`adjective_untranslated`) and surfaced into `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`'s
human-readable `d.flags` at both call sites (`translate_sentence`,
`translate_sentence_with_probes`) -- exactly so Stage F testing/
coverage reporting can single out "insufficient vocabulary" sentences
rather than silently mixing them in with real translations, per direct
user acknowledgment this WILL get flagged there and is wanted that way.

**Verified directly** (`build_lookup_tables()` + `translate()`, both
with the real corpus tables and with tables emptied to force the new
branch specifically): `anapeleka` + subject `mwalimu` -> "Mwalimu
wawepeleka." (`root_untranslated=True`) -- the user's own example,
reproduced exactly. Past tense and a no-data adjective case
(`changamfu`, "cheerful") also produced plausible hybrids
("Walimu widepeleka.", "Mwalimu wawepeleka mchangamfu."
`adjective_untranslated=True`). Ran the existing `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`
`__main__` regression block (4 known-structure + 4 novel sentences) end
to end -- no crashes, no change to any sentence that already had a
real Kitaita root (confirmed by construction: the new branch is the
LAST arm of an elif-chain, structurally unreachable unless every prior
tier already failed).

**One finding worth a follow-up decision, NOT acted on this round**:
`Mungu akawona.` -> `Mlungu ukawona.` now goes through the NEW
root_untranslated tier for Swahili root 'won' (the real written form is
the 'w'-glide variant "wona", not "ona" -- this decomposer does not
normalize that Swahili spelling variant to one root string) -- this
happens to still produce the RIGHT answer only because Kitaita's own
verified root also happens to be the string 'won' (see kitaita_
sentence_generator.py's KUWA_PAST_ALTERNATES comment, same coincidence
noted there for 'ona'/'won'). Separately, found that the PRE-EXISTING
per-form-fallback tier (4th in the chain, tried BEFORE the new one)
sometimes wins with very weak evidence (Dice as low as 0.22-0.33 in the
`__main__` regression run) and returns a frozen, UNFLAGGED-as-guess
full surface form instead of ever reaching the new, explicitly-flagged
hybrid -- e.g. 'pelek' hit a Dice-0.33 fallback ("watoteshwa") before
this change existed at all. Whether that weak frozen-form tier should
be reprioritized BELOW the new Taita-fied-hybrid tier (a confidently-
wrong "real word" vs. an honestly-flagged hybrid) is a real, separate
design question -- not changed this round (one change per experiment;
also pre-existing behavior, not introduced by this fix).

Files: `kitaita_sentence_generator.py` (`translate()`: new
`root_untranslated`/`adjective_untranslated` tiers + components
fields), `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (`translate_sentence()`,
`translate_sentence_with_probes()`: surface both flags into
`d.flags`). No Word Bank Artifact change this round (pure pipeline
logic, not the word list).

## 2026-10-19 (cont.): feature -- descriptive/purposive associative concord ("maji ya kunywa" -> "machi ghenywa"), distinct from genitive/possessive

Direct user correction, a NEW rule, structurally different from the
existing genitive/possessive associative concord (KITAITA_ASSOCIATIVE_
VERIFIED, 2026-10-15): Swahili "[noun] -a ku-VERB" (descriptive/
purposive complement -- "water FOR DRINKING") takes a DIFFERENT
particle allomorph than genitive "-a [noun]" ("water OF [someone]") AND
fuses with the verb's ROOT into one word, dropping the infinitive's
"ku-" entirely -- "Maji ya kunywa" -> "Machi ghenywa" (particle 'ghe' +
root 'nywa'), but "Maji ya Bill" (ownership, same noun/particle
string) stays "Machi gha Bill", two separate words, the ordinary
genitive particle 'gha'. User explicit: works for the descriptor
pattern, NOT for ownership -- same noun+particle, different Kitaita
answer depending on what follows.

**New data**: `KITAITA_ASSOCIATIVE_DESCRIPTOR_VERIFIED = {"ghi": "ghe"}`
(kitaita_verified_corrections.py) -- n=1, class 'ghi' only, explicitly
NOT extrapolated to any other class by formula (same discipline as the
existing associative table's 'lu'->'lwa', which also isn't predictable
from the bare marker). Noted but NOT merged: 'ghi'->'ghe' happens to be
the identical string to this class's UNRELATED subject-marker shift
before the existential 'kogh'+'-re-' past construction (KOGH_RE_FRONT_
VOWEL_SHIFTS['ghi'], kitaita_sentence_generator.py) -- flagged as a
possible shared phonological pattern, kept as a separate table until a
speaker confirms they're really the same rule.

**Mechanism**:
1. `resolve_verb_root()` (kitaita_sentence_generator.py, new) -- mirrors
   translate()'s own non-'kuw' root-resolution chain (VERIFIED_ROOTS ->
   root-level Dice -> derived -> per-form-fallback -> Taita-fy/keep-
   Swahili-root), factored out for reuse by a caller with NO subject/SM/
   TAM of its own (same precedent as kitaita_e2e_pipeline.resolve_class_
   marker(), which already does this for the noun side). The per-form-
   fallback tier is explicitly REJECTED by its caller here (not by this
   function) when used for fusion -- it returns an already-inflected
   whole word built around an unrelated subject+TAM, categorically
   incompatible with "particle + bare root + FV"; using it produced a
   garbled real bug caught directly in testing ("Machi ukinywa" instead
   of "Machi ghenywa" for 'nywa', a weak statistical fallback winning
   over the correct Taita-fy tier) before this guard was added.
2. `associative_descriptor_particle_for_class()` / `apply_associative_
   descriptor_concord()` (kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py, new) -- detects
   "PARTICLE ku-VERB" (bare infinitive only, via decompose_verb; the
   "ku-TAM-root" class-15-subject reading is explicitly NOT handled,
   same known, separately-flagged ambiguity noted elsewhere in this
   project) and fuses particle+root+FV into one `secondary_nouns` entry.
3. **Had to run BEFORE the ordinary noun-candidate scan, not just before
   `apply_associative_concord()`** -- found directly in testing: Swahili
   "ku-" is genuinely both the infinitive marker AND the class-15
   deverbal-noun prefix (already documented, `_noun_lookup()`'s own
   docstring), so the pre-existing per-token noun-candidate sweep (now
   lookup-at-any-confidence-level, 2026-10-09) claimed "kunywa" as a
   (wrong) noun candidate before this new, more specific 3-token pattern
   ever got a chance to run. Fixed by moving the call to the TOP of both
   `decompose_sentence()` and `decompose_sentence_with_probes()` (before
   their own noun_hits loops) and adding an `assigned[i]` guard at the
   top of each of those loops -- zero behavior change for any sentence
   that doesn't contain this new pattern (that guard is only ever
   triggered by this new function's own prior claim).
4. `apply_associative_concord()` (the genitive case) gained a matching
   `assigned[i]` guard so it correctly yields the particle index to the
   descriptive-associative function above, exactly when that function
   actually fires (otherwise it is untouched -- genitive sentences with
   a following NOUN, not an infinitive, are completely unaffected).

**Verified directly** (`build_lookup_tables()` + `translate_sentence()`,
real corpus tables): "Maji ya kunywa." -> "Machi ghenywa." (the user's
own example, reproduced exactly, root 'nywa' flagged untranslated/
Taita-fied). "Maji ya Bill." -> "Machi gha Bill." (ownership,
UNCHANGED, confirms the construction only fires on the descriptive
pattern). "Mayai ya kuku." -> "Maghi gha nguku." (pre-existing genitive
regression check, UNCHANGED). "Mtoto ananywa maji ya kunywa." -> "Mwana
ukinywa machi ghenywa." (finite verb + descriptive-associative phrase
in the SAME sentence, both handled independently, no interference).
"Nyumba ya kulala ni kubwa." (class 'i_nasal', no descriptive-
associative data) correctly falls through untouched to the ordinary
genitive/passthrough handling. Ran the existing `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`
`__main__` regression block (8 sentences, none containing this pattern)
end to end -- byte-identical output to before this change.

**Not verified**: `decompose_sentence_with_probes()`'s copy of this same
fix (mirrors the non-probes version exactly, including its own
`assigned[i]` guard) could only be checked by static/syntax inspection
in this session -- it requires a loaded NLLB model + trained probes,
neither available here; needs a real run before trusting the probes
path specifically.

Files: `kitaita_verified_corrections.py` (new table), `kitaita_sentence_
generator.py` (new `resolve_verb_root()`), `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`
(new `associative_descriptor_particle_for_class()`/`apply_associative_
descriptor_concord()`, call-order fixes in both `decompose_sentence()`
and `decompose_sentence_with_probes()`, matching guard added to
`apply_associative_concord()`).

## 2026-10-20: 4 more classes for descriptive-associative concord + 4 new root translations + a real root-segmentation bug found and fixed

Direct user examples, extending 2026-10-19's "maji ya kunywa" ->
"machi ghenywa" descriptive-associative construction to 4 more
classes:
  "mti wa kuchoma" -> "mudi ghokora" (firewood)
  "ulimi wa kuongea" -> "lumi loghora"
  "mbwa wa kulinda" -> "koshi elindia"
  "mtu wa kucheka" -> "mundu oseka"
  "miti ya kuchoma" -> "midi ekora" (plural of the 1st -- same particle
    class-key AND same root as "mbwa"/"mti" respectively, confirming
    root translation generalizes across classes while only the
    agreement prefix differs, as the architecture already assumes).

**New data**:
- `VERIFIED_ROOTS` += `chom->kor` (burn), `onge->ghor` (talk),
  `lind->lindi` (guard), `chek->sek` (laugh, ch/s correspondence,
  consistent with proto-Bantu *-sek- "laugh").
- `KITAITA_ASSOCIATIVE_DESCRIPTOR_VERIFIED` += `gh->gho, lu->lo, i->e,
  u->o`. Keys are the ACTUAL runtime value `resolve_class_marker()`
  returns for these specific Kitaita nouns, checked directly against
  this project's tables before finalizing -- NOT the canonical class
  name a human would reach for from memory. Found directly: "mudi"
  (mti/tree) has no `VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS` entry, so it falls
  through to the RAW, un-aliased `noun_class_of` induction, whose own
  "subject_marker" field is the bare string 'gh', not the full
  canonical 'ghu' -- keying by 'ghu' would have silently never matched
  at runtime. Also found: "koshi" (mbwa/dog, VERIFIED override) and
  "midi" (miti/trees, raw fallback) both resolve to the SAME bare
  string 'i' despite being unrelated nouns -- flagged as possibly
  coincidental, not assumed to mean they're the same concord class, same
  discipline as the existing i/i_nasal adjective split (a different
  class pair sharing a subject marker).

**Real bug found and fixed while verifying "mbwa wa kulinda" by hand**:
the previous version of `apply_associative_descriptor_concord()`
validated the infinitive via `extract_swahili_grammar.decompose_verb()`,
which wrongly matched "li" as the past-TAM marker inside "kulinda" (ku-
+li+nd+a instead of ku+lind+a) -- the SAME root-vs-TAM-prefix-collision
bug class as 2026-10-19's "ka" inside "kabili-" fix, but for a marker
('li') that ALSO happens to be a legitimate class-5 object marker
elsewhere (kulifuatilia, kulipitisha), which is exactly why that
earlier fix's "reject any TAM match not also a plausible OM" rule
didn't catch this one: the OM reading isn't always right either, this
project just hadn't hit a counter-example before. Fixed NOT by
patching decompose_verb() (shared, used by ~15 other scripts, out of
scope this round) but by removing the dependency entirely for this one
function: the "particle + ku-VERB" syntactic position can ONLY be the
bare infinitive reading (no class-15-subject ambiguity is possible
there at all, unlike running text), so the fix just strips "ku-" and
the final vowel directly rather than calling the general-purpose,
TAM-sensitive decomposer.

**Open finding, NOT fixed this round**: the same "li"/"ki" collision
bug very likely also affects the MAIN verb path (`translate()`/
`decompose_verb()`) for any OTHER "ku-[li|ki]-initial-root" word used
as a bare infinitive outside this construction (e.g. a hypothetical
"Nataka kulinda" would hit the exact same wrong root 'nd') --
2026-10-19's Taita-fy fix only rejected TAM matches that are NOT also a
plausible object marker; this confirms that "IS also a plausible OM"
is not a safe proxy for "is actually correct" in general. Flagged for
a future, separately-scoped fix to `extract_swahili_grammar.
decompose_verb()` or its callers -- not attempted here (one change per
experiment; broad blast radius, ~15 dependent scripts, needs its own
verification pass).

**Verified directly**: all 5 new sentences + the 2 from 2026-10-19
reproduce exactly via `translate_sentence()` against the real corpus
tables. Re-ran the `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` `__main__` regression
block (8 sentences) -- byte-identical output to before this change.

Files: `kitaita_verified_corrections.py` (4 new VERIFIED_ROOTS entries,
4 new KITAITA_ASSOCIATIVE_DESCRIPTOR_VERIFIED entries),
`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (`apply_associative_descriptor_concord()`:
replaced decompose_verb()-based infinitive validation with direct
"ku-"+final-vowel stripping).

## 2026-10-20 (cont.): reverse-inference pilot -- using known Swahili<->Kitaita correspondences + concord-stripping to recover a few unknown Kitaita roots directly from the parallel Bible corpus

Direct user request: pick a few verses with a Swahili word this
project has NO Kitaita translation for, strip concord markers from
both sides down to bare roots using the rules this project already
has, and see whether the leftover Kitaita material converges on a
likely translation. Ran against the FULL parallel corpus
(`bible collection/data/parallel_full_suv/parallel.jsonl`, 31,102
verse pairs -- bigger and not previously used by this project's
alignment tooling, which so far only ran on the older, Genesis-only
1,533-pair `parallel/parallel.jsonl`).

**Method**: `extract_swahili_grammar.decompose_verb()` (Swahili side)
+ `kitaita_tam_allomorphy.decompose_kitaita_verb()` (Kitaita side,
already-existing SM+TAM-stripping for Kitaita, built from
`KITAITA_TAM_VARIANTS` + the SM-prefix set reused from
`VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS.values()` -- same technique `extract_
adjective_concord_tables.py`'s `KNOWN_KITAITA_SM` already uses,
extended not forked). Picked target gap words from the Word Bank's own
already-flagged "no Kitaita candidate" verb-root list, searched the
full corpus for short verses containing them, and read the aligned
Kitaita verse directly.

**Result 1 -- clean, strong (n=6+ independent formulaic verses):**
Swahili root "saidi" (help) <-> Kitaita root "tesi" (ku+tesi+a =
"kutesia"). Directly visible across PSA.22.19/35.2/38.22/40.13/70.1/
71.12 -- all near-identical "help me" prayers on BOTH sides
("kunisaidia"/"unisaidie" <-> "kunitesie"/"kunitesia"), plus the NOUN
form "msaidizi" (helper) <-> "mtesia" independently confirming the same
root in a DIFFERENT grammatical category (PSA.22.11, PSA.30.10,
PSA.72.12). 82 total Swahili "saidi"-containing tokens found project-
wide. **Caveat, found directly**: a crude verse-level Dice score over
ALL "saidi" vs "tesi" occurrences (mirroring `align_roots()`'s own
method) came out misleadingly LOW (0.049, 65 vs 16 vs only 2 co-
occurring verses) -- NOT because the correspondence is weak, but
because `decompose_kitaita_verb()` has NO Kitaita object-marker table
at all (unlike the Swahili side) and so fails to strip Kitaita "ni-"/
"ku-"/etc. object infixes, undercounting true "tesi" root occurrences
(e.g. "kunitesie" decomposes to root_guess "nitesi", not "tesi"). The
clean result above came from reading the clearest, most formulaic
verses directly, NOT from trusting that automated score -- a concrete
demonstration of why this project's own rule ("check directly, don't
assume a metric covers what it claims") matters even for this
project's OWN tooling, not just borrowed models/corpora.

**Result 2 -- idiomatic, not a single root (n=3 independent verses):**
Swahili root "tawal" (rule) does NOT map to one Kitaita root at all --
EXO.15.18, PSA.22.28, and PSA.106.41 all consistently render "tawala"
(rule) as the Kitaita VERB PHRASE "bonya nguma" (lit. "do/exercise
power/strength"), including correctly inflected for voice (PSA.106.41
"wakawatawala" (active, they ruled them) -> "wikabonyerwa nguma..."
(passive, "were done-power-to")). A genuine negative result: this
project's "isaidi"/"jitawal" root-segmentation fix (2026-10-17) and
last session's Word Bank evidence already correctly isolated the
Swahili root "tawal", but this method shows there is NO single Kitaita
ROOT to assign it to for the Word Bank's verb-roots tab -- it is a
periphrastic construction, flagged as such rather than forced into a
single-word answer.

**Result 3 -- partially resolved, 2 candidates not yet disambiguated
(n=4 verses):** Swahili root "kusudi" (intend/purpose) consistently
co-occurs with Kitaita "njama" (plot/scheme) and/or "mipango" (plans)
across PSA.33.10, JOB.5.12, PRO.15.22, PRO.16.30 -- narrowed from
"completely unknown" to "one of these two near-synonyms", not fully
resolved (the 2 Kitaita words appear together in some of these verses,
so which one specifically glosses "kusudi" itself, versus just being
adjacent vocabulary in the same verse, isn't separable from this small
a sample).

**Not added to any VERIFIED_* table this round** -- these are corpus-
inferred HYPOTHESES (the "aligned"/"statistical" confidence tier this
project's own `extract_kitaita_grammar.py` docstring already defines),
not native-speaker-submitted ground truth; merging them into
VERIFIED_ROOTS would misrepresent their provenance. Logged here as a
ranked candidate list for native-speaker confirmation, per that same
docstring's own stated purpose ("hand a native speaker a ranked,
confidence-tagged list of candidates to check").

Files: none changed (investigation only, no code/data edits this
round) -- all queries run as one-off scripts against existing project
tooling (`extract_swahili_grammar.decompose_verb`, `kitaita_tam_
allomorphy.decompose_kitaita_verb`) and the full parallel corpus.

## 2026-10-20 (cont. 2): MVP push -- confirmed 2 of 3 reverse-inference roots into VERIFIED_ROOTS, retracted 2, mined Kitaita person object markers, published hypotheses to the Word Bank for speaker review

Direct user instruction: the 3 reverse-inference candidates from
earlier today are confirmed correct ("all the translations are
correct") -- add them to the tables now rather than keep hand-editing;
natural next step is the Kitaita object-marker gap this session's own
Dice-score investigation already surfaced.

**Added to VERIFIED_ROOTS** (re-verified by closer reading before
adding, not taken on faith from the earlier quick pass -- 2 of
the original 3 did NOT survive this check, see RETRACTED below):
- `saidi` -> `tesi` (help). Unaffected by the closer re-read -- still
  clean, n=6+ formulaic "help me" verses + the independent noun-form
  cross-check (msaidizi<->mtesia).
- `fany` -> `bony` (do/make). NOT one of the 3 originally reported --
  found as a side effect of explaining "tawala" below, independently
  confirmed directly against 8 of 116 corpus occurrences before adding
  (even stronger evidence than "saidi").

**RETRACTED, not added** (closer re-read of the SAME verses used for
today's earlier report found they don't actually hold up):
- `tawal` (rule) -- genuinely NOT a single root; it is the Kitaita

- `kusudi` (purpose) -- this morning's "narrowed to njama/mipango" does

  -- into 1 Kitaita clause). Same idiomatic-dissolution pattern as
  "tawal", not a real 2-candidate narrowing. Explicit RETRACTION of

**Kitaita object markers (person), corpus-inferred HYPOTHESIS, NOT
speaker-verified** -- "natural next step" per direct user request,
and the exact gap this session's own Dice-score sanity check surfaced
(decompose_kitaita_verb() has no object-marker table at all). Mined by

'saidi' and reading off what sits between SM/TAM and 'tesi' in the
matching Kitaita verse:
- 1sg "me" -> 'ni' (n=7, zero exceptions, identical to Swahili's own).
- 1pl "us" -> 'di' (n=3, zero exceptions, DIFFERENT from Swahili's

## 2026-10-20 (cont. 3): reverse inference at full-corpus scale -- 2 new confirmed roots, object-marker evidence strengthened, and a 1-in-4 manual-verification survival rate that matters more than any single finding

Direct user request: run the reverse-inference method across ALL
verses (31,102 pairs), not just hand-picked ones.

**Tooling fix, reused rather than forked**: extended `kitaita_tam_
allomorphy.decompose_kitaita_verb()` with an optional `om_candidates`
parameter (and threaded it through `extract_root_sets()`) -- backward-
compatible, every existing caller omitting it is unaffected. Ran with
the 3 person markers found this morning (ni/di/wi), directly fixing
the undercounting bug that same morning's sanity check caught.

**Method**: root-level Dice alignment (`align_roots()`'s own method)
across all 31,102 verses, restricted to this project's CURRENT verb-
root gap list (Word Bank). 35/115 gaps got some candidate.

**First finding, before even reading a single verse**: 12 of the 115
listed gaps were STALE -- already resolved in `VERIFIED_ROOTS` since
the 2026-10-12 Word Bank batch, never removed from the live page
(ahid, eleke, fiki, fuati, ish, maliz, ongoz, reje, taraji, tarajiw,
wasil, zungumzi). This is a housekeeping gap, not a research finding,
but it means every past session's "how many gaps are left" count has
been overstated by at least 12 for over a week.

**Manually read the verses for every remaining candidate with
cooccur>=3** (same discipline as this morning's 'kusudi' retraction --
the automated score alone is not trusted). Survival rate: 2 confirmed
clean out of 8 checked closely.

CONFIRMED, added to VERIFIED_ROOTS:
- `oko` (save/rescue) -> `kir`. 3/3 directly confirmed (PSA.80.2,
  PSA.118.25, MAT.14.30). Checked it isn't a generic/overloaded root
  first: only 1 other Swahili root project-wide ever ranks 'kir' as
  its #1 candidate. BONUS: independently reconfirms BOTH person object
  markers from this morning on a SECOND, unrelated root -- 1sg 'ni'
  and 1pl 'di' now each have 2 independent roots agreeing (n bumped to
  8/4 in KITAITA_PERSON_OBJECT_MARKER_HYPOTHESIS).
- `ondo` (remove, TRANSITIVE sense only) -> `inj`. Confirmed via PRO.
  25.4. Checked directly that this is NOT conflated with "ondoka"
  (arise) -- that's a genuinely different Swahili root string
  ('ondok', not 'ondo'), already kept separate by the decomposer; same
  class of polysemy as this project's already-documented 'kuwa'
  existential/copula split.

REJECTED after reading the actual verses (kept in kitaita_verified_
corrections.py as an explicit retraction list, not silently dropped):
- `hesab` -> `tal` (Dice 0.265, cooccur 18) -- 'tal' turned out to be
  the NOUN "mtalo" misread as a verb (decompose_kitaita_verb()'s SM-
  prefix list doesn't distinguish "this is a noun" from "this is a
  verb" -- a real, generalizable contamination risk this run exposed,
  not specific to this one word).
- `agiz` -> `laghir` (Dice 0.176, cooccur 23) -- neither of the 2
  verses read shows 'laghir' at all; likely contamination from 'ahid'
  (promise), which already, correctly, uses that root.
- `tegeme` -> `kusaghik` (Dice 0.196, cooccur 5) -- the 2 verses read
  give 2 DIFFERENT, inconsistent renderings.
- `shuhudi` -> `shuhudi` (Dice 0.272) -- didn't actually appear in any
  of the 4 verses read; the real pattern there ("shuhuda"<->"memu",
  4/4 clean) is a NOUN sense, not this verb-root gap.
- `himiz` -> `shashir` -- zero example verses found at all; flagged as
  literally untested, not merely rejected.
One lead flagged as promising but NOT added (1 clean example only,
below this project's own bar even with corpus support implied by the
score): `peleke` (send) -> `dumi` (ACT.10.5, "peleka watu Yafa" ->
"duma wandu Jopa").

**The real takeaway**: filtering by cooccurrence count (>=3) and a
reasonable Dice threshold still let 6 of 8 candidates through that
don't survive direct reading. Scaling this method's OUTPUT without
also scaling the manual-verification step would have added several
wrong entries to VERIFIED_ROOTS. The bottleneck is the reading, not
the alignment math -- worth remembering before running this again on
nouns or at a larger scale.

**Not attempted this round**: a noun-level pass (136 Word Bank noun
gaps) -- same method would apply (whole-word Dice alignment, this
project's own `extract_kitaita_grammar.best_alignment` already does
exactly this), but wasn't run given the verification bottleneck above;
flagged as the natural next scale-up, not done blind.

**Published**: Kitaita Word Bank Artifact, now version 14 -- removed
all 14 now-resolved verb-root entries (12 stale + oko + ondo) from the
live list; 115 -> 101 remaining.

Files: `kitaita_tam_allomorphy.py` (`decompose_kitaita_verb()`/
`extract_root_sets()`: new optional `om_candidates` parameter),
`kitaita_verified_corrections.py` (2 new VERIFIED_ROOTS entries,
updated object-marker hypothesis n-counts, explicit rejection-list
comment), Word Bank Artifact (v14).

## 2026-10-20 (cont. 4): same reverse-inference pass on the noun gaps -- 58/136 were stale, 54/78 genuinely unresolvable from this corpus, 5 new confirmed, 1 flagged part-of-speech mismatch

Direct user request: run the same pass on the noun gaps.

**Housekeeping finding, bigger than the verb-roots one**: 58 of 136
listed noun gaps were ALREADY resolved (VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS or
the statistical noun_kitaita table), e.g. "mtoto"->"mwana" -- 43%
stale vs. the verb-roots list's 12%. Noun-list cleanup had apparently
never been done at all until now.

**Of the 78 genuinely-unresolved gaps, 54 do not occur even once in
this corpus** -- "mfundi"/"mhandisi"/"mwanamuziki" and most modern
occupational/technical nouns are simply absent from a Bible
translation. No amount of alignment effort can resolve these from this
source; they need a speaker or a different corpus, not more compute.

**Of the 24 that do occur, read the verses for the ones with decent
support (same discipline as the verb-root pass) -- 5 confirmed, added
to VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS:**
- `habari` (news/report) -> `malagho`. 3/4 direct matches.
- `kipande` (piece) -> `kibelele`. Confirmed via LUK.24.42, reinforced
  by "kibelele"/"vibelele" independently meaning "piece/unit" elsewhere
  (LEV.27.4, shekel units).
- `vyakula` (foods, plural) -> `vindo`. Confirmed directly (3/4) rather
  than assumed from the already-known singular "chakula"->"vindo".
- `kipimo` (measure) -> `kipimo`. WEAKER -- only 1/3 verses read shows
  this directly (shared loanword, same tier as this project's existing
  "ish"->"ish"); the other 2 paraphrase rather than contradict.
- `kusikia` (hearing, class-15 infinitive-as-noun) -> `kusikira`.
  Confirmed via the recurring "kusikia habari" (hear news) collocation,
  3/3 clean -- same underlying root also added to VERIFIED_ROOTS as
  `siki`->`sikir` for finite verb forms (noun and verb go through
  separate lookup tables in this pipeline, so both needed updating).

**Rejected or left untested** (logged, not silently dropped): `kilele`/
`vilele` (peak) -- the automated top candidate 'pisga' is almost
certainly the place name Pisgah, not "peak"; `pomboo` (dolphin) -- top
candidate's higher-cooccurrence runner-up ('mrongo'="tens") is clearly
a spurious number-word coincidence from long enumeration lists; `kina`/
`waokozi` -- zero example verses found, untested rather than rejected.

**One genuine part-of-speech mismatch, flagged rather than forced into
the table**: `ukame` (drought, an abstract NOUN in Swahili) only
aligns with `jiomie`, which in its one example (EZK.19.13) is used
STATIVELY/ADJECTIVALLY ("land THAT-IS-DRY"), not as a free-standing
noun Kitaita would use the way Swahili uses "ukame" as a subject or
object. Possibly a real typological gap (Kitaita may express this via
a relative clause rather than an abstraction) -- NOT added to
VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS, since doing so risks `translate()`
inserting an adjective form wherever a noun is expected.

**Published**: Kitaita Word Bank Artifact, now version 15 -- removed
all 63 now-resolved noun entries (58 stale + 5 newly confirmed);
136 -> 73 remaining.

Files: `kitaita_verified_corrections.py` (5 new VERIFIED_NOUN_
TRANSLATIONS entries, 1 new VERIFIED_ROOTS entry, rejection/flag
comments), Word Bank Artifact (v15).

## 2026-10-20 (cont. 5): default per-class Kitaita subject marker for sentences with NO identifiable noun -- "Kile kinachonisikitisha" style headless subjects

Direct user request: add a default noun-class mapping (computed as the
MODE across known correspondences) for sentences where the subject/
object noun is unknown or absent entirely, using "kile kinachonisikitisha"
(that which saddens me) as the motivating example -- no concrete noun
anywhere, only a class-7 demonstrative + a class-7 relative marker on
the verb.

**Computed the mode directly from this project's own data** (every
lexicon noun with a known Swahili class AND a known Kitaita
translation, grouped by Swahili class, same "check for a hidden
exception cluster before trusting the mode" discipline the existing
ANIMATE-SG default already uses): generalized `SWAHILI_CLASS_DEFAULT_
SM_GUESS` (kitaita_verified_corrections.py) from its previous 2 entries
(ANIMATE-SG/PL only) to 9 -- added 15->ku (100%, n=17), 7->chi (80%,
n=15), 8->va (82%, n=17), 6->ghi (82%, n=22), 3->ghu (62%, n=21),
4->i (60%, n=15), 5->ji (53%, n=17, weakest included tier). EXCLUDED
2 classes after checking, not guessed anyway: class 11 (u/ghu nearly
tied, 9 vs 7 of 23 -- no real mode) and class 9/10 (scattered across 7+
Kitaita classes, no usable majority).

**New mechanism for the headless case** (kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py):
`REL_MARKER_TO_SWAHILI_CLASS` (which Swahili class(es) a relative-
marker string like "-cho-"/"-vyo-"/"-ye-" can imply) + `resolve_
headless_subject_class()`, which only resolves when a relative marker's
candidate class(es) agree on ONE default Kitaita SM -- several REL_
TABLE strings are genuinely ambiguous ("-o-" is class ANIMATE-PL/3/11
all at once; "-yo-" is 4/6/9) and these correctly resolve to nothing
rather than guessing (confirmed directly: "inayonisikitisha" still
refuses to translate, exactly as before). `translate_sentence()` tries
this BEFORE its existing "no subject -> refuse" guard, and once
resolved, strips the matching relative marker directly (grammatically
motivated by the class resolution itself, not a Dice-evidence
comparison -- the existing evidence-based relative-marker correction
in translate_sentence_with_probes() was checked and is the WRONG tool
for this specific case: a rare/uncommon root and its marker-
contaminated version are both equally likely to have ZERO Dice
evidence either way, a tie that heuristic correctly never breaks, so
it would have left "kinachonisikitisha" stuck at the contaminated root
'chonisikitish' -- confirmed this directly before writing the
alternative path) and re-checks for a now-exposed object marker using
the existing single-unambiguous-candidate heuristic (2026-10-19).

**Verified directly**: "Kile kinachonisikitisha." -> "Kile
chawesikitisha." (previously: outright refusal, "NO NOUN found... 
cannot proceed"). Root cleanly corrected from the contaminated
'chonisikitish' down to 'sikitish' (still untranslated vocabulary,
correctly Taita-fied rather than claimed). Also confirmed the other
unambiguous relative markers resolve correctly ("vyo"/class 8 ->
"Vile vawesikitisha."; "ye"/ANIMATE-SG -> "Wawesikitisha.") and the
ambiguous ones correctly do NOT ("yo" -> still refuses). Re-ran the
existing `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` `__main__` regression block --
byte-identical output to before this change (none of those sentences
hit this new path, confirming it only activates for the genuinely
headless case it was built for).

**Side effect, intended, not yet separately stress-tested**: the 7 new
`SWAHILI_CLASS_DEFAULT_SM_GUESS` entries also widen the EXISTING per-
lemma fallback (an untranslated noun whose Swahili class IS known) --
previously only ANIMATE-SG/PL nouns got a default SM instead of a hard
refusal when untranslated; now classes 3/4/5/6/7/8/15 do too. This is
the natural, intended extension of the same mechanism, not a separate
change, but wasn't independently tested against more example sentences
this round.

Files: `kitaita_verified_corrections.py` (`SWAHILI_CLASS_DEFAULT_SM_
GUESS`: 7 new entries), `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (new `REL_MARKER_TO_
SWAHILI_CLASS`, `resolve_headless_subject_class()`; `decompose_
sentence()`: `d.verb` now also captures `rel_candidates`/`om_
candidates`; `translate_sentence()`: tries the headless-class
resolution before the no-subject refusal guard, passes `subject_
class` through to `translate()`).

## 2026-10-20 (cont. 6): periphrastic-verb mechanism -- "tawala" (rule) now translates as "bonya nguma" instead of being Taita-fied, and "mamlaka"->"nguma" confirmed overwhelmingly

Direct user request: before falling back to the Taita-fy tier, try
rewriting the sentence without the missing word first, using "tawala
-> fanya mamlaka -> bonyera ngao" as the recalled example. Checked
directly rather than taken on faith (small corrections below), then
built the actual mechanism.

**Correcting the recalled example, with evidence**: "ngao" doesn't
hold up -- searched the corpus directly; the real word is "nguma"
(already found 2 sessions ago: "tawal"->"bonya nguma"). "mamlaka"
(authority), checked for the FIRST time this session, turned out to
be an OVERWHELMING match: 40+ clean verses across Daniel, Luke,
Romans, Ephesians, Colossians, Revelation -- "mwenye mamlaka"<->
"wibonyagha nguma"/"uko na nguma", "mamlaka yangu/yako/yake"<->"nguma
yangu/yako/yake", near-1:1 throughout. Added to VERIFIED_NOUN_
TRANSLATIONS. One real mistake caught and fixed mid-session: an
initial single-verse read (DAN.11.3) misattributed "ndighi" (strength)
to "mamlaka" -- "ndighi" there actually glosses a SEPARATE word in the
same sentence ("hodari"/mighty, describing the king), not "mamlaka" at
all. Only caught once the FULL 40+-verse set was read, not from that
one verse -- the exact "check before trusting a single match" lesson
this project keeps re-learning, now with another concrete instance.

This means "tawala" = "fanya mamlaka" (do authority) is a genuine
COMPOSITIONAL Swahili paraphrase, not an opaque idiom someone made up
to patch a gap: both halves are independently, strongly confirmed
elsewhere in this project ('fany'->'bony', 2026-10-20 earlier;
'mamlaka'->'nguma', just confirmed) -- the "bonya nguma" finding from
2 sessions ago is exactly what that paraphrase predicts.

**New mechanism**: `VERIFIED_IDIOMS` (kitaita_verified_corrections.py)
-- {Swahili root: {Kitaita root, fixed Kitaita object noun, note}},
currently just `tawal` -> (`bony`, `nguma`). Consulted by `translate()`
(kitaita_sentence_generator.py) as a NEW tier, checked right after
VERIFIED_ROOTS (same hand-confirmed trust tier) and BEFORE the
statistical root_kitaita/derived/fallback tiers and the Taita-fy
fallback -- "before using Taita-fied Swahili words" literally. The
object noun is appended after the fully-inflected verb, never fused
or re-inflected itself.

**A real ordering bug caught before it could matter**: root_kitaita_
derived already had its OWN statistical candidate for 'tawal' --
'bony', found independently via 2 fallback-form alignments (a
reassuring cross-confirmation of the same root!) -- but with NO fixed
object attached. Checked directly: if the new idiom tier had been
placed BELOW that statistical tier (the "natural" place in a chain
ordered VERIFIED -> Dice -> derived -> idiom -> fallback -> Taita-fy),
the statistical tier would have fired FIRST and silently dropped
'nguma' -- "Mfalme anatawala" would have come out as the incomplete
"Mzuri anabonya" ("he DOES", not "he RULES"). Fixed by placing the
idiom check ahead of the statistical tiers, not behind them.

**Verified directly**: "Mfalme anatawala." -> "Mzuri wawebonya
nguma."; "Mfalme alitawala nchi." -> "Mzuri udebonya nguma isanga."
(object noun "isanga" correctly follows the appended "nguma", natural
word order). No changes needed to kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py's sentence-
assembly logic at all -- the idiom's extra word is folded directly
into `components['kitaita_verb_word']` as one string with an internal
space, which the existing word-at-a-token-position assembly already
handles correctly with zero special-casing. Re-ran the `kitaita_e2e_
pipeline.py` `__main__` regression block -- byte-identical output
(none of those sentences use 'tawal').

**Scope limit, flagged not silently assumed**: only matches the PLAIN
root string 'tawal' (kutawala/anatawala/atatawala etc.). The
applicative ('tawalia') and passive ('tawaliwa') extensions decompose
to a different root string entirely in this project's one-final-vowel
model and are NOT covered -- a known gap, not assumed to also work.

**Published**: Kitaita Word Bank Artifact, now version 16 -- removed
'tawal' from the verb-roots list (now resolved via the idiom
mechanism, not just Taita-fied); 101 -> 100 remaining.

Files: `kitaita_verified_corrections.py` (new `VERIFIED_IDIOMS` table,
1 new VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS entry, updated 'tawal' comment),
`kitaita_sentence_generator.py` (`translate()`: new periphrasis tier
in the root-resolution chain, `idiom_object` threaded into `kit_verb`/
`components`), Word Bank Artifact (v16).
