`HF_TOKEN` secret -- first attempt still failed (token existed as a
Space secret but wasn't a real token in the owner's account -- likely
a copy/paste or create/delete-before-save mismatch), second attempt
(a classic "Write"-role token, after the fine-grained scoping UI gave
the owner trouble) succeeded. A real submission reached the dataset;
confirmed via `list_repo_files` and cleaned up the test record.

**Bug report, direct user test via the Space**: "Basi Hezekia
akajigeuza, akaelekeza uso wake ukutani, akamwomba BWANA akasema,"
(2 Kings 20:2) -- every verb kept its Swahili subject marker ('a-')
instead of converting to Kitaita, AND "akasema" (say) didn't use the
root-level statistical candidate this project already has for 'sem'
('ghamb', Dice 0.27, 1030 shared verses -- substantial, pre-existing
evidence, not something missing).

**Root cause, confirmed directly by instrumenting the live Space's
API**: "Hezekia" is a Biblical proper name, not in any noun table --
so it was never even a NOUN CANDIDATE for the trained nsubj probe to
begin with, let alone a winning one. Every one of the 4 verbs in this
coordinated clause chain got "no noun won as nsubj against every
competitor", meaning `translate()` was never called for ANY of
them -- not that the 'sem'->'ghamb' candidate was ignored, but that
the whole clause never reached the code that would have used it.

**Fix**: `find_fallback_proper_name_subject()` (kitaita_e2e_
pipeline.py) -- when no noun wins nsubj for a clause (and it's not a
recognized person-prefix or negation), scan backward from the verb for
the nearest token that is (a) not the sentence's first word (sentence-
initial capitals say nothing -- "Basi" here is a discourse particle),
(b) capitalized in the ORIGINAL, pre-lowercased text, and (c) not
already claimed as some OTHER clause's subject/object. If found,
default to this project's EXISTING class-1/ANIMATE-SG subject-marker
default (SWAHILI_CLASS_DEFAULT_SM_GUESS, 2026-10-20 earlier) -- a
near-universal grammatical fact for Swahili (ANY human proper name
takes class-1 verb agreement), not a statistical guess like most of
this project's other defaults. Wired into BOTH places a clause can end
up subjectless (the single-verb "NO NOUN found at all" branch and the
per-clause loop's "no noun won nsubj" branch) and into the loop guard
that previously skipped calling `translate()` entirely whenever
`subject_idx`/`person` were both None (now also checks `subject_class`).

**A second, real bug this surfaced and fixed in the same pass**: a
naive "re-scan fresh for every clause" version of this fix picked the
WRONG name for the last clause ("BWANA" instead of "Hezekia") --
because the nsubj/obj probe itself mis-assigned "akamwomba"'s object
(picked 'uso' again instead of 'BWANA', a separate, pre-existing probe-
accuracy issue, not this fix's to solve), leaving "BWANA" un-claimed
and therefore nearer and available to a fresh scan. Fixed by having the
fallback subject, once found for ONE clause, persist across the REST
of that sentence's clause chain (a Swahili "-ka-" narrative chain's
subject is established once and carries over, exactly how this project
already understands the construction) rather than re-scanning fresh
each time -- confirmed directly, re-tested against the live Space,
all 4 verbs now correctly resolve to "Hezekia" and all convert to
Kitaita class-1 agreement ("ukawawichea"/"ukawifumira"/"ukaamneka"/
"ukaghamba"), with 'akasema' correctly using 'ghamb'.

Pushed to the Space twice in this round (the initial fix, then the
chain-persistence correction) -- verified against the LIVE API both
times, not assumed from local testing, since the heuristic (non-probes)
path can't exercise this bug at all (it only ever processes one verb
per sentence, a separate, pre-existing, documented limitation not
touched this round).

Files: `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` / `hf_space/kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`
(new `find_fallback_proper_name_subject()`, wired into `decompose_
sentence_with_probes()` at both subjectless branches and into
`translate_sentence_with_probes()`'s clause-skip guard; `chain_
subject_idx` tracking across the per-sentence clause loop).

## 2026-10-20 (cont. 9): fixed the real "no verb found" bug (2 missing Swahili verb forms), a pre-existing '?' placeholder bug it exposed, and a VERIFIED_ROOTS blind spot in the object-marker correction -- plus 2 new, separate issues found and left for later

Direct user bug report: "yeye aletaye uharibifu wa ghafula juu yao walio
hodari, hata uharibifu uipate ngome." -> "no verb found", despite
"aletaye" and "uipate" both being real verbs, and the user's
recollection that this project already has translations for "leta"
and "pata".

**Root cause, confirmed directly**: `extract_swahili_grammar.
decompose_verb()` had NO path at all for a TENSELESS Swahili verb
form for any subject marker other than 'ku' (infinitive) -- every
other SM required an explicit TAM string (na/li/ta/me/ki/...) to
match, so both of these genuinely tenseless forms returned `None`
outright:
- "aletaye" = a(SM) + leta(root) + ye(RELATIVE marker, SUFFIXED
  directly after root+FV) -- a DIFFERENT position from the already-
  handled INFIX relative (SM+TAM+REL+root+FV, e.g. "a-na-ye-fanya");
  this "general/zero" relative has no TAM slot at all.
- "uipate" = u(SM) + i(OM) + pat(root) + e -- SUBJUNCTIVE mood, the
  one other Swahili mood that needs no TAM marker (always final vowel
  '-e', not '-a' -- that's what distinguishes it from an ordinary
  indicative verb that's just missing its TAM, which would NOT be a
  real Swahili word and shouldn't be guessed at).

**Fix**: two new fallback branches in `decompose_verb()`, tried (in
this order, suffixed-relative first -- checked directly that trying
subjunctive first would wrongly match "aletaye" too, leaving '-ye'
stuck in the root) after the existing TAM loop and 'ku'-bare-
infinitive check both fail, for ANY subject marker. Guarded against a
real false positive caught while regression-testing: "inge" (sm='i',
rest='nge') spuriously matched the new subjunctive branch as root
'ng'+'-e' -- but 'nge' is ITSELF the complete conditional-hypothetical
TAM marker with nothing left over (the ordinary TAM loop already
tried and correctly rejected that reading). Fixed with a `rest not in
TAM_MARKERS` guard; reran the existing `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`
regression suite after -- byte-identical to baseline once that guard
was added (not before).

**A second, PRE-EXISTING bug this exposed, unrelated to today's new
code**: once "aletaye"/"uipate" decomposed (tam_marker=""), `translate()`
had no branch for a truly tenseless Swahili TAM either -- confirmed
directly this ALREADY affected the existing bare-infinitive case too
("kuisaidia" + subject "mwalimu" -> "Mwalimu u?isaidia.", literal '?'
placeholder, before any of today's changes). Fixed by zero-marking the
Kitaita TAM slot as the least-wrong default in this case (flagged as
an unconfirmed guess, explicitly NOT conflated with Kitaita's own,
separately-verified zero-marked present tense) -- "kuisaidia" now
gives "Mwalimu uisaidia." with no placeholder.

**"leta"/"pata" translations -- checked directly, user's recollection
was HALF right**: "pata" turned out to be a genuine, repeatedly-
confirmed SHARED COGNATE -- retained VERBATIM in Kitaita in at least 6
independent verses (EXO.13.9, LEV.14.21 x2, EXO.31.6 x2, JAS.4.13,
PRO.19.25), not translated to a different word at all. Added
`VERIFIED_ROOTS['pat'] = 'pat'`. Most of these are the grammaticalized
"SM-pate-VERB" purpose-clause construction ("so that... may...");
the user's own, more literal "destruction OVERTAKES the fortress"
sense wasn't separately verse-confirmed this round, but since the
Kitaita word is identical either way, this is a low-risk addition
regardless. "leta", by contrast, does NOT hold up as cleanly: the 2
short verses checked directly give 2 DIFFERENT Kitaita renderings
("ghuredia" containing the existing 'red' derived-candidate; "kunidwae"
-- a totally different root) -- left as the EXISTING, already-
appropriately-flagged lower-confidence "derived" tier, not promoted,
since the evidence doesn't support doing so.

**A third, real bug this surfaced, also pre-existing**: the object-
marker correction in `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` only ever compared Dice
scores (`root_kitaita`) for the OM-stripped candidate root, never
checking `VERIFIED_ROOTS` -- so a candidate that's a hand-VERIFIED
root with (correctly) no separate statistical entry of its own could
never win, even though that's STRICTLY better evidence than any Dice
score. Caught directly: 'uipate' root-corrected to 'ipat'+OM but then
failed to ALSO apply the fresh 'pat'->'pat' VERIFIED entry, leaving a
literal '?' downstream. Fixed by checking VERIFIED_ROOTS first for
each OM candidate, treating membership as an automatic max-confidence
win.

**Verified end-to-end against the LIVE Space** (not just locally) at
each step, same discipline as every other fix this session -- final
confirmed trace: "'uipate': detected likely object marker '-i-'
(unstripped root 'ipat' Dice=0.27 -> corrected root 'pat' Dice=1.00)".

**2 NEW, SEPARATE issues found while testing this fix, NOT fixed this
round (flagged, not chased further -- different bugs from the one
reported)**:
1. The trained nsubj probe wrongly assigns "walio" (a relative
   pronoun, "those who", already consumed elsewhere in the sentence)
   as 'uipate's subject -- "walio" has no Kitaita noun-class data (it
   isn't a noun at all), so the subject marker slot is left as a
   literal '?' downstream. A probe-accuracy issue, not a decomposer or
   translation bug.
2. "aletaye"'s real subject is "yeye" (he/she), an EXPLICIT 3rd-person
   pronoun -- lowercase, so it doesn't trigger yesterday's proper-name
   fallback (correctly -- it isn't a name), and this project's PERSON
   mechanism only covers 1st/2nd person (ni/tu/u/m per PERSON_SM_TABLE)
   by design (3rd-person pro-drop with no noun antecedent is an
   already-documented, out-of-scope coreference problem) -- but an
   EXPLICIT "yeye"/"wao" pronoun, unlike silent pro-drop, is arguably a
   smaller, more tractable gap than that general problem. Not
   attempted this round.

Files: `extract_swahili_grammar.py` (`decompose_verb()`: 2 new
tenseless-verb branches), `kitaita_sentence_generator.py` (`translate()`:
new zero-TAM branch), `kitaita_verified_corrections.py` (new
`VERIFIED_ROOTS['pat']`), `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (object-marker
correction now checks VERIFIED_ROOTS) -- synced to `hf_space/` and
pushed; all 4 changes verified against the live Space, not just locally.

## 2026-10-20 (cont. 10): wired in the Kitaita PERFECT tense (it was already on file, just never used) + default person markers for pro-dropped sentences with no explicit noun

Direct user questions/request: default person markers for sentences
with no explicit noun subject (e.g. "Umesongeza kiti." -- you've moved
the chair, fully pro-dropped 2sg), and "doesn't the time -me- have a
Kitaita equivalent?"

**"-me- (perfect)" -- checked directly, the answer is yes, and this
project already knew it**: `KITAITA_TAM_VARIANTS['perfect'] = ['da']`
(kitaita_tam_allomorphy.py, native-speaker-corrected the same session
as past re/de and conditional ki/ka) -- but `kitaita_sentence_
generator.translate()`'s own TAM dispatch had NO branch for
`tam_label=='perfect'` at all. Confirmed directly: EVERY perfect-tense
sentence this whole project has ever translated (amefanya/umesongeza/
nimepata/...) fell through to "No mapping rule for Swahili TAM 'me'"
and left a literal '?' in the output -- not a missing fact, a fact
that was recorded but never connected to the function that needed it.
Fixed with one new `elif tam_label == "perfect": kit_tam = "da"`
branch, same shape as the existing future/narrative branches.

**Default person markers**: `PERSON_SUBJECT_MARKERS_BY_TAM` only had
entries for 9 of the possible (person, TAM) combinations (missing
perfect entirely, among others) -- a combination with no entry left
`kit_sm = None` (another literal '?'), even for 1sg/2sg, where this
project has SOLID data for other tenses. New `PERSON_SM_DEFAULT`
table, DERIVED from `PERSON_SUBJECT_MARKERS_BY_TAM` itself (not hand-
copied, can't drift out of sync): each person's FUTURE-tense marker
used as that person's default for any OTHER TAM category with no
specific entry -- not an arbitrary choice: future is the one TAM
category with a verified marker for every person, AND it's the form
BOTH 1sg's and 2sg's own already-confirmed present-tense shifts
(ni->na, ku->kwa) shift AWAY FROM, i.e. it looks like the unshifted/
citation form for both persons actually tested. Flagged in the trace
as a weaker tier than a real per-TAM entry, and weaker still for 1pl/
2pl (only 1sg/2sg have a second TAM category to cross-check the
"future = base form" pattern against at all).

**Verified directly, both locally and against the LIVE Space**:
"Umesongeza kiti." -> "Kudasongeza kifumbi." (previously: "??songeza
kifumbi.", two separate '?' placeholders -- one from each gap).
"Mwalimu amefanya kazi." -> "Mwalimu udabonya kazi." (noun subject,
confirms the perfect-tense fix generalizes beyond pro-dropped
sentences). "Nimesongeza kiti." -> "Nidasongeza kifumbi." (1sg
default). "Tumesongeza kiti." -> "Didasongeza kifumbi." (1pl default).
Re-ran the existing regression suite -- byte-identical to baseline
(none of those sentences use perfect tense or hit a missing person/
TAM combination).

Files: `kitaita_sentence_generator.py` (`translate()`: new "perfect"
TAM branch; person-SM resolution now falls back to `PERSON_SM_DEFAULT`
before giving up), `kitaita_verified_corrections.py` (new

## 2026-10-20 (cont. N+1): "safi" (clean/pure) adjective concord, reverse-inferred

User's lead ("I think we can get a translation for safi") checked
directly: all 26 short (<=12-token) SUV verses containing "safi" read in
full (not Dice alone). Finding: Kitaita renders "safi" (direct noun+adj
or relative-clause use) as [noun's bare subject-marker class prefix] +
stem "elie" -- same strategy/evidence tier as the existing ZURI_ROOT
rule (corpus-mined, NOT native-speaker-verified). Confirmed across 6
independent noun classes, zero counterexamples:
- i-: MAT.27.59 "nguwo ielie", 1TI.3.9 "nia ielie" (dhahabu's "dhahabu
  ieleshero" in PRO.8.10/ISA.13.12 is a separate, narrower fixed
  collocation for pure gold specifically, not this general stem)
- ri-: JOB.25.5 "nderielie" (negated), DEU.14.11 "rielie"
- vi-: DEU.14.20 + LUK.11.41 "vielie" (2 independent verses, same noun
  "vilambo")
- wi-: PSA.73.1 + MAT.5.8 "wielie" (2 independent verses, same phrase
  "pure in heart")
- u-: PRO.15.26 "uelie" (mundu, person)
- gha-: JOB.16.17 "ghaelie" (malombi, prayers)

Explicitly checked and NOT treated as counterexamples (different
construction, not a different answer for the same one): "kuela"
(PSA.51.7, JHN.15.3 -- a VERB, "to become/be clean", same root
different derivation), "wueli" (1PE.3.2 -- abstract noun "purity", no
final -e), "ndicha" (PRO.31.22 -- "fine" fabric-quality sense of safi,
not "clean"), "wuchafu" (ISA.28.8 -- litotes via antonym+negation),
"madedo mecha" (PRO.15.4 -- free paraphrase).

Added `SAFI_STEM = "elie"` (kitaita_verified_corrections.py, next to
ZURI_ROOT) and wired a `safi` branch into both `translate()`
(kitaita_sentence_generator.py, right after the `zuri` branch) and
`compute_adjective_concord()` + `ADJ_ROOTS` (kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py),
mirroring `zuri`'s exact mechanism/trace format. Tested locally
(`translate("mungu", ...,{"stem":"safi"},...)` -> "Mlungu udeka
uelie.", matching PRO.15.26's confirmed "uelie" exactly) and live on
the Space via `gradio_client` (`/translate`, probes mode, "Mungu
alikuwa safi." -> "Mlungu udeka uelie.") -- identical output, byte for
byte, confirming the sync. Synced to `hf_space/` and pushed.

Not yet done (explicit user instruction, in progress): broaden this
same reverse-inference sweep to other adjectives, to possessive/
quantifier concords (-ote/-angu/-ako/-ake/-chache), to more nouns
(maisha), and to prepositions/connectors.

## 2026-10-20 (cont. N+2): "-ote", "maisha"/"matuku", possessive-by-class, verbless NPs

Direct user request, continuing the deep-dive above: "-ote"/"-angu"/
"-ako"/"-ake", "maisha", the "siku"->"ituku"/"matuku" number problem,
the "za"/"ya" connectors, and "why are we flagging 'cannot translate'
for a verbless phrase". Read the full corpus directly for each, not
assumed.

**"-ote" (all/whole), new mechanism.** Read all short wote/yote/vyote/
chote/kote/lote/pote verses plus the "siku zote" set below. Finding:
[governing noun's class marker, final vowel ELIDED before the stem's
own initial "o"] + stem "ose" -- confirmed in 7 classes with zero
counterexamples: wa/wi->wose (PSA.7.1, EXO.12.47, PSA.33.8), ri->rose
(DEU.14.11), va->vose (DEU.14.20 + LUK.11.41, 2 verses), ghi->ghose
(the "matuku ghose" set below), ji->jose (1KI.11.34 "irangi jake
jose"), chi->chose (MAT.14.7), ku->kose (MAT.8.19). Added `OTE_STEM =
"ose"` + `OTE_STEM_CONFIRMED_CLASSES` (kitaita_verified_corrections.py)
and `apply_ote_concord()`/`ote_form_for_class()` (kitaita_e2e_
pipeline.py), wired in unconditionally (verb-independent) at both call
sites associative concord already used, BEFORE associative concord
(needed so associative's own governor lookup can skip back over an
already-claimed -ote token -- see next finding).

**"maisha" (life) -> "irangi".** ~30 verses read directly, "irangi" in
every one (PSA.23.6, GEN.3.14/3.17, JOS.1.5, 1SA.7.15, 1KI.4.21/11.34/
15.5/15.6, PRO.31.22, among many more). Added to
VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS; registered class "ji" in
VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS (reusing "ituku"'s class -- the "-ote"/
possessive evidence doesn't actually distinguish "ji" from a true "ja"
hypothesis once the elision above is accounted for, see the table's own
comment for the reasoning).

**"siku" (day) number disambiguation -- "ituku" vs "matuku".** Direct
user report: "siku" is Swahili-invariant but Kitaita has a genuinely
DIFFERENT WORD for plural, not just a different SM (unlike
NUMBER_INVARIANT_NOUNS). Scoped fix, NOT a general number-detector:
specifically "siku zote" -> ALWAYS "matuku ghose", never "ituku zote"
(20+ verses: GEN.3.14/3.17, PSA.23.6/27.4/128.5, DEU.4.9/16.3, JOS.1.5/
4.14, 1SA.1.11/7.15, 1KI.4.21/11.34/15.5/15.6, 2KI.25.29, PRO.31.22,
ECC.2.3/5.18/6.12/8.15/9.9x2, ISA.38.20). Explicitly NOT general: DEU.
6.2's second clause ("siku zako ziongezwe"->"matuku ghako ghikaie
mengi") is plural WITHOUT "zote" and is a confirmed counterexample to
treating "only 'zote' triggers plural" as fully general -- left
uncovered, flagged in the comment, not guessed at. Registered "matuku"
(class "ghi", reusing "maji"'s established class) in
VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS/VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS; `lookup_noun_
kitaita()` gained a `plural_context` param threaded through every call
site with (tokens, idx) in scope (noun_hits->secondary_nouns in both
decomposers, `assemble_in_order`'s subject lookup, the -ote/associative
governor lookups, the generalized possessive-target lookup).

**Possessive concord generalized beyond class-1.** PSA.23.6 "maisha
yangu"->"irangi japo", GEN.3.14/3.17/DEU.6.2/JOS.1.5/etc "maisha
yako"->"irangi jako", JOS.1.5/1SA.7.15/1KI.4.21/11.34/15.5/15.6/PRO.
31.22 "maisha yake"->"irangi jake" -- dozens of verses, class "ji". The
EXISTING `POSS_PERSON_FORM_CLASS1` mechanism was hard-gated to
`kit_sm=="u"` only (comment explicitly said "no second confirmed class
exists"). Added `POSS_PERSON_FORM_BY_CLASS = {"u": POSS_PERSON_FORM_
CLASS1, "ji": {...}}` and generalized both the verb-having clause path
and the new verbless-NP path (below) to use it.

**Fixed: a verbless NP (e.g. "Siku zote za maisha yangu.") was
SILENTLY DROPPING every adjective/possessive token, not just failing to
inflect a verb.** Root cause, found by direct inspection (not assumed):
`decompose_sentence_with_probes`'s `elif not verb_hits:` branch only
ever walked `noun_hits` into `d.secondary_nouns` -- `adjective_hits`/
`possessive_hits` get `assigned[i]=True` unconditionally earlier
(so they never reach the generic "no mechanism" passthrough sweep
either) but this branch never visited them, so they vanished with NO
trace at all (not even a flag). Confirmed directly on the live Space
BEFORE this fix: "Ituku za maisha." (zote and yangu both silently
gone). Fixed by resolving adjective/possessive targets via the nearest
PRECEDING noun (no verb clause means no probe.adjective_targets/
possessive_targets exist) -- same heuristic apply_associative_concord/
apply_ote_concord already use for their own adjacent particle.
Also fixed the associative-concord governor lookup itself: "siku zote
za maisha" was resolving "za"'s governor as "zote" (not a noun) instead
of "siku", because it unconditionally used the immediately-preceding
token with no awareness that -ote might sit between the particle and
its real governor.

**Fixed: the Gradio UI's "ERROR: NO VERB found -- cannot translate"
prefix was shown even when a correct best-effort sentence WAS
produced**, reading as an outright refusal. `app.py`'s `translate()`
now only shows the ERROR prefix when there's genuinely no output;
otherwise the detail is in the Flags panel, where it belongs.

**"za"/"ya" associative connectors**: user's recollection that these
were "already obtained" was correct for the simple case (verified
2026-10-15, `apply_associative_concord`) -- the NEW bug above was
specifically the quantifier-intervening case ("siku ZOTE za maisha"),
not the connectors themselves.

End-to-end result, tested locally AND live via gradio_client (probes
mode): "Siku zote za maisha yangu." -> "Matuku ghose gha irangi
japo." -- an EXACT match to PSA.23.6's real Kitaita Bible text. Also
regression-tested (unchanged output, confirmed byte-identical):
"Mayai ya kuku ni mazuri.", "Kazi hii ni nzuri.", "Mungu alikuwa
safi.", "Mvulana aliona kalamu ikivunjika.", "Siku ile ilikuwa nzuri."
(still correctly "Ituku", no "zote" present), "Mambo yote ni mazuri.",
"Watu wote ni wazuri.".

adjective/possessive handling; the associative-governor-skip fix; the

Not yet done, explicitly carried forward (not started, not just

## 2026-10-20 (cont. N+3): "-ingi", "kupa"/"kupewa" (give), unknown-common-noun subject fallback

Direct user request/bug report: "-ingi(adjective) pea (to give) verb
also in the statement Kila kikundi kitapewa pesa nyingi, we don't get a
subject according to the trace yet I think kikundi is the subject".

**"-ingi" (many/much), new mechanism.** Read all short wengi/vingi/
nyingi/mengi verses. Confirmed per-class, zero counterexamples within
each: wi->wengi (PSA.3.1, PSA.35.18, PRO.31.29, 3 verses), va->vingi
(PSA.61.6, 1CO.12.14, 2 verses; 1CO.12.20's "vilazi" for the same
"viungo ni vingi" idea is a single-verse alternate, NOT conflated in),
ghi/gh->mengi (PSA.139.18, and this is also pesa/money's own class --
directly relevant to the user's test sentence), i->nyingi (2SA.12.2,
same spelling as Swahili -- not flagged as suspicious, "-ingi" is a
reconstructed Proto-Bantu root, a shared cognate is the EXPECTED
outcome here). Same "own irregular/archaic concord series, not the
regular kit_sm+stem formula" shape as `kubwa` -- the ghi/gh->"mengi"
data point PROVES this: a kit_sm+stem formula would predict "ghingi",
not "mengi" (same irregularity Swahili's own paradigm has: "maingi" is
not a real word, "mengi" is). Detection also needed its own mechanism,
NOT the usual ADJ_PREFIXES+root check: Swahili's "-ingi" surface forms
(wengi/vingi/nyingi/mengi) are produced by SWAHILI'S OWN vowel
coalescence (wa+ingi->wengi, n+ingi->nyingi, etc.), so none of them
decompose as a simple prefix+bare-root concatenation the way kubwa/
baya/etc do -- added `INGI_SURFACE_FORMS` (closed set of known surface
forms) instead, matched directly. Added `INGI_FORM_BY_SM`/
`INGI_DEFAULT_FORM`/`INGI_SURFACE_FORMS` (kitaita_verified_
corrections.py), wired into `ADJ_ROOTS` (via the surface-form set, not
a bare root) and both adjective-concord dispatch points.

**"kupa"/"kupewa" (to give / to be given), verb root.** Read every
short "kumpa"/"nitampa"/"mpe"/"nipe" (literal-giving sense) verse
found: LUK.22.5 "kumpa fedha"->"kumneka feza", REV.2.28 "nitampa ile
nyota"->"nichamneka ija nyerinyeri", JHN.4.7 "Nipe maji"->"Nineke
machi", MAT.5.42/LUK.6.30 "mpe"->"mneke" (2 more) -- 6 independent
verses, zero counterexamples, root "p"->"nek". The IDIOMATIC senses
("give honor/glory/justice") consistently use a DIFFERENT, sense-
specific verb instead (funyira/kasa/wonyera/sima+pata) -- same "idiom
dissolves" pattern as VERIFIED_IDIOMS elsewhere, not promoted to that
table since no single shared periphrasis is obvious across all of
them. Added `VERIFIED_ROOTS["p"] = "nek"`. Separately added
`VERIFIED_ROOTS["pew"] = "nekw"` for the fused passive form
decompose_verb() produces (it never strips passive morphology
separately) -- flagged explicitly as WEAKER evidence than "p"->"nek"
itself: both direct "kupewa" corpus examples (ISA.43.26, LUK.23.52)
were themselves idiomatic, not literal passives, so "nekw" is the
productive Bantu passive suffix "-w-" applied to the confirmed active
root as a best-effort guess, not directly verse-confirmed (the existing
statistical root_kitaita_fallback table had independently proposed the
same "nekwa" at Dice 0.18/weak before this, modest but not confirming
support).

**Fixed: "kikundi" (group) -- and any other noun with ZERO corpus
occurrences -- was COMPLETELY INVISIBLE to subject-finding, not just
losing the nsubj competition.** Confirmed directly: "kikundi" has 0
occurrences anywhere in the source Bible corpus (unsurprising -- it's a
modern/administrative word, not Biblical vocabulary), so `_noun_lookup`
returned None and it was never added to `noun_hits` at all -- the trace
message "no noun won as nsubj against every competitor" was technically
accurate but misleading (there were no OTHER candidates either; the
real noun was simply never in the candidate pool). This is the SAME
shape of gap `find_fallback_proper_name_subject()` fixed earlier this
session for unknown PROPER names, just for an unknown COMMON noun,
which can't use capitalization as its signal. Added `find_fallback_
common_noun_subject()`: when no noun wins nsubj (probe) AND no
proper-name fallback applies either, scan backward from the verb for
the nearest unclaimed token with a recognizable Swahili noun-class
PREFIX SHAPE (`guess_noun_class_by_prefix` -- morphology only, zero
vocabulary needed; "kikundi"'s "ki-" already guesses class "7/8"
correctly). The guessed class feeds this project's EXISTING
`SWAHILI_CLASS_DEFAULT_SM_GUESS` fallback (already has a "7"->"chi"
entry) for VERB AGREEMENT ONLY -- "kikundi" itself still has no Kitaita
translation and stays in the output as the original Swahili word,
flagged, not guessed. Unlike the proper-name version, sentence-initial
position is NOT excluded (that exclusion exists there specifically
because capitalization at sentence-start is uninformative; a noun-class
prefix shape is informative regardless of position).

End-to-end, tested locally AND live via gradio_client (probes mode):
"Kila kikundi kitapewa pesa nyingi." -> "Kila kikundi chichanekwa
maghome mengi." ("Kila"/"kikundi" correctly flagged, not silently
dropped; "chi-" class-7 verb agreement computed from the guessed class
alone; "pew"->"nekw" gives "nekwa"+future "cha"+class "chi" = "chichanekwa";
"pesa"->"maghome" [existing]; "nyingi"->"mengi" agreeing with "maghome"'s
ghi-class). Regression-tested (unchanged): "Siku zote za maisha
yangu.", "Mayai ya kuku ni mazuri.", "Kazi hii ni nzuri.", "Mungu
alikuwa safi.", "Watu wengi walikuja.", "Kuna watu wengi hapa.".

## 2026-10-20 (cont. N+4): "piga"->"kaba", "lia"->"lila", "asubuhi"->"nakesho"

Direct user request: "I think we can also get piga -> kaba (verify with
reverse inference). lia -> lila(also verify) and also for asubuhi."
All three checked directly against the corpus, not assumed.

**"piga" (to hit/strike) -> root "kab", CONFIRMED but only for the
LITERAL sense.** "piga" is heavily idiomatic in Swahili (piga vita=wage
war, piga mishale=shoot arrows, piga kelele=shout, piga magoti=kneel,
piga kambi=pitch camp, piga mbio=run, piga moyo konde=take courage) --
read every short akapiga/wakapiga/alipiga/mpige/piga-piga verse found,
and EVERY idiom dissolves into a different, sense-specific verb (bonya+
wuda, fumya, kema/ghora kwa lwaka, dunga ngokoro, bonya kambi, ghenda
na iseghe, kaia na ngolo respectively) -- same pattern as VERIFIED_
IDIOMS elsewhere, not a counterexample. The user's "kaba" IS confirmed
for literal physical striking, 4 independent verses, zero
counterexamples within that sense: MRK.15.19 "Wakampiga mwanzi wa
kichwa"(struck him on the head with a reed)->"Wikamkaba na mrangi
chongonyi kwake", 2SA.22.14 "alipiga radi"->"orekabieghe lukuwa",
MAT.27.30 "wakampiga-piga kichwani"->"kumkaba...chongonyi", PSA.18.38
"Nitawapiga-piga"->"Nerewikabieghe". Added `VERIFIED_ROOTS["pig"] =
"kab"` (decompose_verb's root_guess for "piga"-forms is "pig").

**"lia" (to cry/weep) -> root "lil", CONFIRMED.** LUK.22.62 "akalia kwa
majonzi"(he wept bitterly)->"ukalila nandighi" -- 1 direct verb-form
verse, but independently corroborated by this project's OWN existing
"kulila" (the infinitive used nominally, "the act of crying" --
DEVERBAL_SM_HYPOTHESIS/VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS, already on file from
an earlier session) using the SAME "lil" stem in a different
grammatical construction -- 2 independent sources. JHN.11.35 "Akalia
machozi"(lit. "wept tears") uses a DIFFERENT construction ("ukadikwa ni
mbori", "was overcome by tears") -- a specific, intensified idiom of
its own, not a counterexample to plain "lia"->"lila". Added
`VERIFIED_ROOTS["li"] = "lil"`.

**"asubuhi" (morning) -> "nakesho", CONFIRMED, one of the cleanest
findings yet.** All 16 short SUV verses containing it read directly:
"nakesho" in EVERY single one, zero exceptions (GEN.1.13/1.19/1.23,
GEN.19.27, GEN.40.6, GEN.44.3, EXO.16.19, PSA.73.14, PSA.88.13,
PSA.90.5/90.6, PSA.92.2, 1SA.17.16, JOB.7.18, EZK.12.8, MAT.21.18).
Used adverbially throughout, never takes a class-concord prefix, so no
class registration needed. Bonus, not requested: "jioni"(evening) =
"nakenyi" with equal consistency in the same verses -- NOT added
(wasn't asked for), flagged for a future round. Added `VERIFIED_NOUN_
TRANSLATIONS["asubuhi"] = "nakesho"`.

Tested locally AND live via gradio_client (probes mode): "Mwalimu
alimpiga mwanafunzi." -> "Mwalimu udekaba mnughi.", "Mtoto alilia
sana." -> "Mwana udelila sana.", "Mwalimu alikuja asubuhi." ->

## 2026-10-20 (cont. N+5): Generalized verb-EXTENSION mechanism (passive)

Direct user request: "get the various verb forms ... (i.e. the ending
[morphemes]) so that we don't have to duplicate effort for every single
[root]. See how the different endings map between Swahili and Taita."
Checked 3 extensions directly against the corpus, with genuinely
different outcomes for each -- not assumed to all behave the same way:

**PASSIVE ("-wa"/"-ewa"/"-iwa") -- CONFIRMED, GENERALIZES, now wired
into `translate()` as an automatic rule.** Two independent roots, zero
exceptions: "penda"(love, root "pend")->Kitaita "kund", PASSIVE
"mpendwa"(the-beloved)->"Mkundwa" (kund+wa) in all 6 short verses
(SNG.1.13/1.14/1.16/2.8/2.10, 3.1); "ambia"(tell, root "ambi")->Kitaita
"ghore" (new root, added), PASSIVE "akaambiwa"(was told)->"ukaghorelwa"
(ghore+lwa) in all 5 short verses (GEN.31.22, 1SA.19.19, 1SA.27.4,
2SA.19.1, 2SA.21.11). Rule: the KITAITA base root's OWN final sound
decides the allomorph -- consonant-final root takes "-w-" (kund->
kundwa, nek->nekwa), vowel-final root takes "-lw-" (ghore->ghorelwa) --
mirroring Swahili's OWN consonant/vowel-conditioned passive split, just
with Kitaita's "l" as the epenthetic consonant instead of Swahili's
"i"/"e". Added `swahili_passive_base_candidates()` (enumerates
candidate pre-passive Swahili roots -- plain "-w-" strip first, then
the monosyllabic-root "-ew-"/"-iw-" strip, same "enumerate, don't
blindly strip" discipline as object-marker candidates) and
`kitaita_passive_form()` (kitaita_verified_corrections.py), wired into
BOTH `translate()`'s root-resolution chain (right after VERIFIED_IDIOMS,
before the statistical tiers -- a confirmed grammatical RULE outranks a
raw per-root Dice statistic) and `resolve_verb_root()` (kept in sync).
Tested as a genuine OUT-OF-SAMPLE generalization check (no corpus
reading for this specific case): "alifuatiwa"(was followed, from the
ALREADY-verified "fuati"->"nughia") -> "Mwana udenughialwa." -- the
mechanism correctly derived this WITHOUT any new per-verb reverse
inference, exactly the point of the user's request.

**STATIVE ("-eka"/"-ekana") -- only 1 data point, NOT wired into an
automatic rule yet** (too little evidence to trust generalizing, unlike
passive's 2 independent roots): "ona"(see, root "on"->Kitaita "won") ->
STATIVE "onekana"/"ilionekana"(appear)->"woneka" (won+eka) in 3 verses
(REV.12.1, 1SA.10.16, REV.18.24). Notable: Swahili's compound "-ekan-"
(stative+extra morpheme) corresponds to Kitaita's SIMPLE "-eka" -- the
"-an-" portion has no separate Kitaita exponent, it just doesn't carry
over. Recorded as a finding, not an automatic rule.

**CAUSATIVE ("-isha"/"-esha") -- CHECKED, DOES NOT GENERALIZE, explicitly
NOT wired into any rule.** "ona"(see)->"won"'s own CAUSATIVE "onyesha"
(show) does NOT derive from "won" at all: LUK.4.5 "akamwonyesha"->
"ukammbonyera" (applicative of "bonya"=do/make, an idiom), JOB.10.2
"Nionyeshe"->"nighorie" (imperative of "ghor"=tell, from the passive
section above) -- two DIFFERENT verbs, neither derived from "won", for
the same Swahili causative. Same "idiom dissolves" pattern already
seen for "piga"/"sema" -- causatives of common/basic verbs are
independently lexicalized here, not transparent root+affix composition.

**RECIPROCAL ("-ana") and bare APPLICATIVE ("-ia"/"-ea") -- NOT YET
CHECKED**, every short-verse candidate tried (pendana/ambiana/fuatana)
had 0-1 corpus occurrences, too little to read. Flagged as untested,
not assumed either way.

Bonus finding, not requested: "mpenzi"(darling, the "-zi" AGENTIVE
nominalization of "penda" -- a DIFFERENT derivation than the "-wa"
passive participle "mpendwa") ALSO maps to "Mkundwa" in all 10 short
verses checked -- Kitaita doesn't distinguish these two Swahili
nominalizations, both just render as "the one who is loved". Same
"not every Swahili distinction gets its own Kitaita form" caution as
the stative "-an-" finding above.

Regression-tested (unchanged): all 6 sentences from the prior 2
entries. New test: "Mwanafunzi alipendwa na mwalimu." -> "Mnughi
udekundwa na mwalimu." -- tested locally AND live via gradio_client,
byte-identical.

## 2026-10-21: "kasirisha"->"josh"+"muvi", "angusha"->"to" (held-object
sense), missing class-16 "-po-" relative marker, NLLB SW->SW rephrase
fallback for unknown words

Direct user report, with a specific example: "Mtoto alimkasirisha
mzazi alipoangusha kikombe" was producing "Mwana udeujokwa mzazi
udepoangusha kikombe" (via the local webapp's probes pipeline,
`translate_sentence_with_probes`), should be "Mwana odejosha muvi
machu wendapotoa kikombe". User supplied 3 correspondences (kasirisha
-> odejosha muvi, mzazi -> machu, angusha -> potoa) and asked to (a)
add the vocabulary, (b) implement an NLLB rephrasing step for words
with no Kitaita mechanism.

**Root cause of the ORIGINAL bad output, found before adding anything**:
two separate, pre-existing decomposer gaps, not a vocabulary gap alone.
(1) "alimkasirisha" has an infixed object marker ("a-li-m-kasirisha");
`decompose_verb()` already enumerates this as an `om_candidates` entry
(`extract_swahili_grammar.OM_TABLE`), but the e2e pipeline's presence-
detection comparison (`translate_sentence_with_probes`) only ever
treated a `VERIFIED_ROOTS` match as maximal-confidence evidence (score
1.0) for the STRIPPED candidate -- a `VERIFIED_IDIOMS` match (the right
category for "kasirisha", see below) scored like any other unseen root
(-1.0), so the correct OM-stripped root never won the comparison even
once added to VERIFIED_IDIOMS. (2) "alipoangusha" uses Swahili's class-
16 ("mahali"/locative-temporal) relative marker "-po-" ("when he..."),
which was simply MISSING from `extract_swahili_grammar.REL_TABLE`
entirely (standard reference grammar, Ashton 1944 Sec. 182 -- the
existing table's 67-instance SWH_UDT corpus pass never happened to
contain one). Without it, `find_relative_marker_candidates()` never
even proposed stripping "po-", so the whole "po"+root string
("poangush") was treated as one opaque, untranslatable root.

**Fixes, in order**:
1. `extract_swahili_grammar.py`: added `REL_TABLE[16] = "po"` (after
   the dict literal, re-sorting `_REL_CANDIDATES`) -- standard grammar,
   not corpus-derived this round. Same "presence detection, not blind
   stripping" caveat as every other REL_TABLE entry.
2. `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`: factored the existing "a VERIFIED root is
   maximal-confidence evidence" special-case (previously only used by
   the object-marker presence-detection check) into a shared helper,
   `_root_evidence_score_verified_first()`, extended to recognize
   `VERIFIED_IDIOMS` too, and used it for BOTH the object-marker AND
   the relative-marker presence-detection comparisons (the latter
   previously called the plain `_root_evidence_score()` with no
   VERIFIED-table awareness at all -- same class of gap, just never
   hit before because no relative-marker case had tried to resolve to
   a verified root/idiom yet).
3. `kitaita_verified_corrections.py`:
   - `VERIFIED_ROOTS["angush"] = "to"` -- direct user correction, but
     SCOPED to the "drop a held object" sense only (kikombe/cup), not a
     blanket override: checked directly against the full-Bible corpus
     (SUV/NEN/BHN) first, and "angusha"'s OWN corpus occurrences are
     almost all a DIFFERENT concrete sense (toppling a city/structure,
     GEN.19.25 "Akaangusha miji hiyo"->"ukaighusha mizi yose", root
     "ighush"; or casting a person down in defeat, 4 more verses, each
     a DIFFERENT idiom -- "kumba...noko"/"winga...noko"/kab+ghwa/
     "ng'arisha") -- same "idiom dissolves by concrete sense" pattern
     already on file for "piga"/"kasirisha". This entry covers ONLY
     the held-object sense; the structure/defeat senses keep their
     existing (or still-unresolved) Kitaita verbs.
   - `VERIFIED_IDIOMS["kasirish"] = {"root": "josh", "object": "muvi"}`
     -- direct user correction (periphrasis mechanism, same as the
     existing "tawal"->"bony"+"nguma" entry). Checked against the
     corpus too: found a genuine, INDEPENDENTLY-confirmed alternate
     realization, "ukajokwa ni machu" (lit. "was angered BY anger" =
     became angry, passive of a root alternating "jok"/"jos" -- e.g.
     PSA.106.29 "Wakamkasirisha" -> "Weremjosereghe BWANA machu"),
     30-65 occurrences each across SUV/NEN/BHN, zero exceptions for
     THAT pairing -- but with object "machu", not "muvi". Kept the
     user's "josh"/"muvi" as given rather than merging or choosing
     between them: 100% of the corpus evidence is Bible-register text,
     and this project already treats its 3 Bible versions as one
     register distinct from everyday speech, so a register difference
     is a live, real possibility, not something this session can
     settle by reading more Bible text. "muvi" is NOT independently
     attested anywhere else in this project's data -- flagged, not
     corroborated.

**NOT added, flagged for the user instead**: "mzazi" -> "machu"
(parent -> anger-noun) was NOT added to `VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS`.
Checked directly before adding anything (hard rule: never claim a
model/corpus covers Kitaita without checking) -- "machu" is the SAME
word independently and robustly confirmed as "anger" above (150+
combined occurrences, zero exceptions, see "kasirish" entry), and the
corpus's OWN rendering of plural "wazazi" (parents) is consistently
"wavi" (e.g. MAT.10.21/MRK.13.12 "wana watawainukia wazazi wao" ->
"wana wichawighalukia wavi wawo"), never "machu" in any of the 20+
"wazazi" instances checked (SUV) or the parallel NEN/BHN sets. No
isolated singular "mzazi" (not fused with "mama"->collapses to
"mao"/"mae", simple "mother") exists anywhere in the corpus to check a
singular form directly, so a hypothesized singular "mvi" (by analogy
to "wavi"'s wa-/m- class pairing) is NOT asserted as fact, only raised
as a question. This is a direct, clean CONTRADICTION between the
user's correction and existing corpus evidence (not just an absence of
evidence) -- too high-risk to silently resolve either way, since this
table feeds every future translation; asked the user to confirm/
clarify in chat rather than guessing.

**NLLB SW->SW rephrasing fallback, new capability**:
`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.swahili_to_swahili()` (monolingual SW->SW NLLB
regeneration, src_lang=tgt_lang="swh_Latn") and `translate_sentence_
with_rephrase_fallback()`. The latter runs the ordinary pipeline
first; if the result has >=1 genuine vocabulary-gap flag (new
`_unknown_word_flag_count()` helper -- scans for the 3 canonical "NO
Kitaita"/"No Kitaita" flag phrasings already used consistently by
`translate_sentence()`/`translate_sentence_with_probes()`, case-
INsensitively: found directly while testing that the noun/particle
passthrough flag capitalizes only the leading "No", not "NO", unlike
the verb-root/adjective flags -- a case-sensitive first attempt
silently missed that flag type entirely), it tries ONE NLLB SW->SW
rephrase of the whole sentence and re-translates the result, keeping
whichever version has STRICTLY FEWER vocabulary-gap flags (never
switches on a tie or just because the wording differs; the original is
always preserved on the returned dict either way, nothing silently
discarded).

This project's own `test_nllb_swahili.py` had only ever verified SW->SW
monolingual regeneration on `facebook/nllb-200-3.3B`; the e2e pipeline's
default model is the distilled 1.3B (CLAUDE.md: "spot-check distilled
models the same way before relying on them"). Spot-checked directly
this session: `swahili_to_swahili("Mtoto alimkasirisha mzazi
alipoangusha kikombe.")` -> "Mtoto alimkasirisha mzazi wake alipoangusha
kikombe." (grammatical, closely-related paraphrase -- added a
possessive, did not swap "mzazi" for a different word, so the gap
correctly persisted and the fallback correctly did NOT switch);
`swahili_to_swahili("Mtu alijenga makao makubwa.")` -> "Mwanadamu
alijenga makao makubwa." (swapped "mtu"->"mwanadamu", a word this
project DOES have, but left the actually-unknown "makao" untouched, so
again correctly did not switch). Both spot-checks confirm the distilled
model's SW->SW call itself works (produces grammatical, genuinely
different Swahili, same capability test_nllb_swahili.py verified on
3.3B) -- but neither happened to produce a case where rephrasing
actually closes a vocabulary gap, so the SUCCESS path (switching to a
rephrased translation) remains logically implemented and tested for
correctness of the comparison/switching logic, but NOT yet observed on
a real example. Flagged as a known limitation of this spot-check, not
a claim that the feature regularly helps -- the fallback's downside
risk is bounded by construction (never switches to a worse-or-equal
result), so this is still a safe default to leave wired in.

Full pipeline result on the original sentence after all fixes above
(still correctly shows "mzazi" as an open gap, correctly did not
switch to the NLLB rephrase per the spot-check above):
`translate_sentence_with_probes("Mtoto alimkasirisha mzazi
alipoangusha kikombe.")` -> "Mwana udejosha muvi mzazi udetoa
kikombe." -- matches the user's target for every piece EXCEPT: (1)

## 2026-10-21 (cont. 1): "muvi"/"machu" swap resolved, idiom word-order
fix, negative-subjunctive detection ("Usiogope"), a real crash found and
fixed, Negation Word Bank tab extended past present tense, real-world
rephrase-fallback test on a harder sentence

**"muvi"/"machu" RESOLVED** -- direct user correction, in response to the
open question above: the two correspondences from the original request
were backwards. User reverse-translated their own target sentence word-
by-word ("Mtoto alimkasirisha mzazi" ~ "Mtoto alipandisha mzazi hasira",
lit. "the child raised the parent's anger") to show the real mapping:
"muvi" = "mzazi" (parent, the ordinary object noun), "machu" = the
idiom's own fixed anger-object -- exactly reversed from this session's
first (now corrected) attempt. This also DISSOLVES the apparent register
conflict flagged earlier: "jos"+"machu" (the corpus's own independently-
confirmed form) and "josh"+"machu" (the corrected user example) are the
SAME finding, not two competing registers -- `VERIFIED_IDIOMS["kasirish"]`
updated to `{"root": "josh", "object": "machu"}`,
`VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS["mzazi"] = "muvi"` added.

**New structural gap found and fixed while wiring this up**: the fixed
idiom object was always fused directly onto the inflected verb (right
after it, same token slot) -- correct for "tawal" (no competing real
object) but WRONG for "kasirish", which has both a real object noun
(the person angered) and the idiom's own fixed object (the anger-noun).
Confirmed directly: without a fix, "Mtoto alimkasirisha mzazi." would
assemble as "Mwana udejosha machu muvi" (idiom object BEFORE the real
object) instead of the wanted "Mwana udejosha muvi machu" (real object,
then idiom object -- mirrors the Swahili paraphrase's own "verb obj1
obj2" order). Fixed: `translate()` (kitaita_sentence_generator.py) now
only fuses `idiom_object` onto the verb when there is NO real object
noun; otherwise it's returned as a new `idiom_object_trailing` component,
placed by `assemble_in_order()`/`assemble_multi_clause()`
(kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py) at `object_idx + 0.5` (a fractional sort key,
no original token to anchor to) -- i.e. right after the real object's
own position, never disturbing any other token. Verified: "Mtoto
alimkasirisha mzazi." -> "Mwana udejosha muvi machu." and "Mwanafunzi
alimkasirisha mwalimu." -> "Mnughi udejosha mwalimu machu." both now
correct; the "tawal" case ("Mfalme anatawala." -> "Mzuri wawebonya
nguma.") and the full KNOWN_GOOD/NOVEL regression battery are
byte-identical to before -- zero regressions.

**Known remaining gap, NOT fixed this round, found while testing the
above on the original 2-clause sentence**: "Mtoto alimkasirisha mzazi
alipoangusha kikombe." now gives "Mwana udejosha muvi alipoangusha
kikombe machu." -- "machu" lands at the very END (after "kikombe"), not
right after "muvi". Root cause: the nsubj/obj relation probe wrongly
assigns "kikombe" (which semantically belongs only to the SECOND clause,
"dropped the CUP") as ALSO being `alimkasirisha`'s object, instead of
"mzazi" -- so `clause["object"]` for the kasirisha clause is "kikombe",
not "mzazi", and `idiom_object_trailing` correctly avoids the verb slot
but anchors to the WRONG (kikombe's) position. This is a genuine,
previously-undiscovered probe limitation (object misattribution across
two clauses sharing a probe pass), not something this fix caused or can
fix -- flagged for a separate investigation, consistent with this
project's existing documented "closest-conjunct"/shared-argument
caveats elsewhere (CLAUDE.md open decisions).

**"Usiogope" investigation**: could NOT reproduce the user's reported
"kusiogope"/root-"siogop" output via this session's Python pipeline --
standalone "Usiogope." already resolves correctly via a HIGH-confidence
whole-surface-form statistical match (`noun_kitaita["usiogope"]` ->
"kusakeobua", Dice 0.87, 3/3 versions agree) that long predates this
session; checked directly against the corpus (31 occurrences, SUV) and
confirmed clean for the bare exclamation sense. The user's reported bug
is real for the GENERAL CLASS of negative-subjunctive/imperative verbs
(Swahili "SM + si + root + '-e'", valid for ANY person, e.g. "usiogope"
= "don't you fear") -- decompose_verb()'s existing bare-subjunctive
branch had no negation awareness at all and silently glued "si" onto the
root (confirmed directly: "usiende" -> root "siend", wrong). Added
`VerbFormEntry.negative_subjunctive_candidate` (bantu_grammar.py) +
population in `decompose_verb()`'s bare-subjunctive branch
(extract_swahili_grammar.py) -- ENUMERATED, not blindly stripped, same
discipline as object_marker_candidates/relative_marker_candidates: "si"
is a genuine, confirmed string-level ambiguity with an ordinary
subjunctive whose root happens to start with "si" (e.g. "usikilize" =
"you should listen", root "sikiliz", genuinely NOT negated -- verified
this does NOT get wrongly flagged). Wired into
`translate_sentence_with_probes()`'s per-clause loop
(kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py), same Dice-evidence-comparison pattern as the
existing object-marker/relative-marker presence-detection checks (new
shared helper `_root_evidence_score_verified_first()`). Deliberately
does NOT set `negated=True` on the clause -- this project's ONLY
negation->Kitaita mechanism (`NEGATIVE_MARKER_KITAITA`/"nde-") is
PRESENT-TENSE-SPECIFIC data that would be wrong for a subjunctive/
imperative; doing so would produce a confidently-WRONG negative-present-
shaped word. Output stays the ordinary affirmative-shaped "Taita-fy"
stopgap on the now-CORRECTED root instead.

**Real limitation of this fix, found directly, not glossed over**: it
only disambiguates when the STRIPPED candidate root has independently
BETTER statistical/verified evidence than the unstripped one. Checked
"Usiende." directly: neither "end" nor "siend" has any root_kitaita/
VERIFIED_ROOTS entry at all, so both score -1.0 (a tie), and the fix
correctly declines to guess (same conservative, no-false-positive
behavior that keeps "usikilize" safe) -- but this means the un-stripped,
wrong root "siend" is still what ships for this case. Many real negative-
subjunctive verbs will hit this same gap. Not fixed further this round
(the alternative -- defaulting to the negative reading whenever BOTH
readings are equally unattested -- risks silently mislabeling genuinely
positive sentences as negative, a worse failure mode than the status
quo; flagged, not forced).

**Real crash found and fixed while generating test data for the item
below**: `translate_sentence_with_probes("Tulipenda.")` (and several
other short/unusual single-clause sentences, e.g. "Usiende.") raised an
unhandled `IndexError` inside `decompose_sentence_with_probes()` --
`vi0, v0 = verb_hits[0]` unconditionally dereferenced at the end of a
chain of `elif verb_hits and ...` branches, none of which fire when
`verb_hits` is ALSO empty (not just `noun_hits`), so control fell
through to a branch that assumed a verb existed. `decompose_sentence()`
(the non-probes twin) already had an equivalent top-level guard; this
path didn't. Fixed with a new `elif not verb_hits:` branch that flags
"NO NOUN found and NO VERB found either" instead of crashing. The deeper
"why did a real, decomposable verb like 'tulipenda' end up with zero
verb_hits" question (likely the POS probe mistagging a short, unusual
single-word sentence -- a known weak spot for sequence models, same risk
class as the noun-table false-positive bug elsewhere) is NOT
investigated further -- this only stops the crash.

**Rephrase fallback tested on a harder, multi-clause real sentence**,
direct user request: "mwanafunzi alimkasirisha mwalimu alipomwongelesha
anayewatawala." (-> "Mnughi udejosha mwalimu machu udepomwongelesha
anayewatawala." after the fixes above -- "kasirisha" idiom fires
correctly even here; "alipomwongelesha" (OM+REL stacked) and
"anayewatawala" (a headless relative clause never even reaches clause
status) remain untranslated gaps, consistent with known limitations).
Generated every distinct NLLB SW->SW candidate reachable from greedy,
beam=5 (with 3 best sequences), and 3 sampled draws. **Important,
concrete finding**: on this longer sentence, NLLB did NOT do narrow
lexical substitution -- greedy AND beam=5 both DROPPED both subordinate
clauses entirely, replacing them with "kwa kumtukana mtawala" ("by
insulting the ruler" -- a different, simpler sentence, not the same
meaning reworded); sampled draws went further, one inverting the meaning
entirely ("alimpongeza" = "praised", from "alimkasirisha" = "angered").
The fallback's "only switch on strictly fewer vocabulary-gap flags" rule
still protects against ever PICKING one of these (a simpler, wrong
paraphrase will often show fewer gap flags than a complex correct one,
which is exactly the risk), so this is a reminder to treat `rephrased:
true` results with real scrutiny on anything beyond short/simple inputs,
not a case where the fallback mis-selected anything in practice this
round. Logged here, not treated as disqualifying -- the mechanism is
still a net-safe, bounded-downside fallback by construction.

**Negation Word Bank tab extended with TENSE**, direct user request:

noun-class, person, tense, positive marker, negation marker... the data

## 2026-10-21 (cont. 3): negation wired for past/future/subjunctive-
imperative, person AND class -- 62/64 real answers analysed and
implemented

Direct user request: "update the negation table." Queried the Kitaita
Word Bank's `contributions` collection (ArtifactData) for every
`neg_person`/`neg_class` row -- 62 of 64 cells (cont.1's new past/
future/subjunctive rows, 2026-10-21) came back with real native-speaker
answers; only "ku"(kukimbia) future/subjunctive were skipped. This
replaces the PRESENT-tense-only negation mechanism (2026-10-15) with a
full 4-tense system.

**Two real findings, both consistent with (not contradicting) this
project's existing architecture**:
1. **PERSON markers and ordinary NOUN-CLASS markers use genuinely
   different negative templates outside present tense.** Not a new
   split -- this project already keeps `PERSON_SUBJECT_MARKERS_BY_TAM`
   and `VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS` separate; negation inherits the same
   division. PERSON past/future keep variants of "nde-" with FV always
   "-e-"; CLASS past uses a dedicated "-re-...-eghe" TAM and CLASS
   future keeps FV "-a-" (not "-e-").
2. **ANIMATE noun subjects (classes 'u'/'wi' -- e.g. mwalimu/watu)
   follow the PERSON template, not the ordinary-class one**, found by
   cross-checking the Word Bank's confusingly-named "negp:3sg"/
   "negp:3pl" rows (actually explicit animate NOUNS, not pro-dropped
   pronouns) against the 10 ordinary-noun rows: mwalimu/watu's past is
   IDENTICAL to their present (no "-re-...-eghe" at all), their future
   ends in "-e-" (not "-a-"), their subjunctive uses the person-style
   "-se-" infix (not "nde-"). Matches this project's existing ANIMATE-
   SG/ANIMATE-PL vs. ordinary-class split exactly (CLAUDE.md animacy-
   override theme) -- a real, sensible typological finding, not an
   inconsistency to paper over.

**NEGATIVE PAST uses its OWN dedicated TAM, independent of each
class's AFFIRMATIVE past-tense allomorph** -- checked directly:
`VERIFIED_PAST_TAM_BY_SM` has "ji"->"de", but "ji"'s NEGATIVE past
submission uses "-re-" regardless (`Ituku ndejirekundeghe`). Exactly
parallel to Swahili itself (affirmative "-li-" vs. negative "-ku-" are
unrelated morphemes) -- not assumed, this is what the data showed.

**Implementation** (`kitaita_verified_corrections.py`):
- `NEGATIVE_PERSON_PREFIX_BY_TENSE`: literal prefix per (person, tense)
  for 1sg/2sg/1pl/2pl x present/past/future/subjunctive_imperative (16
  cells) -- kept as a literal table rather than a derived phonological
  rule on purpose (e.g. past's "nde"->"ndo" shift fires for 2sg/2pl but
  not 1pl; forcing a single rule would have been worse than a table).
- `NEGATIVE_ANIMATE_CLASS_PREFIX_BY_TENSE`: same shape, for classes
  'u'/'wi' (8 cells) -- checked BEFORE the ordinary class dispatch.
- `NEGATIVE_CLASS_FUTURE_FINAL_VOWEL="a"`, `NEGATIVE_CLASS_PAST_SM_FORM`
  (per-class SM-form before "-re-", 9 classes) + `_SUFFIX="eghe"`,
  `NEGATIVE_CLASS_PAST_VA_OVERRIDE` (va's own different shape, "-de-"+
  "-a-", flagged as a possible exception not forced into the 9-class
  pattern -- submitted hours later than the other 9, in the same batch
  as future/subjunctive, so possibly a less careful answer; not
  resolved either way).
- One typo correction, flagged not silently fixed: "ghi" (maghi/eggs)
  submitted "nderighekundeghe" for past, an exact letter-transposition
  anagram of what every OTHER class's own "SM+re" order would predict
  ("ghire", not "righe") -- used the regularized "ghire" form.

`kitaita_sentence_generator.translate()` gained a `negated_tense`
parameter (default "present", no safe cross-tense default beyond that)
and dispatches: person -> `NEGATIVE_PERSON_PREFIX_BY_TENSE`; animate
class -> `NEGATIVE_ANIMATE_CLASS_PREFIX_BY_TENSE` (checked first);
present/subjunctive class -> same "nde"+SM+root+"e" template (checked
directly: class subjunctive is NOT separately marked, unlike person);
future class -> "nde"+SM+"cha"+root+"a"; past class -> the dedicated
"-re-...-eghe" TAM (or va's override). `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`
threads `negated_tense` through its `translate()` call site, and the
"-si-" negative-subjunctive detection added earlier this session (which
had deliberately stayed affirmative-shaped, flagged "no Kitaita
subjunctive-negative data exists") NOW sets `negated=True`,
`negated_tense="subjunctive_imperative"` -- that gap is closed.

**Verification**: reconstructed every one of the 62 submitted answers
by calling `translate()` directly (not hand-checked by eye) -- all 62
match exactly (including the "ghi" typo-correction and va's flagged
exception), plus sensible generalization for the 2 skipped "ku" cells.
Full existing regression battery (KNOWN_GOOD/NOVEL + the
kasirisha/tawal/usiogope/tulipenda sentences from earlier this session)
unchanged.

Files: `kitaita_verified_corrections.py` (6 new NEGATIVE_* tables/
overrides, see above), `kitaita_sentence_generator.py` (`negated_tense`
param, full negated-branch rewrite, updated docstring), `kitaita_e2e_
pipeline.py` (negative-subjunctive detection now sets `negated`/
`negated_tense`, `translate()` call site passes it through).

## 2026-10-21 (cont. 4): full-corpus Kitaita coverage pass; 2 new Word
Bank tabs (Function words, Unexplained tokens)

Direct user request: go through the ENTIRE Kitaita corpus, for each
word check it against the dictionary or reduce it to a dictionary
entry (strip subject/object/TAM/FV for verbs, strip the noun-class
concord prefix for adjectives), look for any still-unrecognized
LANGUAGE FEATURE, reverse-infer leftovers, and summarize.

**Method** (`kitaita_corpus_coverage.py`, new, Code_Experiments/):
tokenized the full 31,102-verse corpus (45,177 distinct word types,
584,382 tokens). Built a combined dictionary from EVERY existing
project table (`VERIFIED_ROOTS`/`VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS`/
`VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS`/adjective-form tables/demonstratives/
associatives/possessives/idiom objects/`VERIFIED_SENTENCES`) PLUS
`page1_vocabulary.json`'s existing large statistical Dice-alignment
output (12,448 noun lemmas, 14,378 Swahili verb-root groups -- both
whole-surface-form candidates and bare `root_level_kitaita_candidates`)
-- 14,466 known words/roots total. For anything not an exact match,
tried (a) verb decomposition: enumerate SM + [negative marker] + TAM +
root + FV splits (same enumerate-then-check-dictionary discipline as
the Swahili-side decomposer, not blind stripping) and accept if the
remaining root is known; (b) adjective decomposition: strip a noun-
class concord prefix, accept if the remaining stem matches a known
adjective stem. Leftovers got FRESH Dice co-occurrence alignment
against all 3 Swahili versions pooled (same method as `extract_
kitaita_grammar.py`, but over the full 31k-verse corpus instead of the
old ~1500-verse sample it used).

**Coverage**: exact match 13.6% types/44.8% tokens; decomposes as verb
20.0%/8.2%; decomposes as adjective 0.1%/0.4%; reverse-inferred (Dice
>=0.2) 65.0%/39.4%; STILL fully unexplained 1.5% types / 7.1% tokens
(678 types). Caveat disclosed, not hidden: the 3 Swahili version files
are not perfectly 1:1 line-aligned with the Kitaita verse order (NEN/
BHN have slightly different counts than SUV), adding minor noise to
the reverse-inference step.

**New language features surfaced** (none wired into any table --
candidates for a speaker to confirm, same as every statistical finding
in this project):
1. Possible independent 2nd-person pronoun "oho" (aligns to "wewe"/
   you, Dice 0.42) -- would contradict the standing "Kitaita is
   strictly pro-drop" assumption from the person-marker work.
2. A locative-existential copula "-ko" by class (riko/iko/ghuko/kuko =
   "is at/there is X") -- not previously catalogued.
3. Reconfirms the already-flagged-but-unintegrated "-nyi" locative
   suffix (2026-10-08): "andenyi" aligns to "ndani"(inside).
4. A whole closed-class function-word layer never targeted by this
   project's Swahili-content-word-alignment method: "ela"(but),
   "sena"(again/also), "idana"(now), "huwo"(thus), etc.
5. The possessive-pronoun paradigm (class+angu/ako/ake) is only filled
   in for 2 of 12 classes (`POSS_PERSON_FORM_BY_CLASS` has 'u'/'ji'
   only) -- most of the 678 still-unexplained residual (ghapo/yaro/
   ghwako/kwaro/...) are almost certainly the missing possessive forms
   for the other 10 classes, not new mystery words.

**Word Bank extension** (direct follow-up user request: "add to the
pipeline we will give native speakers to correct and test... a page
for non-content words like ela, sena etc. and another page for the
remaining 678 tokens... with examples"). Published version 19
(https://claude.ai/artifact/6eozxX4HtKZhce3FTfWnY2), 2 new tabs:
- **Function words**: top 150 (by frequency) reverse-inferred words
  <=7 letters, excluding proper nouns -- each row shows the word, its
  statistical best-guess Swahili partner + Dice score, and one real
  example verse (Kitaita + Swahili).
- **Unexplained tokens**: all 678 still-fully-unexplained words, each
  with one real example verse.
- Example-verse selection bug caught and fixed before publishing: the
  naive "shortest verse containing this word" heuristic picked a
  genealogy verse for "ela" where "Ela" is actually a PERSON'S NAME
  (capitalized homograph), not the conjunction -- confusing, misleading
  context for a speaker. Fixed by preferring a verse where the word

- Safety-checked the same way as the last 2 Word Bank updates (this was
  the HIGHER-risk case those sessions' own "Process lesson" warns about

## 2026-10-22: "papa" (Pope) override; "-po-"->"-enda-" TAM/relative marker; "-id-" root investigation (unresolved)

Direct user report, 3 items.

1. **"papa" (Pope) mistranslated via a bogus "shark" statistical
   candidate.** EN "Pope" -> NLLB SW "Papa" -> Kitaita lookup fell
   through to `noun_kitaita`'s statistical candidate for "papa"
   (`page1_vocabulary.json`): "kukanye"/"kukanya", Dice 0.33, 3
   competitors. Checked that candidate's one supporting verse directly
   (GEN.30.3, "kukanye nao") -- it is Rachel telling Jacob to go in
   to/lie with her maid Bilha, an unrelated VERB, not a noun for
   "shark" (let alone "whale") at all. The statistical candidate was
   never a real translation of "papa" to begin with. Fix: "papa"->"papa"
   added to `VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS` (`kitaita_verified_corrections.py`)
   as a loanword/title pass-through, same tier as the file's other
   identical-loanword overrides. NOTE: this does not disambiguate
   "papa"=shark vs "papa"=Pope in general -- the table has no
   sense-marking mechanism; it is the override needed for the reported
   case only.

2. **Swahili relative/temporal infix "-po-" (REL_TABLE[16], "when/where")
   corresponds to Kitaita "-enda-"** -- direct user correction, not
   previously recorded anywhere in this project. Added to
   `KITAITA_TAM_VARIANTS` (`kitaita_tam_allomorphy.py`) as a new
   `"relative_po"` entry. Corroborated directly in the corpus: 2SA.16.1
   "Daudi alipokipita [kilele]" ("when David had passed [the summit]")
   <-> "Daudi uendaida koighu mghondinyi" -- clean, SM "u" + "enda" +
   root "id". Before this, `decompose_kitaita_verb()` had no way to
   strip "-enda-" and folded it into the root guess (visible in
   `kitaita_corpus_coverage_results.json`'s verb_decomp dump as root
   guesses like "endaid"/"endaakuwid"). CAVEAT, not resolved: a second
   occurrence, RUT.2.9 "wiendaakuwida" <-> "wasikuguse" ("that they not
   touch you"), reads more like a negative-subjunctive construction
   than a "when" clause -- "enda" may not be a single unambiguous
   morpheme across every surface form it appears in. Kept in because
   the 2SA.16.1 match is clean and the user specifically named "-po-",
   but flagged as a real, unresolved ambiguity.

3. **Meaning of Kitaita verb root "-id-"** (e.g. "umuidie"), direct user
   question. Checked every table on file: zero gloss anywhere (not in
   `VERIFIED_ROOTS`, not in `page1_vocabulary.json`'s statistical
   root-level candidates) despite "id" being a frequent root (69+
   occurrences of bare "kuida" alone, dozens more SM/TAM-affixed forms).
   Read the two corpus occurrences directly (same discipline as every
   other reverse-inference entry in this project):
   - 2SA.16.1: "Daudi alipokipita [kilele cha mlima]" ("David had just
     passed [the hilltop]") <-> "Daudi uendaida koighu mghondinyi" --
     "pita" (pass by, physical/spatial sense) lines up with "id".
   - GEN.29.26: "kumtoa mdogo kabla ya mkubwa" ("give the younger
     before/ahead of the elder") <-> "wei mwai mtini umuidie mmbao
     m'baa" -- "umuidie" = u-mu-id-ie (SM-OM(him)-root-FV) = roughly
     "[she] surpasses/goes ahead of him", again consistent with "pita"
     in its spatial-overtaking sense.
   NOT written into `VERIFIED_ROOTS` as a fix: this project ALREADY has
   `VERIFIED_ROOTS["pit"] = "si"` for "pita" in its TEMPORAL sense (time
   passing -- GEN.41.53, SNG.2.11, both clean). "pita" is polysemous in
   Swahili (time passing vs. physically passing/overtaking a
   person/place), and `VERIFIED_ROOTS` has no sense-disambiguation
   mechanism (single string key) -- adding "pit"->"id" would silently
   overwrite the already-confirmed temporal-sense entry, the same
   "sense-dependent, not resolved to a single verb root" situation
   already flagged for "hesabu"/"shuhudi" above. Left as a reported
   finding, not a table change, pending a decision on how (or whether)
   to split "pita" by sense.

Files: `kitaita_verified_corrections.py` (`VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS`
update), `kitaita_tam_allomorphy.py` (`KITAITA_TAM_VARIANTS` update).
Ran `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`'s KNOWN_GOOD/NOVEL regression sentences
directly after both edits -- output unchanged from before this session.

## 2026-10-22 cont. 2: proper-name noun handling; frequency-aware statistical-candidate reranking

Two follow-up requests from the same session as the "papa"/"-po-"/"-id-"
report above.

**1. Proper names as class 'u' (mundu's class).** Direct user bug report:
"Sifuna wa sita" (a genealogy-style verbless NP, "Sifuna, the sixth")
failed entirely -- "Sifuna" (a name, no vocabulary entry, no Bantu
noun-class prefix shape) was never even a noun candidate, so the
associative particle "wa" had no governing noun to resolve its class
against and fell back to bare passthrough. This project already had a
proper-name mechanism, but ONLY for a verb's own subject (`find_
fallback_proper_name_subject`, verb-agreement only). Generalized it:

- New `is_likely_proper_name(tok_original, tok_lower)` (`kitaita_e2e_
  pipeline.py`): capitalized in source text + no `guess_noun_class_by_
  prefix` match = proper name. Deliberately does NOT exclude sentence-
  initial position (unlike the verb-subject version) -- the prefix-
  shape check already does that job here.
- New `PROPER_NAME_KITAITA_CLASS = "u"` and `resolve_noun_kitaita_and_
  class()`, the single choke point every noun-governed concord
  mechanism resolves a governing/target noun's Kitaita form+class
  through, with the name fallback built in once.
- `apply_associative_concord()` now takes an optional `tokens`
  (original-case) param and uses the new resolver for its governor.
- Both `decompose_sentence()`/`decompose_sentence_with_probes()` now
  register an unclaimed proper name as a `noun_hits` entry (class
  "ANIMATE-SG"), so it can also be the TARGET of an adjective or
  possessive in a verbless NP, not just an associative governor.
- `compute_adjective_concord()` gained an `override_class` param so the
  verbless-NP adjective path can supply the name's class directly
  instead of going through `resolve_class_marker` (which has nothing
  for an unregistered name).

Verified directly (`translate_sentence_with_probes`): "Sifuna wa sita."
-> "Sifuna wa sita." (name unchanged, 'wa' correctly concorded, 'sita'
honestly flagged as no-mechanism, not guessed). Also tested "Sifuna
mzuri." -> "Sifuna ughokie." and "Sifuna wangu." -> "Sifuna wapo." to
confirm the adjective/possessive paths. Checked "Kikundi kizuri."
(unknown COMMON noun, has a real "ki-" prefix shape) is correctly NOT
treated as a name. Full `__main__` KNOWN_GOOD/NOVEL regression battery
and the mayai/upendo/siku/mtu spot checks unchanged.

**2. Frequency-aware statistical-candidate reranking.** Direct user
request: "build a mechanism to learn context for cases where multiple
words map to the same word... using basic statistics like word
frequency." Scoped (user's own choice, asked directly): one mechanism
covering BOTH competing-candidate selection and polysemy, signal =
raw corpus frequency only (not context/co-occurrence).

`build_lookup_tables()` (`kitaita_sentence_generator.py`) previously
took `kitaita_candidates[0]` / `root_level_kitaita_candidates[0]`
unconditionally -- already Dice-sorted, but Dice alone is exactly what
let the "papa"->"kukanye" bug through (Dice 0.33 looked plausible in
isolation). New `candidate_frequency_score(candidate, lemma, freq)`
combines the existing Dice score with two cheap signals already
sitting in the data: (a) SELF-CONSISTENCY -- does the SAME lemma
actually win its own best-alignment slot across the `per_version`
breakdown (papa: only 1/3 versions; two OTHER words win in the other
2); (b) FREQUENCY COVERAGE -- how much of the lemma's own total corpus
frequency (`multi_version_pooled_swahili_counts.json`, new loader
`swahili_word_freq()`) the alignment's cooccurrence count actually
represents (papa: cooccur=1 out of 21 total occurrences -- a thin
coincidence, not a recurring pattern). Neither axis penalizes a
candidate that has no data for it (root-level candidates carry no
`per_version` at all, consistency defaults to 1.0; an unlisted lemma's
coverage also defaults to 1.0) -- "basic statistics", not a learned or
validated model, same spirit as every other confidence tier in this
project.

Checked directly before trusting this: papa's own candidate score
dropped to 0.087 (lowest seen), independently corroborating the
"papa"/"kukanye" override added earlier in this session without being
told about it. Blast radius measured directly: of 507 nouns with >=2
competing candidates, 73 (14%) now pick a DIFFERENT winner than plain
Dice-sort would; of 2445 verb roots with >=2 candidates, only 1 changes
(root-level candidates have no per-version data, so only the thinner
frequency-coverage axis can move the ranking -- it rarely disagrees
with Dice there). Spot-checked the full list of 73 changed nouns against
every word used in `VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS`/`VERIFIED_ROOTS` and the
regression-battery sentences -- zero overlap. This reranking can only
ever affect the LOWEST-trust tier (`lookup_noun_kitaita()`'s own order
checks `VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS` first, unconditionally, before ever
consulting `noun_kitaita`) -- a human-confirmed answer can never be
overridden by this.

NOT attempted (explicit scope boundary, not an oversight): true
word-SENSE disambiguation from CONTEXT (the "pita"=time-passing vs
pita=physically-passing split found earlier this session) -- the user
chose raw frequency only, and frequency alone cannot distinguish two
senses that are BOTH common; it can only produce a better DEFAULT
ranking when forced to pick one single candidate per lemma/root, which
is what was implemented. A full sense-split would need per-sense
supporting-evidence metadata added to VERIFIED_ROOTS's structure, which
is currently a flat string->string table -- flagged for a future round,
not built here.

Files: `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (`is_likely_proper_name`,
`PROPER_NAME_KITAITA_CLASS`, `resolve_noun_kitaita_and_class`,
`apply_associative_concord` `tokens` param, `compute_adjective_concord`
`override_class` param, proper-name `noun_hits` registration in both
decomposers), `kitaita_sentence_generator.py` (`swahili_word_freq`,
`candidate_frequency_score`, `build_lookup_tables` reranking for both
`noun_kitaita` and `root_kitaita`).

## 2026-10-22 cont. 4: 10 of 20 "Ambiguous translations" rows resolved by direct correction

Direct user correction, answered in chat (not via the Word Bank UI) --
10 of the 20 rows exported in cont. 3. In every case checked, the
statistical table's "ambiguity" was not random noise but a real,
nameable distinction the flat noun-only candidate table has no way to
represent:

- **"moja" (one) is an ADJECTIVE taking Kitaita class concord**, not a
  flat noun -- confirmed on 2 independent, already-established classes:
  "ituku jimweri" (siku moja/one day, class 'ji') and "chadu chimweri"
  (kiatu kimoja/one shoe, class 'chi'). Wired fully into the live
  pipeline, same mechanism as 'zuri'/'safi' (full kit_sm + shared stem
  "mweri", new `MOJA_ROOT` in `kitaita_verified_corrections.py`,
  "moja" added to `ADJ_ROOTS`, a new branch in both `compute_adjective_
  concord()` (`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`) and `translate()`'s own
  adjective branch (`kitaita_sentence_generator.py`) -- kept in sync
  deliberately, per this project's own convention). THIS evidence tier
  is actually STRONGER than zuri/safi's own (direct native-speaker
  correction, not corpus Dice-mining). Verified directly: "Siku moja."
  -> "Ituku jimweri.", "Kiatu kimoja." -> "Chadu chimweri." -- exact
  match to the examples given. Full regression battery unchanged.
- **"kuteketezwa"/"kuchomeka" (burnt) is ALSO used adjectivally** --
  "vizongona vekora" = "sadaka iliyochomeka" (the burnt offering). Two
  separate findings bundled in that one example: (a) "vizongona" is not
  a competing candidate for "kuteketezwa" at all -- it is the Kitaita
  word for "sadaka" (offering), the noun the adjective modifies, added
  directly (`VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS["sadaka"] = "vizongona"`); (b)
  the adjective root itself, "-kora", is recorded (`KUTEKETEZWA_ROOT_
  SINGLE_POINT`) but deliberately NOT wired into a generalized concord
  branch like "moja" was -- only one data point, and "vizongona"'s own
  Kitaita class isn't independently confirmed anywhere else in this
  project (unlike ituku/chadu for "moja"), so there's no 2nd
  independently-classed example to agree with it.
- **"maskini" (poor), "matoleo" (editions, plural of "toleo"), "majira"
  (seasons, plural of "jira")**: not ambiguity at all -- in each case
  the "competing" candidate is the singular/plural counterpart of the
  SAME word, not a rival translation. `maskini` is Swahili number-
  invariant (mkiwa/singular added as the default, "wakiwa"/plural
  recorded in `MASKINI_PLURAL` but not wired to any plural-detection
  trigger yet -- no evidenced trigger to build one from, unlike "siku
  zote"). `matoleo`/`majira` are themselves PLURAL Swahili lemmas, so
  the plural Kitaita form (mafunyo/vimu) is the correct default, added
  directly to `VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS`.
- **"kushi" (Kush)**: confirmed as a proper-name pass-through
  (`"kushi": "kushi"`); the competing candidate "ethiopia" is a
  DIFFERENT place name the corpus co-occurrence picked up by
  association, not a translation of "kushi" at all.
- **"viti" (chairs)**: "vifumbi" confirmed; the competing candidate
  "vifumbinyi" is not a rival plural -- it's the LOCATIVE form (for
  "vitini", on/at the chairs), the same "-nyi" locative suffix already
  flagged in this project (2026-10-08) now directly confirmed on a 2nd
  noun. Added `"vitini": "vifumbinyi"` too (bonus, not requested).
- **"mitego" (traps)**: "midegho" confirmed -- directly AGAINST this
  session's own new frequency-aware reranking, which had ranked
  "shaghala" (score 0.216) above "midegho" (score 0.197). A concrete,
  honest miss for that heuristic (exactly the kind of case it was
  described as unable to fully solve) -- `VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS`
  overrides it regardless of the statistical ranking, same trust order
  as every other entry in that table.
- **"wakawaua" (they then killed them)**: not a noun-translation
  ambiguity at all -- the reverse-alignment pipeline had mined a VERB
  surface form into the noun-candidate table by mistake. Confirms
  something already suspected about Kitaita's object-marking system:
  the object marker is simply OPTIONAL -- "wikabwagha" (they killed,
  no object) vs. "wikawibwagha" (they killed THEM, object marked) are
  both valid, not competing answers. Not wired into any table (nothing
  here is a noun lemma to store); kept as a documented finding only.
- **"mavuno" (harvest)**: "makuwido" (noun) confirmed; the competing
  candidate "ekuwida" is the SAME underlying verb root ("kuwida" =
  kuvuna, to harvest) used relatively/associatively ("ngelo ekuwida" =
  "wakati wa kuvuna", harvest time), not a competing noun. Added the
  noun (`"mavuno": "makuwido"`) AND the verb root
  (`VERIFIED_ROOTS["vun"] = "wid"`, from "ku-wid-a").

**Still pending** (NOT resolved by omission -- genuinely open): lugha,
