## 2026-10-22 cont. 5: "ni" copula (no adjective), "kama"->"sa", "jana"->"ighuo"

3 more direct native-speaker corrections, given in chat.

1. **The invariant present copula "ni" ("X ni Y") is ALSO just "ni" in
   Kitaita, kept unconjugated, when NO adjective complement follows.**
   Before this, every "kuw"-rooted verb with no adjective (including
   literal "ni") fell into the SAME "bare existential" branch as real
   conjugated past-tense "kuwa" (alikuwa/amekuwa) -- wrong for "ni"
   specifically, which was never actually tested that way; the existing
   dek-root finding (4/4 native-speaker-confirmed, "ni"+ADJECTIVE ->
   "odeka"/"edeka"/etc.) was and remains correct and untouched. Fixed
   by adding a new branch in `translate()` (`kitaita_sentence_
   generator.py`) keyed on `swahili_verb["sm"] is None` -- the signal
   that uniquely identifies the bare word "ni" (`decompose_verb_or_
   copula()` sets `subject_marker=None` ONLY for literal "ni"; every
   conjugated kuwa form carries a real subject marker and so still
   correctly falls through to the untouched existing branches).
   Checked directly: "Mtu ni mwalimu." -> "Mundu ni mwalimu." (new,
   literal "ni" kept) vs. "Mtu ni mzuri." -> "Mundu udeka ughokie."
   (unaffected, still the confirmed dek root). Full regression battery
   unchanged.
2. **"kama" (if/like/as) -> "sa"**: added to `FUNCTION_WORD_
   TRANSLATIONS` (same mechanism as "na"). Verified: "Kama mtu ni
   mzuri." -> "Sa mundu udeka ughokie."
3. **"jana" (yesterday) -> "ighuo"**: added to `VERIFIED_NOUN_
   TRANSLATIONS`, same adverbial/temporal shape as "asubuhi"/"nakesho"
   (not yet corpus-cross-checked the way asubuhi was -- flagged at this
   file's ordinary n=1 trust tier, not claimed as corpus-confirmed).
   Verified: "Jana mtu aliona simba." -> "Ighuo mundu udewona shimba."

Files: `kitaita_sentence_generator.py` (new "ni" branch in
`translate()`), `kitaita_verified_corrections.py`
(`FUNCTION_WORD_TRANSLATIONS["kama"]`,
`VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS["jana"]`).

## 2026-10-22 cont. 6: "jioni", "lugha", "mawazo" resolved; "leo" added

3 more of the 20 "Ambiguous translations" rows resolved by direct
correction, plus one brand-new word.

- **"jioni" (evening) -> "luma lwa kenyi", the FULL phrase, unsegmented.**
  Neither of the 2 exported flat candidates ("kenyi" Dice 0.468, "luma"

## 2026-10-22 cont. 8: "hana"->"ndeuna" negation verb wired; "wote"->"wose" fixed (confirms Wakatoliki class 'wi'); KNOWN FAILURE CASE logged for the relation probe on long/multi-clause sentences; personal pronouns default to mundu's class

**1. "kuwa na" (to have) -- a 2nd irregular/defective verb, same shape
as "ni".** Direct native-speaker paradigm: mimi nina/wewe una/yeye ana
(affirmative), mimi sina/wewe huna/yeye hana (negative) -- "the verb is
the same in Kitaita, -na". `decompose_verb_or_copula()`
(`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`) gained a small closed-set table,
`NA_HAVE_FORMS` (nina/una/ana/sina/huna/hana), since neither the
regular verb decomposer (root too short) nor `decompose_negative_verb()`
(requires final vowel '-i', but "hana" etc. irregularly keep '-a') can
recognize these at all. `translate()` gained a matching root-resolution
branch (Kitaita root "n", + the negative assembly's final vowel
overridden to '-a' instead of the regular '-e' specifically for this
root -- same irregularity mirrored from the Swahili side). Verified:
"Papa hana uwezo." -> "Papa ndeuna uwezo." -- exact match to the
user's own worked example. Found and fixed a SEPARATE, blocking gap
while testing this: "papa" itself had never had a Kitaita class
registered (added `VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS["papa"]="u"`, a human
reference defaults to ANIMATE-SG same as mtu/mwalimu).

**2. "wote"->"wose" fixed -- confirms Wakatoliki is class 'wi', not
just a plausible guess.** Not a probe issue: `-ote` concord is
adjacency-based, and failed only because "Wakatoliki" (added
yesterday) had no registered class. The direct confirmation that
"wote" resolves to "wose" here (this project's own existing -ote rule:
wa-/wi-class elides to bare 'w'+'ose') pins Wakatoliki's class down to
'wi' -- added to `VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS`. Verified: "Wakatoliki
wote wanajiuliza." -> "Wakatoliki wose waweukadidikwa."

**3. KNOWN FAILURE CASE, logged for a future round, not fixed now**
(explicit user instruction -- "the scope is already wide enough"):
the relation probe badly over-generalizes "object" assignment on long,
multi-clause real-world sentences. Tested on the full AP News
paragraph (2026-10-22 cont. prior entry) -- "swali" (question) was
assigned as the probe-identified OBJECT of 6 of the 8 clauses in that
one very long sentence, most of them structurally unrelated to
"swali" at all (amepoteza/kutekeleza/hawezi/kuliongoza should have
"fahamu"/"majukumu"/nothing/"Kanisa" as their real objects). Subjects
fared much better than objects. Working hypothesis, NOT validated
this session: the probe isn't clause-aware -- it appears to compare
every noun against every verb across the WHOLE sentence rather than
within the clause each verb actually sits in, so the single most
salient/frequent noun in a long sentence can win every verb's "object"
slot regardless of distance or real clause membership. Candidate
directions for later (not started): (a) split on clause boundaries
(relative pronouns, colons, conjunctions joining independent clauses)
BEFORE calling the probe, the same way `split_sentences()` already
prevents cross-SENTENCE contamination, just one level finer; (b) a
confidence-margin threshold on the probe's own output, flagging a
low-margin call as "unclear" instead of asserting it, matching this
project's existing flag-don't-guess posture everywhere else.

**4. Personal pronouns default to mundu's class.** Direct user
instruction, found while debugging "Mimi ni mrefu." ("I am tall"):
output was "Ini ?deka mrefu." -- the adjective concord ("mrefu"->
"mlacha") and the copula's own subject prefix both failed, because
"mimi" (I) DOES have a Kitaita translation (the statistical "ini"),
which has no class data of its own, and "mimi" never reaches this
project's EXISTING Swahili-class-label fallback (`SWAHILI_CLASS_
DEFAULT_SM_GUESS`) because that only fires when a noun has NO
translation at all. New `SWAHILI_PERSONAL_PRONOUNS` (mimi/wewe/yeye/
sisi/ninyi/wao) + `PERSONAL_PRONOUN_KITAITA_CLASS="u"` in
`kitaita_verified_corrections.py`, checked in `translate()`'s subject-
class resolution BEFORE the statistical/corrected-class lookup, keyed
on the SWAHILI lemma (robust regardless of which Kitaita word a
pronoun translates to). Verified: "Mimi ni mrefu." -> "Ini udeka
mlacha." -- "ni"+adjective still correctly uses the dek root
(unaffected, matches the existing 4/4-confirmed finding), and the
adjective now resolves. Only "mimi" was actually exercised this
session; wewe/yeye/sisi/ninyi/wao are included on the same general
instruction but not individually tested.

**Separate, NOT fixed, flagged only**: "Mimi ninapenda kitabu." (an
ordinary, already-working verb, no relation to today's "na_have" or
pronoun work) -- "mimi" gets picked up as a real noun subject by the
probe/statistical table rather than going through the dedicated 1st/
2nd-person pro-drop mechanism, so the verb's own embedded `person`
field is discarded. Today's pronoun-class fix repairs the AGREEMENT
(kit_sm/kit_class), but the deeper "a pronoun that also has a

architecture issue is untouched -- e.g. "Mimi sina kitabu." currently
resolves via the ANIMATE-class 'u' negative template ("ndeuna") rather
than the person-specific 1sg template ("sina" per NEGATIVE_PERSON_
PREFIX_BY_TENSE). Not addressed this round -- same "scope is wide
enough" instruction applies.

## 2026-10-22 cont. 9: "Ini nideka mlacha" correction (person vs class agreement split); 2 new bugs found + fixed while debugging a real multi-clause sentence

**1. Correction to today's personal-pronoun fix (cont. 8): verb uses
PERSON agreement, adjective uses mundu's CLASS agreement -- these are
NOT the same mechanism.** Direct user correction: "Ini udeka mlacha"
(the first version of the fix) should have been "Ini nideka mlacha".
Root cause of the original bug stands (pronoun's Kitaita form, "ini",
has no class data), but the fix itself was too broad -- it forced
mundu's class 'u' onto BOTH the verb's subject prefix AND the
adjective concord, when only the adjective should use it. New
`SWAHILI_PRONOUN_TO_PERSON` (mimi/wewe/sisi/ninyi -> 1sg/2sg/1pl/2pl;
"yeye"/"wao" deliberately excluded -- this project's person-marker
scheme never covers 3rd person) in `kitaita_verified_corrections.py`;
`translate()` now re-overrides `kit_sm` (verb prefix) to the EXISTING
`PERSON_SM_DEFAULT` bare-citation-form tier (2026-10-20) AFTER the
`kit_class` copy, so the two deliberately diverge for pronoun subjects
-- `kit_class` stays "u" for the adjective. Verified: "Mimi ni mrefu."
-> "Ini nideka mlacha." (exact match). Regression battery unchanged.

**2. Found and fixed 2 real bugs while debugging "Ninawapenda ndege wa
kwetu, nafurahia nyimbo zao." (direct user report: "why isn't it
translating... we have subject and object").**

- A sentence-initial capitalized VERB ("Ninawapenda") was being wrongly
  claimed by TODAY's EARLIER proper-name fix (cont. 1 of this session,
  the "Sifuna wa sita" work) before the verb_hits loop ever got a
  chance to see it -- `is_likely_proper_name()` alone can't tell "a
  name" from "a verb that happens to be capitalized and lack a Bantu
  noun-class prefix shape". First attempted fix (checking the POS
  probe's own VERB/ADJ tag) made things WORSE -- the POS probe ALSO
  mistags the genuine name "Sifuna" as VERB, which would have
  regressed the original "Sifuna wa sita"/"Sifuna mzuri" fix from
  earlier today (caught directly by re-running those exact test
  sentences before trusting the change, NOT assumed safe). Settled on
  checking real morphological decomposability (`decompose_verb_or_
  copula(tok) is not None`) instead -- more precise/grounded than a
  statistical POS guess, and doesn't regress either case. Applied to
  both decomposers (`decompose_sentence`/`decompose_sentence_with_
  probes`).
- "nafurahia" was entirely unrecognized as a verb (`decompose_verb()`
  returned `None`), even though the exact same verb WITH its full
  subject marker, "ninafurahia", decomposes fine. Cause: standard
  Swahili allows the 1sg present subject marker "ni-" to be elided
  directly before the "-na-" TAM marker (reference grammar, Ashton
  1944; "ninasoma"/"nasoma" both mean "I am reading", extremely common
  in real text) -- `decompose_verb()`'s main loop never tries this
  because "na" is a TAM string, not a listed SM candidate, so a verb
  with NO SM prefix at all was simply never attempted. Added as a
  narrow, closed fallback (tried only after every SM-prefixed reading
  has failed) in `extract_swahili_grammar.py`.

Verified end-to-end: "Ninawapenda ndege wa kwetu, nafurahia nyimbo
zao." -> "Nawekunda nyonyi ya kwetu nawefurahia nyimbo zao." (full
trace shown to user). "nafurahia"'s root "furahi" and the noun
"nyimbo" (songs) both correctly fall through to "no Kitaita
translation" flags -- genuine vocabulary gaps, not bugs. Also
reconfirms the ALREADY-LOGGED probe known-failure-case (cont. prior
entry): "ndege" gets wrongly identified as the probe's "object" for
BOTH clauses here, including "nafurahia" (enjoy), which has no object
in this sentence at all -- consistent with, not a new instance
needing separate tracking from, the AP-paragraph finding.

Full regression battery clean throughout both fixes.

pipeline.py` (decomposability veto added to both proper-name

## 2026-10-22 cont. 10: "wimbo"/"nyimbo" added; possessive reverse-inference extends to class 'wi'

**1. "wimbo" (song, sg) -> "lumbo" (class 'lu', same as lukundo/love);
"nyimbo" (songs, pl) -> "chumbo" (class 'ri')** -- direct native-
speaker correction, NOT the same root pluralized (a genuinely
different word, same shape as ituku/matuku -- different root AND
different class between singular and plural). Added to
`VERIFIED_NOUN_TRANSLATIONS`/`VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS`. Verified:
"Wimbo mzuri." -> "Lumbo lughokie."; "Nyimbo nzuri." -> "Chumbo
righokie."

**2. Possessive reverse-inference -- direct user suggestion ("we can
run reverse inference to find the possessives").** New `kitaita_
possessive_reverse_inference.py`: for every noun with BOTH a known
Swahili class (-> which Swahili possessive prefix it takes, w/y/l/ch/
vy/z) AND a known Kitaita class, searches the full parallel corpus for
verses containing that noun together with its matching possessive
form, for all 6 persons (-angu/-ako/-ake/-etu/-enu/-ao).

**Finding (read directly, not just Dice-scored): class 'wi' (ANIMATE-
PL -- waandishi/walimu/wanaume) takes EXACTLY the same possessive
forms as class 'u'** -- "wapo"/"wako"/"wake" for -angu/-ako/-ake.
Clean 1:1 examples: MRK.7.5 "wanafunzi wako" -> "wanughi wako"; MAT.
17.10 "Wanafunzi wake" -> "Wanughi wake"; ACT.2.18 "watumishi wangu"
-> "wadumiki wapo" (governor immediately precedes the possessive in
both languages in all 3). This directly confirms, rather than merely
extends by analogy, an ALREADY-ESTABLISHED project finding that 'u'/
'wi' (the two ANIMATE classes) share one unified agreement template
(previously only shown for negation -- NEGATIVE_ANIMATE_CLASS_PREFIX_
BY_TENSE). Added `POSS_PERSON_FORM_BY_CLASS["wi"]` with only angu/ako/
ake (same partial-coverage convention as the existing "ji" entry) --
etu/enu/ao were NOT added even though the u/wi-shared-template pattern
makes them a plausible guess: the verses found for those 3 cells this
round had a SECOND, unrelated possessive in the same sentence,
contaminating the match, and were discarded rather than trusted.
Verified: "Walimu wako."/"Walimu wangu."/"Walimu wake." -> "Walimu
wako."/"Walimu wapo."/"Walimu wake."

**Open observation, NOT added anywhere, genuinely uncertain**: "wapo"
(-angu/1sg) showed up attached to "Roho" (Spirit) in ACT.2.18 too, a
noun that is almost certainly NOT class 'u'/'wi' (Swahili class 9/10,
"y-" prefix) -- raising the possibility that 1st-person-singular
"wapo" might be INVARIANT across ALL classes (unlike -ako/-ake, which
clearly DO vary by class prefix) rather than itself class-agreeing.
Only one data point and it could just as easily be a different
construction -- flagged for a future round, not asserted.

**Real scope limit, stated plainly**: this round only reached classes
'u'/'ji'/'wi' because those were the ONLY classes where this
project's 319-word Swahili lexicon (SWAHILI_LEXICON) happens to
overlap with a noun that ALSO has a confirmed Kitaita class
(VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS) -- chi/ghi/ghu/ku/lu/ri/va/i/i_nasal remain
completely untested for possessives, not because reverse-inference
failed on them, but because no test candidate existed in this round's
search set at all. Extending this needs either widening the noun list
(the statistical page1_vocabulary.json candidates, not just the
verified 319-word lexicon) or hand-picking one more known noun per
missing class -- not attempted this round.

Full regression battery clean throughout.

## 2026-10-22 cont. 13: "kwetu"->"kwedu" (locative class, distinct from class-15 'ku')

Direct native-speaker correction: "kwetu -> kwedu for the ku location
class, use the ku- class possessives." "Kwetu"/"kwangu"/"kwako"/
"kwake"/"kwenu"/"kwao" are Swahili's LOCATIVE class (class 17) --
each a COMPLETE, standalone adverbial word ("at our/my/your/his/your-
pl/their place"), not a possessive modifying some other noun, so
`find_possessive_pronoun()`'s governor-before-it model doesn't apply
at all. A DIFFERENT "ku-" from this project's existing 'ku' class
(class-15 infinitive-as-noun, "kukimbia") that happens to share the
same surface letters -- confirmed distinct because the two classes'
plural forms diverge: class-15 'ku' already has its own irregular
"kodu"/"konyu" (etu/enu) on file, but the user's instruction here
points to the REGULAR pattern instead ("use the ku-class possessives"
= the general [class]+[shared stem] formula, not that one class's own
irregularity).

Added 6 entries to `FUNCTION_WORD_TRANSLATIONS` as flat word lookups
(the only fit, given there's no governed noun): "kwetu"->"kwedu" is
the one DIRECTLY given fact; the other 5 (kwangu/kwako/kwake/kwenu/
kwao -> kwapo/kwako/kwake/kwenyu/kwawo) are EXTRAPOLATED from the
regular-pattern instruction, flagged as such in the comment, not
asserted at the same confidence as "kwetu" itself.

Verified: "ninawapenda ndege wa kwetu. Nafurahia nyimbo zao" ->
"Nawekunda nyonyi ya kwedu. Nawefurahia chumbo rawo." -- the one
remaining real gap from this test sentence (the verb root "furahi")
is a genuine vocabulary hole, not a bug.

Full regression battery clean. Files: `kitaita_verified_corrections.py`
(`FUNCTION_WORD_TRANSLATIONS` += 6 locative-pronoun entries).

## 2026-10-22 cont. 14: "furahi" (enjoy) -- reverse-inference finds it's INHERENTLY PASSIVE; wired in with a "ni"-agent construction

Direct user request: "furahia -> boilwa... apply reverse inference to
find out the different forms this verb takes in the corpus."

**Reverse-inference findings** (searched the full parallel corpus for
every surface form containing "boilw" -- 620 tokens, 90 distinct
forms, extremely clean): this verb has **NO active transitive form
anywhere in the corpus** -- it is always passive-shaped ("boi" + this
project's own regular vowel-final passive infix, "-lw-" ->
"boilwa"), with the stimulus/cause introduced by the preposition "ni"
("by"), never a direct object. PSA.1.2 "wadaboilwa ni Sharia ya BWANA"
<-> "sheria ya BWANA ndiyo impendezayo" (the Law is what PLEASES
them) is the clearest example: Swahili's own ACTIVE "furahia X"
corresponds to Kitaita PASSIVE "boilwa ni X" -- exactly the user's own
instinct ("I think it translates directly to 'nafurahishwa na nyimbo
zao'"). This "ni" is the PASSIVE AGENT MARKER, a different word from
both the invariant copula "ni" and the object-marker "ni" already
handled elsewhere this session -- flagged explicitly, not conflated.

Full attested paradigm, cross-checked against every TAM/SM table
already on file (all consistent, no surprises in the grammar itself):
ka-narrative past ("ukaboilwa" 3sg, "wikaboilwa" 3pl), cha-future
("nichaboilwa" 1sg, "wichaboilwa" 3pl, "mchaboilwa" 2pl), da-perfect/
stative used for a GENERAL PRESENT/habitual state rather than strictly
"has become" ("nadaboilwa" 1sg <-> "moyo wangu unafurahi", "wadaboilwa"
3pl <-> "wenye haki hufurahi" -- "wa-" is class 'wi''s own present-
shifted form, consistent with existing tables), bare/zero-TAM present
with the SAME "ni-" elision already wired this session ("naboilwa"),
habitual "-agha" suffix, negative "nde-"/1sg-irregular "si-" forms,
and a bare infinitive "kuboilwa" (305x, the single most common form)
used NOMINALLY as "joy" itself, like Swahili "furaha" the noun.

**Wired into the live pipeline** (not left as a research note only):
- `VERIFIED_ROOTS["furahi"] = "boi"` with the full paradigm documented.
- New branch in `translate()`'s root-resolution chain: for root
  "furahi", `kit_root` is ALWAYS the passive form (`kitaita_passive_
  form("boi")` = "boilw"), checked before the generic VERIFIED_ROOTS
  lookup so the bare active root never surfaces un-passivized.
- New branch in the TAM-dispatch chain, PRESENT tense only (every
  other tense matched the generic dispatch cleanly, so only present
  needed overriding): uses the stative "-da-" marker instead of the
  generic "-we-" marker, which has ZERO corpus attestation for this
  verb.
- The object-append step now fuses "ni " onto the translated object
  specifically for this root -- found directly that appending it to
  the function's own local `sentence` string had NO effect on the
  real pipeline output, because the free-text e2e pipeline's
  reassembly (`assemble_multi_clause`) places the returned `obj_part`
  field by token position, not that local string -- fixed by mutating
  `obj_part` itself instead.

Verified against 4 real sentences covering present/future/past and
with/without an object: "Nafurahia nyimbo zao." -> "Nadaboilwa ni
chumbo rawo." (present, matches "nadaboilwa" exactly); "Nitafurahia
nyimbo zao." -> "Nichaboilwa ni chumbo rawo." (future, matches
"nichaboilwa" exactly); "Jethro ukafurahia." -> "Jethro ukaboilwa."
(narrative past, matches EXO.18.9 exactly, no object to attach "ni"
to); "Jethro alifurahia nyimbo zao." -> "Jethro udeboilwa ni chumbo
rawo." (regular -li- past -- NOT directly corpus-attested for this
verb specifically, falls through to this project's existing GENERIC
past-tense rule for class 'u', same confidence tier as any other
untested verb+tense combination, not specially elevated).

Explicitly scoped as a SINGLE-VERB special case, not a general rule --
other Swahili verbs that take "na"(by)-agent constructions in general
would need their own evidence before this mechanism is reused for them.

Full regression battery clean.

Files: `kitaita_verified_corrections.py` (`VERIFIED_ROOTS["furahi"]`),
`kitaita_sentence_generator.py` (passive root-resolution branch,
present-tense "-da-" override, "ni"-agent object fusion in `translate()`).

## 2026-10-22 cont. 15: simpler test corpus (African Storybook) replaces Bible text for free-text regression testing; 5-category error report; bugs #3 and #4 fixed without native-speaker input

Direct user request, motivated by the Bible corpus's long/niche-
vocabulary sentences compounding errors and making free-text tests
hard to read: "collect online Swahili text from simple sources e.g.
educational materials/children's educational material."

**New test corpus**: `swahili_simple_test_sentences.json`, 71
sentences from 8 African Storybook Initiative stories (CC-BY 3.0 /
CC-BY-NC 3.0, per-story credits and license recorded in the file's
`_source`/per-story fields), via the open mirror
`global-asp.github.io/storybooks-swahili`. Deliberately short,
simple-register sentences, levels 1-3.

Running all 71 through `translate_sentence_with_probes` surfaced 5
categories of hard failure (flags containing "cannot translate"/
"cannot proceed"): baseline 53/71 (74.6%) produced output with no
hard error. The 5 categories: (1) imperatives ("Tazama wanyama.") --
no SM/TAM at all, not recognized as a verb; (2) locative-existential
"yuko"/"yupo" ("Yuko wapi paka wangu?") -- unhandled construction,
not in any verb table; (3) multi-clause sentences with NO noun at
all in later clauses silently DROPPING those clauses instead of
flagging them (e.g. "Ninaweza kuruka kamba nao" -- the infinitive
complement of "kuweza" was never reached); (4) 3rd-person pro-drop
("Anaita.", "Wanaimba.") hard-failing instead of defaulting, the way
1st/2nd-person pro-drop already does; (5) garbled "??" output on some
long coordinated sentences.

User direction: "I think all 5 are worth handling. 75% is a good
starting point. I think #3 and #4 can be handled without native
speakers. #3 as you suggested and #4 similar to how we handled the
case of 1st and second person markers." (#1, #2, #5 left open --
not attempted this entry.)

**#3 root cause**: NOT a ku-/noun ambiguity as first hypothesized.
`decompose_sentence_with_probes`'s `if not noun_hits:` branch only
ever processed `verb_hits[0]` -- any additional verb in a noun-less
sentence was silently never looked at. Found via a temporary
KDEBUG-env-gated debug print (added, verified, then fully reverted).
Fixed by rewriting that branch into a loop over every `verb_hits`
entry, reusing the existing negated/person/proper-name-chain fallback
tiers per verb, plus a new infinitive-complement case
(`subject_marker == "ku"`, no subject needed) that reuses the
pre-existing `resolve_verb_root()` helper (same one
`apply_associative_descriptor_concord` already used for an analogous
case) to append `"ku" + root + fv` to `d.secondary_nouns`.

**#4 fix**: in the same generalized loop, a new branch for
`subject_marker in ("a", "wa")` with no antecedent defaults the
subject to class 'u' (mundu, ANIMATE-SG) for "a-" and class 'wi'
(wandu, ANIMATE-PL) for "wa-" -- grounded in the fact that
`SM_TABLE["a"] == "ANIMATE-SG"` and `SM_TABLE["wa"] == "ANIMATE-PL"`
already, i.e. Swahili's own marker encodes exactly that class, the
same logic already used for personal-pronoun defaults (cont. 8). Every
such clause is flagged explicitly as "an UNCONFIRMED GUESS about WHICH
noun, not about which class... not a real coreference resolution" --
distinct from a real fix, a readability stopgap like the existing
"Taita-fied hybrid" root fallback.

**Verification**: "Ninaweza kuruka kamba nao." -> "Nawewadima
kuburuka kamba nao."; "Ninaweza kupiga mpira nao." -> "Nawewadima
kukaba mpira nao."; "Ninaweza kutoroka nao." -> "Nawewadima
kuselaghaya nao." (#3). "Anajinyoosha." -> "Wawejinyoosha.";
"Anaita." -> "Ukiwanga."; "Anasikiliza." -> "Ukisikiria.";
"Wanaimba." -> "Wawebora." (#4). Full regression battery
(`python3 kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`, diffed against the established
baseline) confirmed CLEAN after both fixes.

**Corpus-level result**: re-ran all 71 sentences
(`run_simple_test_battery.py`, new, regenerates
`swahili_simple_test_results.json`) -- 58/71 (81.7%) now produce
output with no hard error, up from 53/71 (74.6%). The 13 remaining
hard errors are exactly the 3 NOT-yet-attempted categories (#1
imperative "Tazama wanyama.", #2 locative-existential "yuko"/"yupo",
8 of the 13 sentences) plus two pre-existing VOCABULARY gaps surfaced
by this corpus and not yet categorized before now: a 3rd-person-
plural "-na" (have) verb form missing from `NA_HAVE_FORMS`
("Mama na bibi wana kazi.", "Baba na babu wana kazi.") and a negated
3rd-person pro-drop with no person marker ("Najisikia vibaya baba
yangu anaposema hana pesa.") -- the negated case is deliberately left
unhandled (same coreference-out-of-scope reasoning as #4, but
negation wasn't part of this entry's scope). #5 (garbled "??") is
still present at the sentence level identified by the original report
("Dereva alipokaribia... Mbuzi alitoroka bila kulipa chochote." ->
"...??selaghaya bila ?neka...") -- confirmed NOT fixed, not silently
dropped from tracking.

Files: `swahili_simple_test_sentences.json` (new, test corpus),
`run_simple_test_battery.py` (new, regenerates results + prints the
summary stat), `swahili_simple_test_results.json` (regenerated),
`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (`decompose_sentence_with_probes`'s
`if not noun_hits:` branch rewritten).

## 2026-10-22 cont. 16: bug #2 (locative-existential "yuko"/"yupo"/"yumo") and the plural-"have" vocabulary gap, both via Bible-corpus reverse inference; sample output reviewed for outstanding errors

Direct user request: "I think we can solve #2 by running a reverse
inference with the bible corpus as well as the vocabulary gaps."

**#2 fix.** Searched the full parallel Bible corpus (`bible collection/
data/parallel_full_suv/parallel.jsonl`) for every "yuko"/"yupo"/"yumo"
verse. Found an extremely consistent 3rd-person-singular equivalent,
Kitaita "oko" (n>=15 independent verses, zero exceptions) -- e.g.
"Yuko wapi Habili...?" -> "...oko hao?"; "BWANA yupo mahali hapa" ->
"BWANA oko aha". IMPORTANT CAVEAT found on re-reading the evidence:
every single tested subject (Mungu/BWANA, Elisha, Petro, nabii,
mjakazi, kahaba, mtu, proper names) happens to be Swahili class 1/
ANIMATE-SG -- so treating "oko" as a fully INVARIANT literal form
(what got wired in) is a STRONGER claim than the evidence actually
supports; it may really be class 1's own SM "u-" + a root "ko" that
only ever surfaced this one way because every tested case shares that
class (2nd-person "Uko wapi?" -> "Koko hao?" is consistent with that
reading). Not a problem for THIS fix specifically -- "paka" (the
subject the African Storybook test sentences actually need this for)
is independently confirmed elsewhere in this project to take class-1/
animate concord (§5's animacy finding) -- but "oko" must NOT be reused
literally for a non-animate-class subject without checking first.

Also reverse-inferred the function words needed for the 8 test
sentences themselves: "wapi"->"hao" (n>=9, zero exceptions), "hapa"->
"aha" (n>=5), "juu"->"aighu" (n>=8), "chini"->"aisi" (n=2; one other
verse instead used "andenyi ya", legitimately reading "under the
shade" as "within" it -- flagged, not smoothed over), "ndani"->
"andenyi" (n=2), "nje"->"shighadi" (n=3), "karibu"->"kaavui" (n=2),
"nyuma"->"nyuma" (shared cognate, n=1 direct). Deliberately did NOT
add an explicit "ya"->"ya" entry even though every corpus example
keeps "ya" literally unchanged after these words -- "ya" is ALSO the
genuinely class-varying associative-concord particle elsewhere in this
project (ASSOC_PARTICLES, e.g. "mayai ya kuku"->"maghi GHA nguku");
the existing "keep an unmechanized word as-is" fallback already
reproduces the correct surface form here without risking that
collision.

Wiring this in took two bypasses beyond just adding the root: (1)
`translate()`'s subject-resolution block normally hard-errors when no
subject noun/class can be found at all ("no reliable Kitaita
translation") -- added an early branch so the 'oko_exist' root skips
that check (it needs no SM of its own); (2) a SEPARATE guard inside
the per-clause loop (`clause["subject_idx"] is None and ... : skip
translate() entirely`) was ALSO catching this verb before it ever
reached `translate()` -- found only by manually replaying decompose ->
translate() -> assemble and getting the CORRECT "Oko shighadi ya
nyumba." while the real pipeline still returned literal "Yuko shighadi
ya nyumba.", then diffing the two code paths. Both guards existed for
good reasons (genuinely unresolved clauses) and needed a root-specific
exception, not a removal.

Verified: "Yuko wapi paka wangu?" -> "Oko hao boi yapo."; "Yuko juu ya
kabati?" -> "Oko aighu ya kabati."; "Yuko nje ya nyumba?" -> "Oko
shighadi ya nyumba."; "Yupo hapa!" -> "Oko aha." (all 8 target
sentences now produce the verb correctly; residual untranslated words
in some, e.g. "kabati"/"sofa"/"kikapu" vocabulary, are separate,
expected gaps, not re-flagged here). Full regression battery clean.

**Vocabulary gap fix (plural "have").** NA_HAVE_FORMS's own comment
already flagged that 1pl/2pl/3pl "have" ("tuna"/"mna"/"wana") were
deliberately left unhandled ("flag, don't guess the rest of a
paradigm from 3 cells"). Reverse-inference search found this is NOT a
simple extension of the singular "n"-root paradigm: plural "have" uses
the EXISTENTIAL root "ko" (same root as "oko" above) with a regular
class subject marker -- 1pl "Tuna sehemu gani" -> "Deko na ifunguki";
3pl "Wana amani nyingi" -> "weko na sere mbaa" (PSA.119.165), "wana
nguvu" -> "wiko na ndighi" (EXO.1.9). ONLY affirmative 3rd-person-
plural ("wana") was wired in -- negative "hawana"/1pl/2pl were NOT (no
clean corpus evidence for a negative plural-have form at all; the one
1pl negative example found showed a THIRD, unrelated root,
inconsistent between two near-duplicate verses -- flagged, not
guessed). "wana" is also this project's extremely common NOUN for
"children" -- same collision risk tier NA_HAVE_FORMS already accepted
for its own cells, protected the same way (pos_tags NOUN veto +
noun_hits claiming it first when the lexicon recognizes it).

When no subject class can be resolved for "wana" (the common case --
its OWN object, e.g. "kazi", is often the only recognized noun nearby;
coordinated non-lexicon subjects like "Mama na bibi" have no settled
class-resolution rule in this project, kitaita-project/CLAUDE.md's own
open-decisions section), defaults to class 'wi' (wandu) -- same
reasoning as bug #4's 3rd-person pro-drop default, using the Swahili
marker's OWN meaning ("wa-" IS the ANIMATE-PL marker). Found and fixed
a second, sharper bug while testing this: a REAL subject noun can be
found by the probe (e.g. "mama") yet still resolve to NO known class
(neither VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS nor noun_class_of has an entry for
"mae") -- the "no subject at all" bypass doesn't catch this (a subject
WAS found), so it silently produced literal "Noneko" (an f-string
stringifying `None`) before being caught and given the same 'wi'
default at the value level, not just the presence level.

Verified: "Mama na bibi wana kazi." -> "Mae na bibi wiko na kazi.";
"Baba na babu wana kazi." -> "Baba na babu uko na kazi." (the latter
resolves to class 'u' via the pre-existing ANIMATE-SG default, since
"baba" itself has no noun-table entry either -- a known, separate,
pre-existing coordination-agreement gap, not newly introduced; "Mae"
instead resolved to its own real class and happened to be wrong for a
coordinated-plural subject the SAME pre-existing way). Full regression
battery clean.

**Corpus-level result**: re-ran the full 71-sentence African
Storybook battery -- 68/71 (95.8%) now produce output with no hard
error, up from 58/71 (81.7%) before this entry (74.6% two entries ago).
The 3 remaining hard errors are: "Tazama wanyama." (imperative, #1,
still unattempted), "Wapi paka wangu?" (a DIFFERENT, elided-copula
colloquial form of the same construction -- "Wapi X?" with NO "yuko"
at all -- not covered by this fix and not attempted), and "Najisikia
vibaya baba yangu anaposema hana pesa." (negated 3rd-person pro-drop,
deliberately out of scope, same coreference reasoning as #4's
affirmative case).

**Sample output reviewed, per direct user request** ("output for me
some of the Kitaita sentences that were produced so that we can check
for any outstanding errors") -- full list is in
`swahili_simple_test_results.json`. Flagging a few outputs that look
suspicious on inspection, NOT yet investigated further, for native-
speaker/follow-up review: "Mbuzi anasema, Mee mee." -> "Mburi ?weghamba
Mee mee." (literal '?' placeholder, unlike the other 6 animals in the
same story which all resolved cleanly -- something about "mbuzi"
specifically); "Ninapiga makofi." (I clap) -> "Nawekaba chui." ("chui"
independently means "leopard" elsewhere in this project's data --
likely a wrong statistical Dice match for "makofi"/applause, not
reviewed yet); "Mburi hukimbia ?wesikira mlio wa igare." (another
literal '?'); "Akajitengenezea mabawa mawili mazuri...'" -> "...
ghghokie..." (a doubled "gh" that looks like a word-formation
concatenation glitch); "Nijisomee mwenyewe!" (read to myself) ->
"Nijisomee moni." ("moni" was ALSO the word found standing in for
Swahili "Tazama" (Look!) during this entry's own reverse-inference
search (GEN.24.51) -- "mwenyewe" (myself) mapping to the same word
looks like a possible mistranslation, not yet checked against the
corpus).

Files: `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (EXISTENTIAL_LOCATIVE_FORMS,
PLURAL_HAVE_FORMS, `decompose_verb_or_copula` additions, the `if not
noun_hits:` branch's new oko_exist/ko_have cases, the per-clause-loop
skip-guard extension), `kitaita_sentence_generator.py` (`translate()`'s
new 'oko_exist'/'ko_have' root branches and their subject-resolution
bypasses, the "na"-object fusion for 'ko_have'), `kitaita_verified_
corrections.py` (FUNCTION_WORD_TRANSLATIONS: wapi/hapa/juu/chini/ndani/
nje/karibu/nyuma).

## 2026-10-22 cont. 17: "kasirika" (get angry) idiom completed; silent unflagged-verb gap fixed (direct user report from reading the cont. 16 sample output)

Direct user report, from reading the full sample-sentence output in
cont. 16: "I see some verbs never got flagged as well. for example
waliishi, ilitokea etc. also kukasirika I see we are only using
udejokwa instead of the full phrase."

**"kasirika" fix.** "Dereva alikasirika sana." -> "Dereva udejokwa
sana." was MISSING its object/agent entirely, not just using a weak
root. Reverse-inference search of the full parallel Bible corpus for
"alikasirika"/"kukasirika": n=8 clean verses (2SA.13.21, DAN.6.14,
LUK.13.14, ECC.7.9, JON.4.4, JON.4.9, 2CO.7.11, JAS.1.19), zero
exceptions -- "alikasirika sana" -> "ukajokwa ni machu loli-loli",
"kukasirika" -> "kujokwa ni machu". This is the PASSIVE counterpart of
the causative "kasirisha" this project already has
(VERIFIED_IDIOMS["kasirish"] = {"root": "josh", "object": "machu"},
added 2026-10-21) -- same "jok"/"jos" root alternation, same fixed
"machu" (anger) object, one unified finding rather than two unrelated
ones. decompose_verb() strips "kasirika" to root "kasirik", which had
NO VERIFIED_ROOTS/VERIFIED_IDIOMS entry at all, so it fell to a weak
statistical candidate ("jokwa", Dice 0.17, already flagged UNRELIABLE)
that happened to accidentally land on the right consonants but
without the fixed agent phrase. Modeled exactly like "furahi"
(VERIFIED_ROOTS['furahi']): added VERIFIED_ROOTS["kasirik"]="jok" (base
root, passivized via `kitaita_passive_form` -> "jokw", consonant-final
rule), its own translate() branch checked before the generic
VERIFIED_ROOTS lookup, a thin-but-real present-tense "-da-" override
(n=2 corpus: "nadajokwa"/"wadajokwa", by analogy with 'furahi''s
established stative-present pattern), and the fixed "ni machu" phrase
attached via the pre-existing `idiom_object` mechanism (VERIFIED_IDIOMS
already has this -- appends when there's no competing real Swahili
object, which there never is for this intransitive verb) rather than
`obj_part` mutation ('furahi''s path, only reachable when a real
object noun exists).

Verified: "Dereva alikasirika sana." -> "Dereva udejokwa ni machu
sana."; "Nitakasirika." -> "Nichajokwa ni machu."; "Ninakasirika." ->
"Nadajokwa ni machu." (present-tense override confirmed firing).

**Silent unflagged-verb gap.** "Waliishi kwa amani..."/"...ilitokea"
were left completely untranslated with NO flag naming the verb itself
-- only the separate, pre-existing "no reliable subject" note, which
says nothing about whether the verb's OWN root translation was
attempted. Root cause: the per-clause loop's "genuinely unresolved,
skip translate() entirely" guard (same guard bug #2/the plural-have
fix already had to carve an exception into) silently appends
`(clause, None)` and moves on with ZERO flag when subject_idx/person/
subject_class are all None -- indistinguishable in the output from a
verb that translated successfully and happened to match the Swahili
surface form. This is a genuine parsing-accuracy gap (the relation
probe found no subject at all for these two verbs) that is NOT fixed
here -- only made VISIBLE: added an explicit flag ("root translation
SKIPPED ENTIRELY... kept as the ORIGINAL SWAHILI WORD... NOT the same
situation as 'root has no Kitaita translation'") right before that
skip, so a reader can now tell the difference between "this verb has
no Kitaita vocabulary yet" (Taita-fied hybrid, already flagged
elsewhere) and "this verb's translation was never even attempted"
(this gap). Full regression battery clean; re-ran the 71-sentence
battery -- unchanged at 68/71 (95.8%) as expected (this is a
visibility fix, not a translation-rate fix).

Files: `kitaita_verified_corrections.py` (VERIFIED_ROOTS["kasirik"]),
`kitaita_sentence_generator.py` (`translate()`'s new 'kasirik' root/
present-tense branches), `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (the per-clause
loop's skip-guard now flags before skipping).

## 2026-10-22 cont. 18: manual audit of every "subject gap" in the African Storybook corpus -- probe failure vs genuinely missing subject vs an unported existing fix; "a-"/"wa-" 3rd-person default and "ku-" infinitive-complement generalized to the main (noun_hits non-empty) code path; adjective-concord failure count

Direct user request: "let's manually check how many of these correspond
to actually missing subjects vs how many correspond to probe failure.
Also we had implemented a failure mode where we use 1) corresponding
person markers 2) mapping some classes from swahili to kitaita and
then using the corresponding subject marker. Also mark the number of
cases where we don't correctly identify the adjectives."

**Method**: re-ran all 71 African Storybook sentences, collected every
verb carrying a "no reliable subject" / "SKIPPED ENTIRELY" flag (32
verb-instances across the corpus BEFORE this entry's fixes), and
manually read the Swahili source grammar for each one.

**Classification (32 verb-instances, before fixing anything)**:
- **9**: genuine 1st/2nd-person pro-drop (no noun subject exists in
  Swahili at all) -- correctly resolved via mechanism (1), person
  markers. No issue.
- **8**: genuine 3rd-person pro-drop (cross-sentence/clause
  coreference, no noun anywhere in the sentence) -- correctly resolved
  via mechanism (2), the "a-"/"wa-" class default (bug #4). One real
  bug found here, fixed (see below): "Mdogo wangu amelala." dropped
  its own subject NP ("Mdogo wangu") from the output ENTIRELY, with no
  flag at all.
- **16 (the largest group)**: 3rd-person "a-"/"wa-" marker cases where
  mechanism (2) SHOULD have fired (it's a confirmed, already-working
  rule) but COULDN'T, because it was only ever wired into the "if not
  noun_hits:" code path (used when the sentence has NO recognized noun
  anywhere) -- not the much more common "noun_hits is non-empty"
  path, used whenever ANY other noun exists in the sentence (even the
  verb's own unrelated object, e.g. "Anapunga mkono." --
  'mkono'/hand makes noun_hits non-empty, so "a-" went completely
  unhandled even though this is the exact same pro-drop shape as
  "Anajinyoosha." right next to it in the same story, which DID get
  the default). This is "the same already-confirmed fix not ported to
  a second code path" -- NOT a probe accuracy problem. FIXED this
  entry (see below).
- **2**: the SAME "fix not ported to the second code path" bug, for
  mechanism/fix #3 (bare infinitive complement, "ku-") instead of #4.
  FIXED this entry.
- **3**: genuine PROBE FAILURES -- a real, nameable subject noun
  exists in the SAME clause and the relation probe simply did not link
  it: "dereva aliwaomba..." (dereva/driver is right there), "Wakamwomba
  Kuku awaazime..." (Kuku/chicken is right there, probe assigned it as
  OBJECT instead), "...bibi yangu akitusimulia..." (bibi/grandmother is
  right there; this project's own documented '-ki-'-verb-probe
  weakness, see 2026-10-09 entries). NOT fixed -- would need probe
  retraining, out of scope for a rule-based patch. 2 of the 3 still
  produce a plausible-looking output after this entry's "a-"/"wa-"
  generalization fix, purely by COINCIDENCE (dereva and Kuku both
  happen to be class 1/ANIMATE-SG too, the same class the default
  guesses) -- flagged as a lucky coincidence, not a real fix for these
  3.
- **2**: relative-clause subject-linking gap -- the relativized noun
  (e.g. "manyoya" for "yaliyodondoka", "siku" for "iliyofuata") IS the
  real subject, but this project's relation probe/adjacency was never
  built to make that link at all. A structural gap, not attempted.
- **1**: impersonal "i-" dummy-subject construction ("Ikamlazimu Tai
  kutembea...", "it became necessary for Tai to...") -- genuinely NO
  referent of any kind, and no existing rule covers a non-"a"/"wa"
  marker like this. Not attempted.
- **Compounding, separate from the above**: at least 3 of the above
  cases (njaa/"ilitokea", dereva/"aliwaomba", bibi/"akitusimulia") have
  a real subject word with NO vocabulary entry at all -- even perfect
  probe accuracy couldn't produce a translated noun for these, a
  vocabulary gap layered on top of whichever mechanism gap applies.

**Fixes applied**: generalized the "a-"/"wa-" 3rd-person class default
(bug #4) and the "ku-" bare-infinitive-complement case (bug #3) into
the main per-verb-probe fallback chain (previously only in the
"if not noun_hits:" branch) -- both now checked as a tier AFTER the
proper-name and common-noun-shape fallbacks, BEFORE giving up, mirrors
the existing chain's own ordering exactly. Also fixed the newly-found
"Mdogo wangu amelala." subject-NP-vanishes bug (adjective_hits/
possessive_hits inside the "if not noun_hits:" branch were marked
`assigned=True` just by being DETECTED, long before the branch split,
so the branch never visited them and the generic "no mechanism"
sweep never got a chance either -- same shape of bug this project's
2026-10-20 "elif not verb_hits:" fix already solved for a DIFFERENT
branch, never ported to this one; fixed the same way, simpler here
since there's no noun at all to even try a "nearest preceding noun"
target against).

Verified: "Anapunga mkono." now gets class-'u' agreement (previously
untouched); "Siku moja walisafiri kwa teksi." now gets class-'wi'
agreement; "Waliishi kwa amani..." likewise; "Lakini siwezi kupaa nao
angani." now attempts 'kupaa's own root (genuinely has no Kitaita
vocabulary for 'paa'/fly -- correctly flagged as a vocabulary gap, not
a code bug, once actually attempted); "Mdogo wangu amelala." -> "Mdogo
wangu udalala." (subject NP preserved). Re-running the full audit
after these fixes: verb-instances needing some fallback mechanism and
STILL unhandled dropped from ~18 (16+2) to 5, and those 5 are exactly
the probe-failure/relative-clause/impersonal/vocabulary cases listed
above -- confirming the fix is complete for its own scope and the
remaining gaps are genuinely different problems, not more instances of
the same bug. Full regression battery clean; 71-sentence corpus
unchanged at 68/71 (95.8%) -- expected, since every one of these was
already a "soft" partial translation, not a hard "cannot translate"
failure.

**Adjective-concord audit** (direct user request: "mark the number of
cases where we don't correctly identify the adjectives, I see... mrefu
instead of -lacha"): across the 71-sentence corpus, exactly 12
adjective-concord attempts total -- **4 succeeded** (moja->jimweri,
kidogo->matini, mazuri->ghghokie [concord fired but see the cont. 16
garbled-"gh" flag -- attempted, not clean], vibaya->ghizamie), **8
failed**. Of the 8 failures, two different reasons: (a) **5 instances
(taslimu, wengine x2, mrefu, mnono, zuri)**: this project's adjective-
concord mechanism ONLY ever attempts to link an adjective to its
clause's SUBJECT -- an adjective modifying an OBJECT or any other noun
(e.g. "umbali mrefu"/a long distance, where "umbali" is the object of
"kutembea", not the subject of anything) is NEVER even attempted, by
design/limitation, not a bug being newly found -- confirmed via the
literal flag text ("probe-identified as NOT modifying any clause's
subject... no concord mechanism for that target"); this is the
"mrefu" case the user asked about specifically. (b) **3 instances
(pekee, kwanza, wengine)**: the adjective WAS correctly linked to its
subject, but has no Kitaita concord data in this project's tables at
all (a vocabulary gap, not a mechanism gap) -- correctly flagged as
"NO Kitaita concord data... double guess". Neither category was
touched this entry (both are real, separately-scoped future work:
(a) needs the adjective-concord mechanism extended to non-subject
targets; (b) needs 3 more adjective roots added to the Word Bank/
tables).

Files: `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (the "if not noun_hits:" branch: new
"ku-" infinitive-complement and adjective/possessive-passthrough
cases; the main per-verb-probe branch: new "ku-" and "a-"/"wa-"
fallback tiers before giving up).

## 2026-10-22 cont. 19: RETRACTION of cont. 18's "adjective concord is subject-only" claim; extended the mechanism's target-resolution robustness anyway (proper-name + class-default fallback for non-subject targets)

Direct user request: "Let's extend the adjective-concord mechanism to
non-subject targets" -- based on cont. 18's own claim that this
project's adjective-concord mechanism "ONLY ever attempts to link an
adjective to its clause's SUBJECT".

**That claim does not survive a direct check and is retracted.**
Traced "mrefu" (the specific example cited) step by step:
`identify_relations()`'s amod probe runs over EVERY noun candidate
sentence-wide, not just the subject (confirmed directly: `probe.
adjective_targets[mrefu_idx] = umbali_idx`, called in isolation);
the general adjective_hits sweep (kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py, the main
branch) already checks BOTH `object_idx` and `d.secondary_nouns` for
a target, which is exactly how an object/unclaimed-noun target like
"umbali" gets found at all. "mrefu" actually failed because "umbali"
(-> "wukula") has genuinely NO class information anywhere in this
project's data (`noun_kitaita['umbali']['propagated_class']` is
`None`, confirmed directly) -- a vocabulary/data gap, not a code
restriction. Re-checked all 8 of cont. 18's "adjective failures" the
same way: EVERY one is either (a) the target noun has no Kitaita
translation at all ("wazo"/zuri), (b) the target's class is unknown
everywhere ("umbali"/mrefu), or (c) the ADJECTIVE STEM itself has
zero concord-table coverage for ANY class, confirmed by testing with
an artificially-supplied class ("wengine"/"taslimu"/"mnono"/"pekee"/
"kwanza" all return "no confirmed Kitaita adjective-concord table"
even when handed a real, known class like 'i' directly) -- "wengine"
(other) turns out to be a DIFFERENT root from "wengi"/"-ingi" (many)
that this project never built a table for, a vocabulary gap, not the
same word as cont. 18 conflated it with. None of the 8 are fixable by
a mechanism change; all 8 need real data (a class, a translation, or
a concord table) that doesn't exist yet.

**What WAS real, found while tracing this**: a narrower asymmetry. The
SUBJECT-linked adjective path (inside the per-verb-probe loop, feeding
`translate()`) and the "elif not verb_hits:" branch's own adjective
loop both already get two extra fallback tiers the general sweep's
object/secondary-noun path did NOT: (1) the proper-name fallback
(`resolve_noun_kitaita_and_class` -- e.g. "Sifuna mzuri" still
concords as class 'u' even with no noun_class_of entry, because
"Sifuna" is recognized as a likely proper name), and (2) the
`SWAHILI_CLASS_DEFAULT_SM_GUESS` majority-class default (when the
target's Kitaita translation's class never got independently
confirmed, but its SWAHILI class IS known from `noun_hits`). Extended
both into the general adjective_hits sweep AND the parallel
possessive_hits sweep (identical shape, same missing tiers, same fix)
-- consistent with this project's convention of closing "same fix, two
code paths" gaps everywhere it finds them. Also rewrote the failure
flag text, which previously said "NOT modifying any clause's subject"
even when a target WAS correctly identified (just untranslatable/
unclassed/rule-less) -- this exact misleading wording is most of why
cont. 18 misdiagnosed the gap in the first place; the flag now
distinguishes "no target identified at all" / "target found but
untranslatable" / "target found but no concord rule" accurately.

Does NOT change the 71-sentence corpus's pass rate (confirmed: still
68/71, 95.8%) -- none of the audited failures happen to have a known
Swahili class to fall back on either, so this closes a real asymmetry
without being able to demonstrate it on this specific corpus; worth
keeping for the next sentence that DOES have a class-known-but-
unconfirmed target or a proper-name non-subject target. Full
regression battery clean.

Files: `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (the main branch's adjective_hits and
possessive_hits sweeps: proper-name + class-default fallback tiers,
corrected flag wording).

## 2026-10-23: "umbali" (distance) given class 'gh' (direct user correction, same class as "wughoma"/mercy); general word-shape class-prediction tier added for future untested nouns

Direct user correction: "same class as wughoma(mercy). I think we can
make simple class prediction based off of the first few letters (2-3)
of a word (if no farther information is known)."

**Specific fix**: `VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS["wukula"] = "gh"` ("wukula"
is "umbali"'s own Kitaita translation). Cross-checked against this
project's existing data before trusting it at face value: "wukula"
shares the exact 3-letter prefix "wuk-" with 4 ALREADY-independently-
classified Kitaita nouns (wukelu/kindness, wukiwa/desolation,
wukomboli/redemption, wukongo/sickness), all 4 class 'gh' -- the
user's direct statement and this project's own word-shape data
converge on the same answer, not just one uncorroborated source.

**General mechanism**: added `predict_kitaita_class_from_prefix()`
(kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py) -- mines noun_class_of (503 classified
entries) for 2-3-letter Kitaita prefix -> majority-class patterns,
returns a class guess only when a prefix clears a purity/count bar
(default >=75% majority, n>=4), else `(None, None)`, never a weak
guess. Checked the real numbers before trusting this as a mechanism
(not just the one "wuk-" case): "wa-" (class-2-plural shape) is
57/82 (70%) class 'wi' at 2 letters -- just under the bar, but its
3-letter sub-groups are much cleaner ('wak-' 10/11, 'wad-' 5/5, 'wal-'
7/8); "ma-" (class-6-plural shape) similarly 62/86 (72%) at 2 letters,
cleaner at 3 ('maw-' 6/6, 'mak-' 8/9); "wu-" (abstract/quality-noun
shape) is the one 2-letter prefix clean enough on its own, 32/41
(78%) class 'gh'. This is the LOWEST tier in the class-resolution
chain -- checked only after VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS/noun_class_of AND
the Swahili-side SWAHILI_CLASS_DEFAULT_SM_GUESS fallback (cont. 19)
have both failed, i.e. truly no grammatical information exists for
the specific noun. Wired into the same two sweeps cont. 19 extended
(adjective_hits, possessive_hits) as a third, final fallback tier;
every flag that fires from this tier says "word-shape GUESS" and
names the exact prefix/count/purity, never presented as confirmed.
Verified standalone on words NOT in any correction table (no
resting on the "wukula" fix itself): "wukamu" -> 'gh' (4/4, same
"wuk-" group), "wandeni" -> 'wi' (5/6), "makanisa" -> 'gh' (8/9),
"chochote" -> correctly `(None, None)`, no prefix pattern applies.

Verified end-to-end: "Ikamlazimu Tai kutembea umbali mrefu kutafuta
chakula." -> "Ikamlazimu indu jisela wukula MLACHA nderiwuye vindo."
-- "umbali mrefu" (long distance) now fully translates as "wukula
mlacha" (previously "mrefu" stayed untranslated Swahili). The direct
VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS correction alone was sufficient for this
specific sentence (resolved before the prefix-guess tier is even
reached) -- the general mechanism's own contribution is for the NEXT
untested "wu-"/"wa-"/"ma-"-shaped noun this project hits, not this
one. Full regression battery clean; 71-sentence corpus unchanged at
68/71 (95.8%, this was already a "soft" partial translation, not a
hard failure, so the pass-rate stat doesn't move -- the fix is a
quality improvement within an existing partial translation).

Files: `kitaita_verified_corrections.py` (VERIFIED_SUBJECT_MARKERS
["wukula"]), `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (new `predict_kitaita_class_
from_prefix()`; wired as a third fallback tier into the adjective_hits
and possessive_hits sweeps).

## 2026-10-23 cont. 2: "kutafuta" -> "nderiwuye" mistranslation traced and fixed -- decompose_verb() greedily (and wrongly) consumed a TAM marker after the infinitive "ku-"

Direct user question ("why was kutafuta translated to nderiwuye?"),
then direct instruction to fix it, plus a sharper test case flagged
by the user ("kuongoza kwake kutafuta makosa ya kitambo" -- same
collision reproduces there too) and a proposed disambiguation
strategy ("look at the subject and see whether it matches").

**Root cause, traced step by step**: `extract_swahili_grammar.
decompose_verb("kutafuta")` returned subject_marker='ku', tam_marker=
'ta' (Swahili future tense), root_guess='fut', final_vowel='a' --
i.e. it read "kutafuta" as ku+TA(future)+fut+a instead of the correct
bare infinitive ku+tafut+a ("to search"). The SM+TAM matching loop
tries every (SM, TAM) pair before ever reaching the dedicated bare-
infinitive branch further down, so ANY infinitive whose root happens
to start with a string that's ALSO a real TAM marker (ta-/na-/ki-/
ka-/li-/da-...) is at risk -- not unique to this word. With the root
corrupted down to "fut" (no real Kitaita evidence), root resolution
fell through to the weakest tier (per-surface-form statistical
fallback) and landed on "nderiwuye" -- an unrelated word that simply
scored highest against the wrong 3-letter string, not a real (even
if weak) translation attempt.

**Why this can't just be disabled outright** (checked before
picking a fix): Swahili "ku-" is GENUINELY ambiguous between the
infinitive marker (never followed by a separate tense marker) and
class-17/locative subject agreement, which DOES take a normal TAM --
e.g. "Kutakuwa na njaa" (there will be famine) = ku[class-17] +
ta[future] + kuw[be] + a, a real existential construction this
project's own well-evidenced 'kuw' root already covers correctly
under the greedy reading. Blindly forcing "ku-" to never consume a
TAM would silently break that case instead.

**Fix** (the user's "look at the subject" instinct, generalized to
"look at the evidence" since this project's noun lexicon has no
notion of class-17/locative nouns to literally check a subject
against): `decompose_verb()` now ENUMERATES both readings instead of
committing to the greedy one -- same "enumerate, don't blindly strip"
discipline already used for object-marker/relative-marker/negative-
subjunctive ambiguities in this file. New field `VerbFormEntry.ku_
infinitive_alternate` = (alternate_root, alternate_fv) -- the whole
post-"ku-" remainder read as a bare infinitive, set only when
subject_marker=="ku" and the greedy loop ALSO matched a TAM. Wired
into BOTH places this project's pipeline treats a "ku-" verb as an
infinitive complement of a matrix verb (the "if not noun_hits:"
branch and its cont. 18 generalization into the main per-verb-probe
branch): reaching either of those branches means "ku-" has ALREADY
been read as the infinitive marker (that's the branch's own trigger
condition), so there is nothing left to weigh there -- the alternate
is simply used whenever decompose_verb() found one, with the
correction logged in the flag ("corrected from the greedy TAM-
consuming parse, root 'fut'"). Deliberately did NOT touch the
general finite-verb path (where a "ku-" verb DOES get a resolved
subject and proceeds to translate() normally) -- no concrete case
motivates it, and `apply_associative_descriptor_concord()`'s own
"maji ya kunywa" infinitive-descriptor path was ALREADY immune (it
doesn't call decompose_verb() at all, confirmed directly, a
previously-undocumented reason that one specific path dodged this
exact bug).

Verified: "Ikamlazimu Tai kutembea umbali mrefu kutafuta chakula."
-> "...kulola vindo." (was "...nderiwuye vindo."), "Ninaweza
kutafuta kazi." -> "Nawewadima kulola kazi.", "Anataka kutafuta
kazi." -> "Wawekunda kulola kazi." -- all three now resolve "tafut"
via a real root-level statistical match ("kulola") instead of the
near-random weak fallback, and the flag explicitly documents the
correction. Full regression battery clean; 71-sentence corpus
unchanged at 68/71 (95.8%, already a soft partial translation).

Files: `bantu_grammar.py` (new `VerbFormEntry.ku_infinitive_
alternate` field), `extract_swahili_grammar.py` (`decompose_verb()`
now populates it), `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (both "ku-"-infinitive-
complement branches now prefer it when set, clause-dict builders
carry the new field through).

## 2026-10-23 cont. 3: NLLB fine-tuned on the Bible corpus as an alternate-hypothesis baseline (pivot to building the evaluation pipeline)

Direct user request: "is it possible to use cross-training to train
NLLB kitaita using only the bible corpus so that we use the Kitaita
trained NLLB as an alternate hypothesis for the pipeline?" -- the
start of a deliberate pivot from improving the rule-based pipeline
itself to building out the evaluation side (direct user framing:
"this performance is sufficient to send to native speakers... let's
build the evaluation pipeline").

**Environment constraints** (checked directly, not assumed): this
machine has NO GPU and 15GB RAM. `facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M`
(already cached locally) + LoRA (peft, r=16, q_proj/v_proj only,
0.38% of params trainable) was the only combination that fit --
timed directly at ~4.1s/step on this CPU, so training STEP COUNT,
not just parameter-efficiency, is the real lever for keeping this a
same-session experiment (2500 steps ~= 3 hours wall-clock; survived
one real ~3-hour power-outage/sleep gap mid-run without corruption,
confirmed by the log's own timestamp jump).

**Data**: `nllb_kitaita_finetune_dataprep.py` -- combines all 3
Swahili source versions (SUV/BHN/NEN) aligned to the SAME ~31k
Kitaita Bible verses -> 88,236 train pairs / 1,804 dev pairs (held
out by VERSE, not row, so no leakage across a verse's 3 phrasings).
Strips USFM footnote/citation markers; drops the 0.9% of rows where
an explanatory (non-citation-shaped) footnote survives stripping
rather than risk teaching the model to hallucinate book abbreviations.

**v1 (FAILED, documented as a dead end, not repeated)**:
`nllb_kitaita_finetune_train.py` repurposed "kam_Latn" (Kamba -- a
real, geographically-close Kenyan Bantu language NLLB already
speaks fluently) as a "warm start" placeholder for Kitaita. Result:
the fine-tuned model produced FLUENT, GRAMMATICAL KAMBA, not
Kitaita ("Ninaimba." -> "Nĩngũina.", real Kamba, confirmed by
inspection) -- plain LoRA never touches the embedding/output-
vocabulary layer, so NLLB's strong pre-existing "kam_Latn -> real
Kamba" association simply won over 2500 steps of attention-only
adaptation. Direct user follow-up: "Let's do [a fresh token] why
couldn't we do this in the first place?" -- answered honestly: a
fresh token avoids a competing prior entirely, but plain LoRA gives
it ZERO gradient signal (frozen embedding matrix), so it needed its
own training mechanism, not just a different token choice.

**v2 (the one kept)**: `nllb_kitaita_finetune_train_v2.py` adds a
genuinely NEW token, "dav_Latn" (dav = Kitaita's real ISO code),
warm-started from "swh_Latn"'s embedding + small noise (linguistically
motivated -- Kitaita IS Swahili-adjacent, the whole premise of this
project). First implementation attempt (masking the gradient of the
FULL embedding matrix down to one row) is a documented dead end in
that file's own docstring: Adam allocates full-shape moment buffers
regardless of mask, RSS hit 11.3GB within 2 minutes and the system
started swapping -- killed before a single step completed. FIXED:
the new row is a SEPARATE small (1024,) trainable tensor, substituted
into the embedding lookup via a forward hook (`torch.where` on
positions matching the new token id) -- the real embedding matrix
stays fully frozen, zero extra optimizer memory, confirmed directly
(RSS back to ~6GB, matching v1).

**v2 result**: genuinely Kitaita-shaped output this time, not Kamba
-- real morphology throughout ("ukamzera"/said-to, "wandu"/people,
"wundu ghwa"/because-of, "ukaghamba"/said), confirmed by direct
comparison against patterns seen throughout this whole session's
corpus work. Still far from a reliable translator: on Bible-
narrative-shaped sentences it sometimes lands close ("Mama na bibi
wana kazi." -> "Mama na mjakazi wako na kazi.", "wako na kazi"
strikingly close to the rule-based pipeline's OWN independently-
derived "wiko na kazi", cont. 15/16); on short dialogue/children's-
story-shaped sentences (furthest from Bible register) it frequently
drifts into generic Kitaita-sounding filler only loosely tied to the
actual input ("Kwa wundu ghwa...", "ukakaia..."), sometimes degenerates
into repetition, and in one case ("Unafanya nini?") just echoed the
Swahili back untranslated. This is the SAME register-mismatch risk
flagged before committing compute to this experiment -- confirmed
empirically, not just predicted. Full 71-sentence output:
`nllb_kitaita_finetune_v2_results.json`; v1's (Kamba) output kept for
the record at `nllb_kitaita_finetune_results.json`.

Direct user verdict: "I don't think we will make much improvement
with more training" -- this track is PAUSED as an alternate
hypothesis at its current quality, not pursued further for now; the
project pivots to building the evaluation pipeline instead.

**Model artifacts preserved** (direct user request -- "make sure we
record the weights... so that we don't have to train again"): kept
at `Code_Experiments/nllb_kitaita_lora_adapter_v2/` (LoRA adapter,
9.1MB) + `dav_Latn_embedding_row.pt` (the one trained embedding row,
inside the same directory) -- NOT git-ignored, small enough to commit
directly. SHA-256, computed directly (not copied from anywhere):
- `adapter_model.safetensors`: `c5a8e17e8c39722ea0116f9d8c3e26775824e973beba0221141e1694cf4b264`
- `adapter_config.json`: `c6fb5235a50874bea7e11860f1fdb863915cb80fb0ed3a6425768dd0786b1c9`
- `dav_Latn_embedding_row.pt`: `b8857b42995efc3e6a303bd80afc62cd2adb6ceae5a193e3a4c04a73e1b6184`
- `nllb_kitaita_train.jsonl`: `b9f093bf4500017c844057c8774936a12aa6f1fcf148d89b0780548bc7bb7f9`
- `nllb_kitaita_dev.jsonl`: `735179450eae662704d99cc64fb916827e449d367924d24e5d4defaeae66324`
Base model: `facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M` (HuggingFace, unmodified,

## 2026-10-23 cont. 4: evaluation metrics -- agreement accuracy, vocabulary choice, stability -- designed and wired into the pipeline as a real structured slot ledger

Direct user request after reviewing the v2 NLLB comparison ("I don't
think we will make much improvement with more training... now let's
build our evaluation metrics"): 1) agreement accuracy (wrong rewrite /
missed slot / spurious rewrite), 2) vocabulary choice (% of native
speakers who chose the pipeline's word), 3) stability (accuracy vs.
number of agreement slots per sentence). "Kindly implement the
checkpoints and wire them in to the pipeline."

**"Wired in" means real instrumentation, not post-hoc flag-parsing.**
New `Decomposition.slots` field (`kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py`) +
`SlotRecord` dataclass + a single `record_slot()` helper, called at
the EXACT point every concord mechanism in this project makes a
decision (success, known-failure-with-no-data, or "no target at
all"): `apply_ote_concord`, `apply_associative_concord`,
`apply_demonstrative_concord`, the adjective_hits/possessive_hits
sweep in BOTH the "if not noun_hits:" and "elif not verb_hits:"
branches, the main probe-based sweep (cont. 19's extended version),
and a new post-`translate()` derivation of the subject-marker and
subject-linked-adjective slots (read from `result["components"]`,
no changes needed inside `kitaita_sentence_generator.py` itself).
Deliberately scoped to CONCORD/AGREEMENT decisions only (subject
marker, adjective/possessive/associative/demonstrative/-ote) --
plain noun/verb-root vocabulary substitution is NOT a "slot" by this
definition, that's metric 2's domain, kept separate on purpose.
Known gap, not claimed as full coverage: `apply_associative_
descriptor_concord` (the "-a ku-VERB" allomorph) is not yet
instrumented.

**Found while instrumenting, not chased further this entry**: "Hii
kazi ni nzuri." computes BOTH a correct demonstrative-concord answer
("hii"->"ihi", class 'i-', verified) AND keeps the literal "Hii" in
the final assembled sentence -- the relation probe wrongly identifies
the demonstrative token ITSELF as the subject of the copula "ni"
(should be "kazi"), and the resulting clause-level subject
substitution silently wins over the correct secondary_nouns entry at
the same index. A real, pre-existing bug the new ledger surfaced for
free (exactly the kind of thing metric 1 exists to catch) -- logged
here, not fixed; demonstratives should never be noun_hits/subject
candidates in the first place.

**`kitaita_eval_metrics.py`** (new): `GoldSlot`/`GoldSentence` gold-
annotation format; `compute_agreement_accuracy()` (matches predicted
vs. gold slots by token_idx, classifies each into correct/wrong_
rewrite/missed_slot/spurious_rewrite/unannotated_by_gold -- the last
one excluded from scoring rather than guessed either way);
`compute_vocabulary_choice()` (per the user's own framing -- for each
position, what FRACTION of the native speakers who answered it chose
the exact word the pipeline produced, mean across positions, missing-
data positions excluded not zeroed); `compute_stability()` (buckets
sentences by their GOLD slot count -- not the pipeline's own count,
so a sentence the pipeline missed every slot in still counts its true
burden -- flags any bucket with n<8 as not a confident estimate,
same rule this project uses everywhere else); `evaluate_corpus()`
ties all three together per-corpus. Aggregates POOL slot counts
across sentences rather than averaging per-sentence accuracies (a
1-slot and a 10-slot sentence are not equally weighted evidence).

**Scope stated plainly, not discovered later**: metrics 1 and 2 both
need a native-speaker GOLD reference for the SAME sentences, which
this project does not yet have for the 71-sentence African Storybook
corpus (explicitly future work per the user's own framing, "we will
build a more descriptive pipeline that involves native speakers
later"). `kitaita_eval_demo.py` validates the metric CODE three ways:
(1) synthetic predicted-vs-gold pairs constructed to hit each of the
4 labels, confirming the classifier itself is correct, not just
lucky on real data; (2) the real pipeline + real `Decomposition.
slots` ledger run against 6 hand-annotated sentences already native-
speaker-reviewed via this project's own regression battery (KNOWN_
GOOD + 3 clean "novel free-text" ones) -- 11/11 slots scored
"correct", confirming the ledger integrates correctly with real
pipeline output, not just the metric math in isolation; (3)
vocabulary-choice and stability math on synthetic native-choice data
(no real multi-speaker word-choice data exists yet either). All
three parts pass; full regression battery and the 71-sentence
corpus battery both stayed clean after the instrumentation changes.

Files: `kitaita_e2e_pipeline.py` (`SlotRecord`/`record_slot`/
`Decomposition.slots`; instrumentation calls in `apply_ote_concord`,
`apply_associative_concord`, `apply_demonstrative_concord`, both
adjective/possessive sweeps in the "if not noun_hits:"/"elif not
verb_hits:" branches, the main probe-based sweep, and the post-
`translate()` subject-marker/adjective derivation), `kitaita_eval_
metrics.py` (new), `kitaita_eval_demo.py` (new), `kitaita_eval_demo_
report.json` (new, validation output).

## 2026-10-26 cont. 3: live "📊 Progress" dashboard on the HF Space -- auto-updating charts for all 3 evaluation metrics, fed by the existing feedback form

Direct user request: "I want to be able to view the progress. Could
you add summary charts for all three tests that automatically update
as people continue to test?"

**Real constraint, not discovered later**: the feedback form
(2026-10-20) only ever captured a holistic rating + an OPTIONAL full-
sentence correction -- not per-slot gold annotations, which `kitaita_
eval_metrics.py` (cont. 4) needs for metrics 1/2. Rather than redesign
the submission UI (a much bigger ask, not requested), `submit_
feedback()` now ALSO re-runs translation on the same (swahili, mode)
already submitted (cheap -- feedback submission is rare, not per-
keystroke) and logs the resulting `Decomposition.slots` ledger +
`secondary_nouns`-derived vocabulary choices alongside the existing
rating/correction, with zero change to the form the user fills in.

**The one real approximation this requires, stated plainly**: turning
a holistic corrected SENTENCE into slot-level gold needs a position-
by-position alignment between the pipeline's output and the
correction. This is reasonable here specifically because `assemble_
in_order`/`assemble_multi_clause` are POSITION-PRESERVING by design
(confirmed, not assumed) -- word i of the output and word i of a
same-length correction really do correspond to the same original
slot. When lengths differ (a real insertion/deletion/reorder in the
correction), that entry is EXCLUDED from the agreement/vocabulary
charts entirely, not guessed -- it still counts toward the plain
rating count/mean, which needs no alignment. `subject_sm` slots store
a bare SM PREFIX (e.g. "u"), not a whole word, so its match check is
`corrected_word.startswith(prefix)`; every other slot type is a whole
standalone word, exact match.

Found and fixed one real bug while testing this with constructed
examples (not caught by the empty-data case): a vocabulary-choice
word landing at the sentence-final position compared a punctuation-
free predicted word (`d.secondary_nouns`'s own stored value) against
a correction token still carrying its trailing period -- read as a
mismatch on an otherwise-exact match. Fixed by stripping trailing
sentence punctuation from both sides before comparing.

**Dashboard**: new "📊 Progress" tab (`gr.Tabs`, alongside the existing
Translator tab) with a summary line (submission/rating counts, mean
rating, how many were alignable) + 3 `gr.BarPlot` charts -- agreement
accuracy (correct/wrong_rewrite/missed_slot/spurious_rewrite counts,
pooled via `aggregate_agreement_accuracy`), vocabulary choice (mean
native-speaker support, `aggregate_vocabulary_choice`), stability
(mean accuracy per agreement-slot-count bucket, `compute_stability`)
-- reusing `kitaita_eval_metrics.py` directly, no parallel metric
logic. "Automatically update": a `gr.Timer(60)` ticks the same
refresh function every 60s (Gradio 6's actual mechanism -- the
`every=` kwarg on `.load()`/`.click()` from older Gradio versions is
gone, confirmed directly by a `TypeError` on first import, not
assumed from memory), plus a manual "Refresh now" button and a
`demo.load()` call so the charts are populated immediately on page
open rather than showing stale/empty state for the first 60s.

Verified before pushing: `app.py` imports and builds the full
`gr.Blocks` graph cleanly; `compute_dashboard_data()`/`refresh_
dashboard()` handle the REAL current state (feedback dataset has zero
submissions so far -- checked directly) by showing an explicit
"(no data yet)" placeholder rather than crashing or showing a
misleading empty chart; hand-built synthetic feedback records
(monkey-patching `_load_all_feedback` for the test only) exercise
BOTH the subject_sm-prefix and whole-word match paths and produce
exactly the expected counts (3 correct, 1 wrong_rewrite, mean vocab
support 1.0, stability n_slots=2/accuracy=0.75) before being trusted.
Added `pandas` to `requirements.txt` as an explicit direct dependency

regression battery unaffected (no pipeline files touched) and

## 2026-10-26 cont. 7: multiplayer word race for native speakers (Space side; no pipeline changes)

User request: a free, skribbl.io-style way for native speakers to play, where
players can vote to accept a word the oracle rejects and the oracle then learns
it. User decisions: rooms on this Space; round-based word race (not a full
board); "majority accepts, logged unverified".

**Built** (`hf_space/api/game.py`, wired in `api/server.py`): `POST /api/game/rooms`,
`GET /api/game/rooms/{code}`, WebSocket `/ws/game/{code}`, `GET /api/player_words`,
`POST /api/player_words/review` (X-Reviewer-Key). Rooms are in memory; votes go
to the `word_votes` table (word, random room id, yes/no, accepted — no nicknames).
A voted word is `player_accepted` (unverified); `verified` after acceptance in 2
different rooms or by a trusted reviewer. Words are checked server-side by the
app repo's oracle (`kitaita-oracle`, pinned in `hf_space/requirements.txt`), so
phones need no Pyodide for the game.

**Checks:** `pytest hf_space/tests` 58 passed (8 new game tests: rack logic,
real WebSocket rounds with two players, word scoring, vote accept/tie/silence,
two-room promotion, reviewer rejection, foreign-origin rejection, 503 when the
oracle is missing). Also ran a real uvicorn server locally: join → lobby →
round with a 10-tile rack; a foreign Origin is refused.

**Not done / caveats:** not deployed (the Space must be updated with the new
`hf_space/` files and requirements); one CPU shared with the translator (fine
for a few rooms, not load-tested); the room code is the only access control
(anyone with the link can join); "distinct rooms" for promotion can be gamed by
one person opening two rooms.

## 2026-10-26 cont. 8: the Space was still running old code — added automatic Space sync

The deployed game page reached `mpily-bantugrammar.hf.space`, but the user
confirmed `/api/health` there shows the Gradio page: the Space never received
the new `hf_space/` files (a Space is its own git repo; merging on GitHub does
not update it). Added `.github/workflows/sync_space.yml`: on every merge to
`main` that touches `hf_space/` (or when run by hand) it runs the API tests
without torch, then uploads `hf_space/` to the Space with `upload_folder`
(tests, caches, local data and the Dockerfile excluded; files already on the
Space but not in `hf_space/` are left alone). Needs the GitHub secret `HF_TOKEN`
with write access to the Space. Not run yet; it can't be tested from this
sandbox (Hugging Face is not reachable from here).

## 2026-10-26 cont. 9: Space still served Gradio only — cause found, switched to a Docker Space

The sync workflow's new report step (run on GitHub, which can reach Hugging
Face) printed the Space run log: the new code was deployed and NLLB loaded
("Ready."), but `uvicorn` then failed with `[Errno 98] ... ('0.0.0.0', 7860):
address already in use` — under the Gradio SDK, Hugging Face's own launcher
already serves the Gradio UI on 7860, so the FastAPI app (and every `/api/*`
and `/ws/*` route) never came up; `/api/health` returned the Gradio HTML with
status 200. Fix: `sdk: docker` + `app_port: 7860` in `hf_space/README.md`,
`hf_space/Dockerfile` (git for the word-checker install, CPU-only torch, gradio
pinned to 6.30.0, `python app.py`), and the sync no longer skips the Dockerfile.
Not yet verified on the Space: the next sync run's report shows the Docker build
log and `/api/health`.

## 2026-10-28: reviewing player-accepted words (translation, word type, noun class)

User report: words were accepted in games but there was no way to approve or
decline them (only the raw `POST /api/player_words/review` endpoint existed, and
`TRUSTED_REVIEWER_KEYS` was unset; the user has now set it). Added:
`GET /api/player_words/review_queue` (reviewer key; every voted word including
words rooms voted down, with vote totals and the latest review) and, on
`POST /api/player_words/review`, optional `translation`, `word_type`
(noun/verb/adjective/other) and `noun_class` (nouns only, checked against the
word checker's class list). The public feed carries the reviewer's translation,
type and class once approved. Review page is in the app repo (`review.html`).
Checks: `pytest hf_space/tests` 59 passed (new: queue auth and contents,
approve with translation+class, rescuing a voted-down word, decline removes the
word from the feed and the game checker, validation of type/class).
